name: ApeCoin
description: ApeCoin airdrop lacked snapshot protection against flash loans. An attacker flash-loaned BAYC NFTs from NFTX, claimed the airdrop allocation for those NFTs (60,564 APE tokens), and sold them for ~$820K profit in ETH.

name: DefiChain
description: DeFiChain’s atomic swap implementation contained a fee-denomination vulnerability that allowed attackers to substitute BTC for DFI while preserving the numerical fee amount. This caused the protocol to pay disproportionately large fees in BTC-denominated assets, introducing unbacked dBTC into circulation. The vulnerability existed from approximately June 2021 and was discovered on January 2, 2022.

name: Coinrail
description: On June 10, 2018, South Korean exchange Coinrail suffered an intrusion that resulted in the theft of over $40M in altcoins. The attack compromised approximately 30% of assets held on the platform, including ~$20M in NPXS tokens, $14M in Aston X, and $6M in other tokens. Two-thirds of stolen assets were recovered through partner exchanges.

name: GMX V1 EVM
description: GMX V1's AVAX/USD perpetuals were drained via wash trades on CEXs that manipulated oracle-reported prices, allowing arbitrage at zero slippage.

name: Grizzifi
description: On August 13, 2025, Grizzifi, a BSC-based staking protocol, was exploited via a flaw in its reward mechanism. The attacker created multiple controlled wallets to amplify the milestoneReward through the harvestHoney function, then collected additional rewards via collectRefBonus. The root cause was that milestone calculations were based on total cumulative investments rather than active investments.

name: TronBank
description: A backdoor was injected into TronBank's compiled bytecode during deployment via TronSmartContract.space. The hacker exploited the backdoor in the withdraw() function to extract 26.73M TRX from the contract.

name: Bad Guys by RPF
description: The Bad Guys NFT WhiteListMint function failed to properly check the number of NFTs minted per wallet. Users could pass arbitrary amounts and bypass the one-per-wallet limit, allowing two accounts to mint approximately 450 of the 1,221 free NFTs.

name: PlayDapp
description: The PlayDapp deployer key was compromised via spear-phishing attack. The attacker added themselves as a minter for the PLA token contract and minted 1.79 billion tokens across two transactions (Feb 9 and Feb 12), valued at $290M.

name: Stepp2p
description: On July 20, 2025, Stepp2p on Binance Smart Chain suffered a smart contract exploit resulting in approximately $43,000 in losses. The attack exploited a logic vulnerability in the protocol's core functions.

name: Nirvana V1
description: Nirvana V1 lost $3.5M on July 28, 2022 to a flashloan attack via Solend. Attacker borrowed 10M USDC, minted 10M+ ANA at artificially low prices by manipulating the oracle, swapped for USDT, and repaid the flashloan. ANA crashed 85% from $8.97 to $0.81.

name: DFX V2
description: On November 10, 2022, DFX Finance V2 was exploited for $4.3 million (plus $3.2M via MEV) through a reentrancy vulnerability in the flash function introduced in V2. The contract failed to prevent reentrant deposits, allowing attacker to repay flashloans while recording deposits as debt.

name: Typus Perp
description: On October 15, 2025, Typus Finance's custom price oracle was exploited via missing assertion logic and improper access control. The attacker called update_v2 to arbitrarily set token pair prices to extreme values and drained $3.44M in SUI, USDC, xBTC, and suiETH.

name: AIRWA
description: AIRWA token exploited on Binance Smart Chain through improper access control vulnerability. Lack of proper permission checks allowed unauthorized fund extraction from the protocol.

name: Skyward Finance
description: Skyward Finance was exploited on November 2, 2022 when missing input validation in treasury redemption logic allowed attacker to redeem 1.08M $NEAR (~$3M) in a single transaction. Attacker purchased SKYWARD on Ref.finance and redeemed at unfavorable rates.

name: Gamma
description: Gamma Strategies (formerly Visor) was exploited for at least $4.5M via infinite mint vulnerability. Attacker minted unlimited tokens and converted to other assets; token migration announced two days later.

name: CometDEX
description: CometDEX’s Soroban AMM allowed same-asset swaps such as USDC→USDC. When token_in and token_out were identical, the contract loaded two independent copies of the same reserve record, added the input amount to one copy and subtracted the output from the other, then wrote both back to the same map key. The second write overwrote the first, causing the pool’s recorded reserve to fall below its actual token balance. The attacker then deposited against the understated reserve, received excess LP shares, and redeemed those shares for real pool assets. The cycle was repeated 36 times using flash liquidity. Blend contracts themselves were not exploited, but Blend Backstop depositors were exposed because the backstop held BLND/USDC Comet LP shares

name: US Permissionless Dollar
description: In December 2025, USPD stablecoin protocol was exploited through its smart contract deployment process. Attacker used Multicall3 to claim admin role before the official deployment script, then deployed a malicious proxy that forwarded to the audited code while using event manipulation and storage slot spoofing. After months, attacker minted 98M USPD and drained ~$1M in stETH.

name: FTX
description: In October 2022, an attacker exploited FTX's withdrawal fee sponsorship mechanism by submitting 500,000 gas unit withdrawal requests—far exceeding normal 21,000 gas transfers. FTX subsidized the excess fees, unknowingly covering costs for smart contract calls that minted XEN tokens on the attacker's behalf.

name: Fake GIWA Bridge
description: Scammers deployed a counterfeit OP Stack-style network impersonating GIWA, including an RPC endpoint, Ethereum bridge and batch-posting infrastructure. The fake network reported GIWA’s expected mainnet Chain ID 9134, causing DYORSWAP and users to mistake it for the legitimate GIWA mainnet. Users voluntarily deposited ETH into the fraudulent bridge. After accumulating deposits, the scammers drained 766.25 ETH to an attacker-controlled address. GIWA’s actual mainnet had not launched, and neither GIWA nor DYORSWAP’s smart contracts were exploited

name: MintRisesPrices
description: MintRisesPrices on BNB Chain suffered a reentrancy attack where the attacker repeatedly entered and exited mint and burn functions in a single transaction, manipulating pricing mechanisms to drain approximately $59K from the protocol.

name: Terraport
description: Terraport, a Terra Classic DeFi platform, was drained of liquidity barely 10 days after launch through an access control vulnerability. An attacker with excessive permissions manipulated the DND token price and systematically drained liquidity pools.

name: Taiko Bridge
description: On June 21, 2026, an SGX signing key leaked on GitHub allowed an attacker to forge invalid proofs and drain approximately $1.7M from Taiko's ERC20 Vault on Ethereum.

name: UtopiaSphere
description: On July 21, 2024, UtopiaSphere (UPS) token on BSC was exploited for approximately $521,000 through a flashloan-based price manipulation attack. The attacker exploited the swapBurn() mechanism by flash-loaning 89.672M USDT and 6.424M USDT in vUSDC to manipulate UPS token prices and drain the PancakeSwap pair.

name: KaoyaSwap
description: KaoyaSwap's swap function had faulty logic allowing attackers to manipulate token calculations. Using a flashloan, an attacker exploited the vulnerability to extract value from the protocol's swap mechanism.

name: Solrise Finance
description: On July 26, 2024, the Casper blockchain was exploited via a privilege escalation vulnerability that allowed contract installers to bypass access rights checks on urefs. Attackers gained unauthorized access to 13 accounts and transferred approximately $6.7M in tokens before validators halted consensus to prevent further exploitation.

name: Ooki
description: Attackers exploited bZx price oracle on February 14-15, 2020, taking flash loans and spreading funds across exchanges to manipulate wrapped bitcoin prices, profiting $350K. Oracle lacked sufficient price source diversity.

name: FixedFloat
description: On February 16-18, 2024, FixedFloat (non-KYC exchange) was compromised and ~$26.1M in Bitcoin and Ether were stolen: 409.304 BTC and 1,728.48 ETH. Private keys controlling hot wallets on both networks were compromised. Initially suspected as insider attack or rug pull, the team claimed external attackers exploited infrastructure vulnerabilities. Ethereum funds moved through eXch exchange; Bitcoin funds dispersed across addresses.

name: Tapioca DAO
description: Tapioca DAO co-founder was compromised on October 18, 2024 via social engineering and malware download. Attacker gained control of TAP vesting contracts and drained stablecoin pools for $4.4M in USDC and ETH.

name: Celer cBridge
description: The cBridge DNS was hijacked, redirecting users to malicious smart contracts. Users who approved transactions on the fake site had their approved token amounts drained.

name: Altsbit
description: The Italian exchange Altsbit suffered a hot wallet breach on February 5, 2020, losing cryptocurrency including Bitcoin, Ether, Pirate Chain (ARRR), VerusCoin (VRSC), and Komodo (KMD). The attackers accessed hot wallets holding 'almost all funds', forcing the platform to suspend operations and eventually cease operations in May 2020. LulzSec claimed responsibility on Twitter.

name: Roe Finance
description: On January 11, 2023, Roe Finance was exploited for $80K via a flashloan-enabled Uniswap V2 oracle price manipulation attack. The attacker borrowed massive amounts of UNI-v2 tokens to create pool imbalance and manipulated the oracle price, then swapped at the false rate without Roe Finance validating freshness.

name: Fence Finance
description: An attacker exploited a tranche vault associated with Fence Finance and Valinor Digital by using a flash loan to obtain an inflated allocation of vault shares. The attacker subsequently redeemed those shares to withdraw approximately $1.01 million in USDC from the vault

name: SushiSwap
description: Attacker exploited SushiMaker's fee-conversion mechanism by creating a fake DIGG/WETH trading pair with minimal liquidity. By routing 0.05% of DIGG/WBTC swap fees through this illiquid pool, the attacker caused massive slippage and captured 81 ETH in outsized fees that should have gone to xSUSHI stakers.

name: Harvest Keeper
description: Harvest Keeper, marketed as an AI-based DeFi platform, executed a coordinated rug pull barely one month after launch. The team drained the contract through a privileged getAmount function and conducted ice phishing attacks to steal additional user funds.

name: Polymarket
description: Polymarket's internal operations wallet was drained on May 22, 2026 of ~$700K in POL tokens. An attacker obtained a 6-year-old private key and withdrew funds in 5,000 POL batches, but Polymarket confirmed user funds were unaffected.

name: X2Y2
description: Attackers created fake X2Y2 URLs via Google Ads with display URLs matching the legitimate site, tricking users into connecting wallets to phishing contracts. ~100 ETH (~$200K) was stolen from victims across multiple phishing sites.

name: UdonFi Lending
description: Udon Finance’s lending pool was exploited through a vulnerability in its withdrawal function that allowed an attacker to extract funds without proper authorization. The team confirmed that the stolen assets remained on Chromia and offered the attacker a 10% bounty in exchange for returning the remaining 90%. The precise technical mechanism and total loss were not disclosed

name: JayPegs Automart
description: JayPegs Automart DONA auction ($3.1M) on SushiSwap MISO exploited when contractor injected malicious code into the frontend deployment, redirecting proceeds to their wallet. Funds were fully recovered after identification and legal threats.

name: Atomic Green
description: On August 8, 2026, Atomic Green on Arbitrum was exploited via a signature replay vulnerability, resulting in a loss of approximately $29,984. Flagged by SlowMist with the exploiter address and transaction identified on-chain.

name: MOBOX
description: MOBOX borrow function exploited by cyclically borrowing and redeeming funds while incrementally increasing loan amounts. Referral rewards were transferred back to the contract to inflate the next borrow, netting ~$750K USDT.

name: Coinbene
description: Coinbene hot wallet was compromised and all ERC-20 tokens were drained to unknown addresses. The exchange downplayed the incident as routine 'maintenance' while customer assets were transferred out.

name: dYdX V3
description: On July 23, 2024, the dYdX domain (dydx.exchange) was compromised when attackers changed DNS nameservers via a compromised Squarespace account. Two users lost approximately $31,000 when redirected to a malicious contract attempting to steal their tokens. The site was restored within three hours and the domain was transferred to Cloudflare.

name: BUBAI
description: On October 29, 2024, BUBAI token on Ethereum executed a rug pull by removing liquidity, resulting in approximately $131K in losses for users.

name: TermFinance Vaults
description: An attacker acquired majority voting power in the thinly held governance tokens controlling Term Vaults and used that voting power to pass malicious governance proposals. The proposals gave the attacker control over the affected vaults, enabling the underlying assets to be withdrawn. The attack therefore did not require stealing an administrative key or bypassing an authorization check—the attacker obtained the required authority through the governance mechanism itself. Recent reporting indicates the affected products were Term’s strategy vaults built on Yearn V3 infrastructure rather than Term Finance’s core fixed-rate repo lending architecture

name: Cryptobottle
description: Cryptobottle's swap contract was exploited by disabling balance checks after callback, allowing arbitrary swaps that manipulated NAS token price and drained $490K in USDT to the attacker's address.

name: CoinsPaid
description: Lazarus Group stole $37.3M from CoinsPaid via a 6-month social engineering campaign posing as recruiters. Attackers conducted fake job interviews and tricked an employee into installing JumpCloud Agent malware on their laptop, gaining access to operational systems and wallets.

name: Merlin
description: Merlin was exploited for $330K when an attacker deployed a fake Alpaca-BNB vault and sent 1000 BNB to trick the contract into inflating reward calculations.

name: Vowcurrency
description: On August 13, 2024, Vowcurrency Protocol on Ethereum was exploited for approximately $1.2M when the usdRateSetter address changed the VOW/vUSD exchange rate from 1 to 100 without atomic validation. In the 15-30 second window, a bot minted $2 billion in vUSD using exploited rates and swapped 26.1M VOW for 175.4778 ETH and 595,970 USDT.

name: Swaprum
description: Swaprum founders exploited a backdoor add() function in their smart contract to steal approximately $3 million in deposited liquidity pool tokens from users. The stolen funds were laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: StepHeroNFTs
description: The StepHeroNFTs claimReferral function was vulnerable to reentrancy, allowing an attacker to repeatedly trigger transfers before state updates. The attacker drained approximately 90K USD in a single transaction.

name: VRug
description: On November 7, 2024, VRug executed a rug pull by removing liquidity from its protocol, resulting in approximately $8.4K in losses for users.

name: BasketDAO
description: BasketDAO was exploited via a flaw in its smart contract that allowed arbitrary low-level external calls in the approval process. The vulnerability enabled attackers to drain approved funds from users, resulting in over $1.2M stolen. The protocol subsequently shut down and was acquired by PieDAO.

name: Nebula Revelation
description: Nebula Revelation's staking contract on Optimism was exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability. The attacker used a self-destructing contract to complete all malicious operations within a single transaction, enabling unauthorized token withdrawals totaling approximately $180,264.

name: FH Token
description: FHToken was exploited through faulty sell-handling logic in its token contract. Reporting on the incident identifies a flaw in _transfer involving the isSell path, which incorrectly altered token balances during sell transactions. The attacker repeatedly bought and sold FH to exploit this behavior and extract value from the FH/USDT PancakeSwap V2 pool

name: SmartCredit
description: On May 4, 2026, SmartCredit's Leveraged Lido staking module was exploited for 26.382 ETH (~$72K) via an undisclosed vulnerability. The team paused the feature and compensated users from the Loss Provision Fund; technical details were never published.

name: Akropolis
description: On November 12, 2020, Akropolis lost $2 million in DAI from its yCurve and sUSD pools. The attacker used a flash loan to exploit a bug in the SavingsModule smart contract where the deposit logic minted tokens twice, allowing withdrawal of double the intended amount.

name: Polter Finance
description: Polter Finance on Fantom exploited November 16, 2024 via flashloan oracle manipulation. Attacker borrowed ~1.4M BOO from SpookySwap, collapsing the pool and inflating BOO price. With 1 BOO valued at $1.37T by the oracle, attacker extracted massive loans.

name: Hector Network
description: Hector Network's compensation contract for token holders was exploited when a malicious account deposited only 0.0001 HEC and then transferred $2.7M worth of assets to itself. The vulnerable AddEligibleWallet function allowed the attacker to designate arbitrary addresses as eligible and drain the treasury via mintWithdraw and transferRedemption functions.

name: Grin
description: Unknown miner(s) acquired 57.4% of Grin's network hash power on November 7-8, enabling 51% attack capabilities. The attacker reorganized at least one forked block, likely through rented hashrate from cloud mining services during a price surge.

name: Papertrade
description: Papertrade, a perpetual trading protocol on HyperEVM, reportedly suffered an oracle manipulation attack shortly after launch. The attacker manipulated Hyperliquid’s ETH order-book midpoint through external trades while opening and closing highly leveraged synthetic positions on Papertrade. Because the protocol used the instantaneous BBO midpoint without TWAP, deviation limits, or independent price validation, manipulated prices were accepted for execution and PnL settlement, transferring approximately $1.28M from the Martingaler LP

name: Umbrella Network
description: Umbrella Network's Polar Stream staking contracts on Ethereum and BSC suffered an unchecked underflow in the withdrawal function. The attacker drained LP tokens and used them to withdraw liquidity from UMB-ETH Uniswap and UMB-BNB Pancakeswap pools.

name: Aperture LM
description: On January 25, 2026, Aperture Finance V3/V4 contracts across Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum were exploited for $3.67M via arbitrary external call vulnerability. Insufficient validation allowed attackers to abuse existing ERC-20 and ERC-721 approvals and drain assets without key compromise.

name: SKYDAO
description: SKYDAO’s taxed sell flow called its pool controller before the seller’s net tokens were credited to the PancakeSwap V2 pair. The controller sold the 35% tax, moved the gross sell amount from the pair to the dead address through controlburn(), and called pair.sync(), causing the pair to record an almost-zero SKYDAO reserve. When the original transfer subsequently credited the net SKYDAO to the pair without updating that recorded reserve, the attacker exploited the balance/reserve mismatch through pair.swap() to extract USDT liquidity

name: Layer2DAO
description: On October 23, 2022, a hacker gained access to Layer2DAO's multisig wallet on Optimism and drained 49,950,000 L2DAO tokens. Layer2DAO negotiated with the attacker and repurchased 31,239,677 tokens to stabilize the market. The token price dropped 36.48% following the incident.

name: Bankr
description: The Bankr AI wallet's X account was compromised on July 25, 2026. The attacker posted fake airdrop links while draining the project's wallet of approximately 1.5 billion BNKR tokens that lacked MFA protection.

name: TempleDAO
description: TempleDAO's staking contract lacked access control on the migrateStake function. An attacker exploited this vulnerability to withdraw 321,154 xLP tokens from the staking contract and swap them for 1,418,303 TEMPLE tokens and 1,262,438 FRAX tokens, totaling $2.3M.

name: Flurry Finance
description: Flurry Finance yield aggregator was exploited via manipulation of the rhoToken multiplier. An attacker switched an address from EOA to contract and artificially inflated rhoToken balance, then redeemed inflated shares to withdraw underlying stablecoins from the FinanceRabbit strategy vault.

name: Drips Network
description: On July 14, 2026, legacy DaiDripsHub on Ethereum was exploited for 24,883 DAI via unsafe unsigned-to-signed integer conversion that reversed transfer direction from deposit to withdrawal.

name: Balancer V2
description: Balancer V2's boosted pools suffered a $893k-$979k exploit on August 27, 2023 via rate manipulation in linear pools (ERC4626). The attacker manipulated token conversion rates to drain liquidity.

name: SuperRare
description: On July 28, 2025, SuperRare RareStakingV1 contract was exploited for ~$730K (11.9M RARE) via broken access control in updateMerkleRoot(). Attacker submitted malicious Merkle roots for fraudulent token claims; a frontrunner later hijacked the exploit.

name: Ankr
description: On December 2, 2022, a former Ankr employee exploited an access control flaw in the aBNBc staking token contract, minting 10 trillion tokens and converting ~$5M to USDC. Binance froze $3M; Ankr reimbursed affected users from company reserves.

name: AzukiDAO
description: On July 3-4, 2023, AzukiDAO's governance token claim contract was exploited via signature replay when the signatureClaimed mapping was never verified. The attacker replayed one valid signature across multiple transactions to steal approximately 1.79M BEAN tokens (~$68,000).

name: GPU.NET
description: Unverified incident claimed on Ethereum involving GPU.NET on 2026-06-03 (~$10,600); no news coverage, security report, or on-chain confirmation.

name: Weft V2
description: Weft V2 accepted HUG as collateral using a severely incorrect live oracle valuation. HUG traded around 0.000131 XRD, but Weft’s Default PriceFeed valued it at 1,330.41 XRD at the time of the borrow, roughly 10 million times its actual value. The attacker bought 539,703.17 HUG for 70.6 XRD and introduced it through the flash_remove_collateral / flash_add_collateral path, which remained enabled despite normal HUG collateral additions having been disabled. Weft valued the HUG at approximately 718M XRD and allowed the attacker to borrow 47.28M LSULP and 13.1005M XRD

name: Bloom Trading Bot
description: An attacker exploited a reported remote code execution vulnerability in a third-party software module used by Bloom’s trading infrastructure, enabling unauthorized transfers from user wallets. Approximately 9,408 SOL was drained from 48 wallets belonging to nine traders within 94 seconds. Bloom attributed the incident to the third-party module and denied that private keys were exposed, while Bitquery confirmed that the transactions were signed using the affected wallets’ keys

name: DoodiPals
description: The DoodiPals project on Solana suffered a private key security vulnerability. Hackers exploited the flaw to sell tokens from multiple wallets, converting them into approximately 917 SOL (valued at $171K). The team announced plans to relaunch after a security audit and committed to providing 1:1 compensation to holders prior to the attack.

name: Vara Bridge
description: An attacker reportedly exploited Vara Bridge's cross-chain proof verification process to submit fraudulent Merkle roots representing outbound messages from Vara. These roots allegedly enabled unauthorized messages to be processed on Ethereum, resulting in approximately $12,776 in losses

name: MainnetSettler
description: On November 20, 2024, the MainnetSettler contract was exploited through an approval vulnerability that allowed arbitrary calls. Users with Hold token approvals to MainnetSettler had their tokens drained when attackers executed transferFrom calls, resulting in approximately $66K in losses.

name: Pirate Chain
description: Pirate Chain suffered an exploit in the transparent supply-accounting layer introduced with its Ironwood upgrade. Two transaction-validation failures reportedly allowed an attacker to bypass issuance restrictions and exploit incorrect output-script interpretation, creating approximately 39.8 million unauthorized ARRR. The tokens were transferred into the Sapling shielded pool, obscuring subsequent transfers. The team initially proposed a blockchain rollback but later confirmed that it could not execute one unilaterally

name: Pawnfi
description: Pawnfi's ApeStaking contract allowed attackers to use the same NFT as collateral multiple times for borrowing APE tokens. The vulnerability stemmed from missing NFT transfer verification in the depositAndBorrowApeAndStake() function, enabling an attacker to borrow without securing proper collateral by leveraging an already-staked NFT.

name: Bent Finance
description: Bent Finance was exploited by rogue developer who inserted backdoor into contracts during period lacking multisig protection, extracting 513k cvxcrv LP tokens (~440 ETH/$1.75M).

name: FEG Token
description: FEG's swapToSwap() function lacked input validation on the 'path' parameter, allowing attackers via flashloan to gain unlimited allowance and drain contract assets. Multiple attacks on May 15-16 extracted ~$1.3M + $1.9M total across ETH and BSC networks.

name: Shido
description: On February 29, 2024, the Shido staking contract was compromised via a private key compromise. The attacker transferred ownership, upgraded the contract with a hidden withdrawToken() function, and drained 4.3 billion SHIDO tokens ($3.3M realized in ETH). Token price collapsed 94% within minutes.

name: CheckoutPool
description: Fun.xyz's legacy CheckoutPool contract on Polygon exposed a bridge() function without access control or recipient binding, allowing attackers to redirect execution into trusted settlement paths and drain funds to attacker-controlled accounts.

name: Enjin
description: Enjin’s legacy CryptoItems infrastructure was exploited through a storage-slot collision between a registered adapter and its Managed Delegate Proxy. Because adapter functions execute in the proxy’s storage context via DELEGATECALL, the attacker called the adapter’s public initialize(uint256), which wrote the attacker’s address into the proxy’s pendingManager storage slot. The attacker then called acceptManager(), gained managerial control, registered a malicious adapter, stole ENJ-backed assets from users, and liquidated them through melt().

name: Uranium Finance
description: Uranium Finance on BSC suffered a calculation error in its v2 pair swap function. The sanity check validation used an incorrect constant (1,000,000) that was 100x too large compared to actual balance adjustments (10,000), allowing attackers to send minimal value and extract maximum reserves through the swap function.

name: Axion
description: Insider(s) injected malicious code into Axion's OpenZeppelin dependencies prior to deployment, enabling unlimited token minting via the unstake function. Attacker minted 79 billion AXN and dumped on the market, causing 99% price collapse and netting 1,300 ETH (~$500K) despite passing audits from Hacken and Certik.

name: Midas Capital
description: On June 17, 2023, Midas Capital's HAY/BUSD pool on BSC was exploited for $340K-$600K via a rounding error in cToken redemption logic. The attacker crafted positions that rounded down to 1 wei, repeatedly exploited the error with minimal deposits and flash-loaned ANKR collateral to withdraw disproportionately large sums.

name: Seascape
description: An early investor's private key was compromised, allowing an attacker to transfer 18,750 CWS tokens from the investor's wallet. The tokens were immediately liquidated on-chain.

name: Balancer
description: Balancer pools holding deflationary tokens (like STA which burns 1% per transfer) were exploited. An attacker used a dYdX flashloan to repeatedly trade between STA and ETH, depleting STA to 1 wei while Balancer's balance tracking failed to account for the fee burns. They extracted ETH, WBTC, LINK and SNX from severely imbalanced pools.

name: Gym Network
description: GYM Network deployed a new contract function on June 6, 2022. On June 8, attacker exploited missing caller verification in depositFromOtherContract() to create deposit records without actually transferring tokens, inflating balance and draining approximately 2,475.91 WBNB (~$716K). Funds were laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: Pythia
description: On September 2, 2024, Pythia Finance's algorithmic stablecoin protocol was exploited for approximately $53,000 via a reentrancy vulnerability in the claim rewards function. The attacker repeatedly called the function without allowing reward balances to update between calls, extracting unauthorized rewards.

name: Lava
description: On March 28-29, 2024, Lava Lending on Arbitrum was exploited for $340K via calculation error in liquidation engine. Flashloan enabled improper collateral/debt evaluation; markets paused within 15 minutes of detection.

name: MonoX
description: On November 30, 2021 MonoX was hacked for $31.4 million across Ethereum and Polygon when an attacker exploited a swap function that allowed same-asset swaps, using rapid swaps to manipulate the __updateTokenInfo function and artificially inflate MONO token price through a feedback loop, draining $18.2M WETH and $10.5M MATIC.

name: Uwerx
description: Uwerx was exploited on August 2, 2023 for $327,000 (176 ETH). Attacker flash-loaned 20,000 ETH, swapped for WERX tokens, dumped them into Uniswap pool, then used the skim() function with a specific address. The 1% burn mechanism on transfers created a price imbalance the attacker arbitraged for profit.

name: Zunami Protocol
description: On August 13, 2023, Zunami Protocol lost $2.1M to a flash loan attack that manipulated pricing via donation. The attacker exploited a flawed calcTokenPrice function (total_holdings / token_supply) to inflate pool value, increasing their UZD balance 3.5x before withdrawing through Tornado Cash.

name: GeniusAI
description: Gnus.AI suffered a $1.27M exploit on May 5, 2024 when a Discord breach exposed the team's deployment wallet private key. The attacker minted 100M fake GNUS tokens on Fantom, bridged them to Ethereum, and sold them into Uniswap pools, crashing the price 95%.

name: Hundred Finance
description: On March 15-16, 2022, an attacker exploited a reentrancy vulnerability in Hundred Finance's callback handling to borrow $6 million across multiple markets. The attacker deposited ~$2M USDC collateral, then repeatedly borrowed against it via the onTokenTransfer() callback which triggered before debt was updated.

name: Stake.com
description: Stake.com's hot wallets were compromised on September 4, 2023, leading to $41.3M theft of USDT, ETH, and other assets across Ethereum, BSC, and Polygon.

name: Telcoin
description: Telcoin's Polygon wallet proxy contracts were uninitialized, allowing an attacker to initialize dormant wallets with malicious versions and drain user funds that had never executed transactions.

name: Tornado Cash
description: An attacker exploited Tornado Cash governance by proposing a malicious proposal that appeared identical to a previously approved one, gaining voter trust. The malicious code granted 1.2M governance votes to the attacker, exceeding legitimate votes and gaining full governance control. The attacker drained 483,000 TORN tokens ($2.17M) from governance vaults before later proposing its reversal.

name: ZoomerCoin
description: A flash loan attack on ZoomerCoin exploited constructed calldata parameters to call transferFrom, transferring tokens previously authorized to the project contract. Attackers then exchanged stolen tokens for ETH.

name: Wasabi Perps
description: On April 30, 2026, Wasabi Protocol's deployer EOA was compromised, which held the sole ADMIN_ROLE without timelock or multisig protections. The attacker executed unauthorized UUPS proxy upgrades on vaults and pools across Ethereum, Base, Berachain, and Blast, sweeping approximately $5.5M in collateral and pool balances.

name: EOS Lelego
description: EOS Lelego gambling DApp was exploited via a randomness vulnerability in November 2018. Attackers predicted the random number generation algorithm by using information from previous blockchain blocks. Lelego was one of eight EOS gambling platforms targeted in coordinated attacks using the same vector.

name: HOPE Lend
description: HopeLend was exploited via a precision loss vulnerability in hToken's share calculation during the _handleFlashLoanRepayment function. The attacker minted tiny PEPE shares, donated large volumes to distort the exchange rate, then borrowed ETH using rounding errors in the redeemUnderlying function.

name: Somesing
description: Somesing, a South Korean Web3 social music service, suffered a vulnerability attack that resulted in the theft of 730 million SSX tokens. Of these, 504 million were undistributed tokens and 226 million were foundation-held tokens. The foundation reported the incident to the National Police Agency Cyber Investigation Unit.

name: Sheep
description: On February 10, 2023, the SHEEP reflection token on BSC was exploited. The attacker repeatedly executed the burn function and synchronized the pair to manipulate the reflection mechanism, causing balances to drop due to improper rate calculations and extracting approximately $3K.

name: Origin Protocol
description: On 2020-11-17 at 00:47:19 UTC an attacker exploited a flash-loan-funded reentrancy in OUSD VaultCore's mint function to inflate totalSupply. The contract failed to validate the transferred-in asset and lacked reentrancy protection, allowing the attacker to redeem against the inflated supply and drain the vault.

name: LuBian
description: On December 28, 2020, LuBian Bitcoin mining pool (6% of network hashrate in 2020) was hacked. An attacker exploited weak key generation in LuBian's infrastructure to brute-force private keys and steal 127,426 BTC (~$3.5B).

name: Multichain
description: Multichain's token contracts for WETH, PERI, OMT, WBNB, MATIC, and AVAX lacked proper validation of ERC20 permit() function calls. An attacker exploited this vulnerability to steal tokens from users who had previously granted approvals. A white-hat responder later returned approximately $1M of the $3M total loss, retaining 62 ETH as a bounty.

name: Kannagi
description: Kannagi Finance, a yield aggregation protocol on zkSync Era, performed an exit scam on July 30, 2023, draining nearly all value from contracts (leaving $0.17 TVL). The launched contract code contained malicious functionality not present in the audited version. The team deleted all online presence.

name: Bitcoinica
description: Bitcoinica suffered its first major hack when attackers breached Linode web hosting and stole 43,000 BTC from the exchange. The compromise of the hosting provider gave attackers direct access to Bitcoinica's wallet infrastructure.

name: Bogged Finance
description: A flashloan attacker exploited a bug in Bogged's deflationary token _txBurn() method, which charged only 1% instead of the intended 5% fee per transfer. This allowed the attacker to manipulate self-transfers to inflate staking reward calculations and mint 15M BOG tokens. The token crashed 98% from $8.50 to $0.15.

name: DAO Maker Vesting
description: On September 4, 2021, DAO Maker's vesting contracts were exploited via an unauthenticated init() function allowing contract reset and ownership claim. The attacker used emergencyExit() to extract ~$4M from vesting contracts for DERC, CPD, CAPS, and SHO.

name: Tinyman
description: Tinyman's AMM pools were exploited via a vulnerability in the liquidity withdrawal mechanism. An attacker could receive the same token twice after a burn rather than two different tokens, extracting twice as much liquidity as authorized. The initial attack was imitated by others, with approximately $3M in losses and $2M in additional at-risk liquidity before the team urged removal from all pools.

name: Badger DAO
description: Sandwich attack exploiting SushiMaker's fee-conversion vulnerability in the DIGG/WBTC Sushiswap pool. When Sushiswap added DIGG/WBTC to Onsen but failed to set up a bridge in SushiMaker, the attacker routed protocol fees through an illiquid pool, capturing 81 ETH in excessive slippage fees intended for xSUSHI holders.

name: Yield Protocol
description: In April 2024, an attacker drained $181,000 from Yield Protocol on Arbitrum by exploiting a logic error in pool token accounting. Using flash-loaned assets, the attacker created a discrepancy between actual token balance and recorded total supply, then withdrew excess tokens.

name: Cryptovoxels
description: Cryptovoxels' Discord server was compromised via a vulnerable bot. An attacker posted a phishing link promising 0.01 ETH parcels, tricking users into connecting MetaMask wallets and approving malicious transactions that drained approved assets.

name: TokenHolder
description: TokenHolder suffered an insufficient access control vulnerability where unauthorized callers could invoke restricted functions. The attacker exploited missing permission checks in the contract to drain approximately $26K from the protocol.

name: Compounder Finance
description: Twenty-two days after launch, Compounder Finance's development team replaced audited strategy pools with malicious 'Evil Strategy' contracts, removing restrictions on the withdraw function and draining every asset pool. Despite advertising 24-hour timelocks, the team retained ability to swap strategy contracts as a premeditated exit.

name: GDAC
description: GDAC, a South Korean crypto exchange, was hacked on April 9, 2023 (detected at 07:00 KST), with $13.9M stolen. Attacker gained access to the hot wallet and transferred 61 BTC, 350.5 ETH, 10M WEMIX, and $220K USDT. Stolen ETH was laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: pandorachainDAO
description: On June 22, 2022, pandorachainDAO on BSC suffered a flash loan attack exploiting price oracle manipulation. The attacker leveraged flash loans to artificially manipulate asset prices and execute profitable transactions on the platform, extracting approximately $128,000 in value.

name: UNCX Network V2
description: An attacker exploited UNCX Vesting V2’s shared token accounting by creating vesting positions, releasing a large position, donating tokens into the pool, and cancelling a topped-up vest. This sequence allowed a small remaining vesting position to withdraw tokens belonging to other users. UNCX confirmed additional affected assets across four chains and introduced emergency fees and restrictions to contain the exploit

name: LNbits
description: On November 8, 2026, attackers exploited vulnerabilities in LNbits, an open-source Bitcoin Lightning wallet management platform, to create unauthorized accounts and withdraw funds from affected installations. One confirmed operator reported losing 2,285,545 satoshis, while the aggregate loss across other instances remained undisclosed. LNbits instructed operators to shut down their servers and subsequently released version 1.7.0 on November 10 to address the vulnerabilities. The project also advised operators to rotate wallet keys and funding-source credentials, with the exact attack mechanism pending a full technical report

name: PacaSwap DEX
description: An attacker exploited an arithmetic flaw in Tessellation’s metagraph fee-transaction accounting. A specially constructed batch of fee transactions caused an intermediate subtraction to underflow and wrap into a large positive balance, creating SWAP that was not backed by deposits. Because validation focused on the resulting batch state rather than validating each balance-changing operation individually, the final balances remained apparently valid and reconciled. The attacker created the unbacked SWAP in one snapshot and subsequently sold it into PacaSwap’s SWAP/DAG liquidity pool, extracting approximately 12.1M real DAG contributed by LPs. The flaw was specific to Tessellation’s metagraph fee-transaction path; Constellation’s Hypergraph and DAG supply were unaffected

name: TENDRIL
description: On November 5, 2026, an attacker exploited TENDRIL's token sell logic to drain approximately 550,000 USDT from its PancakeSwap V2 liquidity pool on BSC. Each sell triggered PoolControl.sellToken(), which called TENDRIL.controlburn() to burn tokens directly from the liquidity pair and synchronize its reserves before the seller's remaining tokens arrived. The attacker used flash-loan-funded transactions to exploit the resulting reserve imbalance and withdraw nearly all the pool's USDT liquidity. ExVul estimated the attacker's campaign profit at no more than 181,910 USDT after observed purchases and gas costs, excluding an unresolved LP-position basis

name: Vertcoin
description: Vertcoin suffered a 51% attack on December 10-12, 2018 when an attacker gained majority hashpower using the Nicehash rental service. The attacker executed 22 deep chain reorganizations, 15 of which included double-spend transactions with the largest reorg exceeding 300 blocks. Estimated losses exceeded $100,000.

name: MetaLabz
description: MetaLabz token locker contract had an unprotected emergencyWithdraw() function that bypassed NFT stake records and reward calculations. Users could deposit both NFTs and ERC20 tokens, then execute emergencyWithdraw to extract tokens without processing proper stake accounting.

name: Aurellion
description: Aurellion Labs on Arbitrum was drained of $456,442.53 USDC on May 12, 2026 after incomplete Diamond Proxy initialization left the SafeOwnable facet's _initialized slot at zero. The attacker called initialize() to seize ownership and inject a draining facet.

name: Zabu Finance
description: On September 12, 2021, Zabu Finance's ZABUFarm contract on Avalanche failed to account for deflationary token transfer fees. Attacker was credited with full input amount despite fees, draining liquidity.

name: Resupply
description: On June 25, 2025, Resupply's newly-deployed (2 hours old) crcrvUSD vault on Ethereum was exploited. Attacker performed ERC4626 donation attack, minting 1 wei shares against 2,000 crvUSD, then deposited 1 wei collateral to borrow entire $9.6M vault through exchange rate rounding.

name: M2 Exchange
description: On October 31, 2024, M2 Exchange's hot wallets were compromised via an access control vulnerability across multiple blockchains, draining 3.7M USDT, 97M SHIB, 1,378 ETH (~$13.7M total). The exchange detected and froze assets within 16 minutes, restoring customer funds from reserves.

name: Polymarket International
description: Attackers reportedly compromised a third-party website monitoring service used by Polymarket, allowing malicious JavaScript to execute on its international trading platform. The script hijacked authenticated trading sessions to sell prediction-market positions and transfer assets to attacker-controlled wallets. Polymarket temporarily suspended trading, removed the affected integration, and committed to reimbursing impacted users

name: Clipper
description: On December 1, 2024, Clipper DEX was exploited for ~$450K via single-asset withdrawal flaw on Optimism and Base. Attacker caused severe pool imbalances and withdrew more than deposited (Optimism: $318K to $23K, Base: $197K to $36K).

name: Solareum
description: On March 29, 2024 Solareum (Solana-based Telegram trading bot) suffered a major security breach when a North Korean developer hired by Solareum compromised users' private keys imported into the bot through insecure storage, likely via third-party service vulnerability. Over 6,045 SOL (valued at $1.4M) from approximately 300+ users were stolen.

name: Harmony Bridge
description: On August 11, 2026, the Harmony chain was affected by an infinite mint exploit, per a CertiK alert. The loss amount was not disclosed and no dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: Venus Core Pool
description: On March 15, 2026, an attacker drained $3.7M from Venus Protocol THE market on BSC by directly transferring THE tokens to inflate the exchange rate 3.81x, enabling massive borrowing. The attacker had spent 9 months accumulating 84% of the supply cap. The vulnerability was in getCashPrior() reading contract balance directly instead of tracking internal accounting.

name: BFB
description: BFB token's custom price-defense deflationary logic could be triggered by zero-value transferFrom calls without per-transaction limits. An attacker used flash loans to repeatedly invoke the burn function ~151 times in one transaction, destroying BFB reserves and draining WBNB from the PancakeSwap liquidity pool.

name: Zerion Wallet
description: Lazarus hackers used AI-assisted social engineering over weeks to compromise Zerion employee credentials on Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack, gaining access to internal hot wallet private keys and draining $100K. User funds remained unaffected.

name: Belt Finance
description: Belt Finance on BSC lost $6.3M on May 29, 2021 to a flash loan exploit. Attacker used flash loans to deposit into undersubscribed strategies and manipulate pool ratios, exploiting faulty vault-share valuation that assumed strategies remained balanced.

name: Pinecone Finance
description: On August 18-19, 2021, Pinecone Finance's staking pool was exploited when an attacker bypassed the frontend and directly invoked the smart contract to deposit more PCT tokens than their account balance. Due to failed balance verification, the attacker withdrew more tokens than deposited, extracting approximately $200K before the PCT token price collapsed 61%.

name: Fetch.ai
description: Fetch.ai’s TokenConversionManagerV3 conversionIn() relied on an ECDSA signature from a single authorizer as its principal authorization mechanism. After obtaining that authorizer’s private key, the attacker signed a fresh conversion message for an attacker-controlled recipient and called conversionIn(). Unlike conversionOut(), the function lacked the checkLimits(amount) restriction and did not independently require proof that corresponding assets had been burned or locked on the other side of the conversion. The valid signature was therefore sufficient to release the converter’s entire remaining FET inventory in one transaction

name: NoOnes
description: NoOnes' Solana cross-chain bridge was exploited via a vulnerability in the relay contract's message processing logic. The attacker crafted malicious bridge messages that bypassed validation, tricking the relayer into authorizing unauthorized withdrawals across multiple blockchains through hundreds of small transactions each under $7,000.

name: sDAO
description: sDAO token on BSC suffered a business logic flaw allowing attackers to manipulate protocol mechanics and extract funds.

name: Nemo Yield Trading
description: Nemo on Sui was drained of ~$2.59M when unaudited code left an internal flash-loan function publicly callable and a query function able to mutate state, enabling the attacker to drain the Market pool and bridge to Ethereum.

name: Cypher
description: Cypher Protocol, a Solana-based futures exchange, was exploited for ~$1.035M via flashloan-enabled price manipulation. The attacker artificially inflated token prices through flashloans and exploited the protocol's economic model through repeated buying and selling at manipulated prices.

name: Stake DAO Yield
description: Stake DAO suffered multiple 2026 exploits: March 12 Oracle Message Spoofing caused $176K loss; May 27 deployer key compromise enabled minting 5.4T vsdCRV on Arbitrum in 25 seconds via LayerZero v2 OFT bridge. Incomplete ownership handover since March 2024 left deployer EOA as owner.

name: ShapeShift
description: Between March-April 2016, ShapeShift suffered three separate thefts totaling ~$230K. An employee stole $130K in mid-March, then after dismissal sold security credentials to external hackers who stole an additional $100K (154 BTC, 5,800 ETH, 1,900 LTC). No customer funds were lost as ShapeShift used a non-custodial architecture.

name: TLN Protocol
description: TLN Protocol's lending market smart contract was exploited through an undisclosed vulnerability. The attacker drained approximately $280,000 in assets, which were subsequently laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: Super Sushi Samurai
description: On March 21-22, 2024, the Super Sushi Samurai gaming token on Blast was exploited via a double-token transfer vulnerability in the mint function, allowing an attacker to drain approximately 1,310 ETH (~$4.6-4.8M). The attacker claimed to be a whitehat rescuer and offered reimbursement minus a 5% bounty.

name: GateHub
description: GateHub wallets were compromised via API tokens authorized with valid credentials, allowing attackers to steal 23.2M XRP from approximately 100 user accounts. Of this, 13.1M XRP was laundered through exchanges before recovery efforts.

name: ThalaSwap
description: On November 15, 2024, an attacker exploited missing balance validation in Thala's v1 farming contracts to unstake $25.5M in LP tokens without owning them. Thala recovered $25M within 6 hours through white-hat negotiation.

name: Lodestar V0
description: On December 10, 2022 Lodestar Finance V0 on Arbitrum suffered a flashloan and oracle manipulation attack when an attacker manipulated the price of PlutusDAO's plvGLP token to 1.83 GLP per plvGLP, then used flashloans to borrow all available platform liquidity with the inflated collateral, resulting in $6.9M loss.

name: Saga
description: On January 21, 2026, attackers exploited an inherited vulnerability in SagaEVM's Ethermint EVM precompile to bypass IBC messaging validation and mint unbacked Saga Dollars, causing a $7M exploit and protocol pause.

name: Fractal Protocol
description: Fractal Protocol's USDF vault on Arbitrum was drained of 13,700 USDC.e via re-entrant flashloan attack. The attacker looped through Balancer V2 batchSwap callbacks to recursively call the vault's deposit and withdraw functions. The vault's tokenPrice accrued only once daily and its share arithmetic rounded favorably for the depositor, allowing each re-entrant round-trip to extract more than it put in.

name: Vesper Finance
description: Vesper Lend on Rari Fuse Pool #23 exploited when Uniswap v3 oracle returned infinite VUSD price due to missing bounds checking. Attacker claimed unlimited collateral and borrowed ~$3.37M in miscellaneous assets.

name: Impermax
description: On July 16, 2022, private keys to Impermax team wallets were stolen, allowing the attacker to drain approximately 9 million IMX tokens and most of the protocol-owned liquidity. The team responded by frontrunning the attacker's potential sell-off and executed a token swap recovery plan from IMX to IBEX.

name: Jaypeggers
description: On December 29, 2022, Jaypeggers (JAY token) on Ethereum was exploited through a reentrancy vulnerability. The buyJay function lacked proper validation and allowed the attacker to insert a malicious contract as an ERC-721 token. The attacker reentered through the sell function using a miscalculated price to profit approximately 15.32 ETH (~$18.5K).

name: Remilia
description: Remilia Collective's multisig was breached, likely via malware intercepting Bitwarden password manager credentials. Attackers stole ~490 ETH, USDC, and 130+ Milady NFTs, with floor-price valuation exceeding $6M.

name: Cryptsy
description: Cryptsy announced on July 29, 2014 that an attacker under the nickname Lucky7Coin had inserted Trojan code into the exchange's systems, stealing 13,000 BTC and 300,000 LTC. Though later evidence suggested CEO Paul Vernon may have conducted internal theft and misattributed it, the reported mechanism involved compromised private keys.

name: Secret Network
description: The Axelar-Secret Network ICS-20 bridge was exploited on June 10, 2026. An attacker created a custom IBC channel and forged deposit packets, minting $4.67M in unbacked tokens without validating the packet source channel.

name: Equalizer Exchange
description: On June 7, 2022, Equalizer's vault contracts across four chains were exploited via a flawed calculation in getRatioForOneEToken(). The attacker used flash loans to manipulate vault balances and withdraw more assets than entitled. All losses were covered by Equalizer, with no impact to users.

name: PHX
description: PHX token's transfer-fee logic burned tokens from the pair before crediting post-fee amounts, causing recorded reserves to desynchronize with actual balances. An attacker used a flash loan to fund the manipulation, exploiting the mismatch to drain WBNB from the liquidity pool.

name: Usual USD0
description: Usual USD0++ Investment vault lost $43K on May 27, 2025 via an arbitrage exploit. Attacker abused a capped unwrapping mechanism lacking proper validation while depositing into the fund; no user funds were affected.

name: Curve Finance MEV Bot
description: An MEV arbitrage bot on Ethereum was exploited when an attacker discovered a vulnerability allowing unauthorized calls to a function that traded wBTC for wETH. Using a flash loan to manipulate Curve pool prices, the attacker forced the bot to purchase wBTC at inflated prices.

name: MoonHacker
description: MoonHacker Vault on Optimism was exploited when an attacker took a flashloan of USDC from Aave, passed a malicious contract as the mToken parameter in the executeOperation function (which lacked validation), gained unauthorized approval to transfer vault USDC, and drained the vault.

name: Gamma
description: Visor Finance's staking contract was exploited via reentrancy in the delegateTransferERC20 interface. Attackers recursively called the withdrawal function before state updates were completed, stealing 8,812,958 VISR tokens (~$8.2M).

name: FlyCow
description: FlyCow's FCOW token burned its own LP pair balance mid-swap and synchronized reserves immediately after, allowing an attacker to manipulate the liquidity pool state and drain approximately $65.3K USDT through a subsequent swap.

name: Molt EVM
description: On March 7, 2026, Molt EVM on Base was exploited for ~$127K via missing access control on the setSpawnerToken() function. The attacker overwrote the authorized spawner with their own contract, then called the protected spawnTokens() function to mint 100 million mEVM tokens at zero cost and swapped them for WETH.

name: CoinsPaid
description: CoinsPaid, a crypto payment gateway, was exploited for the second time in six months. An attacker with compromised wallet access stole $7.5M in digital assets from ETH and BNB chains, including USDT, USDC, CPD, BNB, and BSC-USD. The attacker swapped stolen assets into ETH and distributed them across multiple EOAs and exchanges including WhiteBit, MEXC, and ChangeNow.

name: xWin Finance
description: A flashloan attacker exploited invalid slippage control logic in xWin's reward distribution system, which did not properly validate transaction slippage limits. The attacker obtained a flashloan of 76,000 BNB, manipulated the swap price, and extracted 303,998 XWIN tokens by exploiting the broken slippage validation in the _swapBNBToTokens function.

name: Llamascape
description: Staff member accounts on Llamascape's Discord were phished, allowing attackers to post a fake minting scam. Holders lost 30-40 ETH by interacting with the malicious contracts. The team committed to compensation and security improvements.

name: THORChain DEX
description: On June 29, 2021, THORChain was exploited via a same-symbol deposit flaw where ERC20 tokens with the 'ETH' symbol were incorrectly identified as genuine ETH, allowing attackers to exchange fake ETH for other tokens and steal approximately $350K. This was the first of three consecutive attacks on THORChain.

name: Yearn Ether
description: Yearn Finance yETH stableswap pool drained for $9M on deposit of 16 wei. Attacker minted 235 septillion yETH via accounting flaw caused by cached storage variables not resetting at zero liquidity, then swapped for legitimate derivatives.

name: Velar Perps
description: On February 19, 2026, Velar's PerpDEX on Mezo was exploited via predictable oracle price updates. Attacker manipulated BTC/MUSD perpetual pool by systematic trading patterns, flowing ~$72M volume and draining ~$401K through exploitable oracle timing.

name: DefiPlaza
description: DeFiPlaza V2 had a complex vulnerability allowing a carefully crafted transaction to drain all liquidity pool tokens. An MEV bot front-ran the attacker and captured ~$24K before being contacted by the team and returning the funds.

name: Dragoma
description: Dragoma move-to-earn game was a rug pull. The core team exploited admin privileges immediately after listing on MEXC, withdrawing funds and abandoning the project, crashing the token 99.8%.

name: Munchables
description: On March 26, 2024 Munchables (gaming NFT project on Blast layer-2) suffered a $62.5 million exploit by a rogue developer (pseudonym 'Werewolves0943') hired to write the smart contracts who deliberately built in vulnerabilities, using control of the upgradeable proxy to assign themselves 1 million ETH and drain the protocol.

name: Orange Finance
description: Orange Finance admin address was compromised on January 8, 2025, and used to upgrade contracts on Arbitrum and transfer $840K. Protocol had inadequate multisig implementation (effectively unisig); ~$731K remained.

name: Bitrue
description: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in Bitrue's withdrawal risk-control second-review process, bypassing security checks to drain 9.3M XRP and 2.5M ADA from the hot wallet.

name: Furucombo
description: Furucombo exploited February 27, 2021 for ~$14M via delegatecall hijack. Attacker deployed a fraudulent contract impersonating Aave v2 implementation. Furucombo failed to authenticate the target, allowing the attacker to drain pre-approved tokens (3,900+ stETH and USDC) from ~22 users.

name: ParaSpace Lending V1
description: On March 17, 2023 ParaSpace (NFT lending protocol on Ethereum) suffered a price manipulation exploit in the AutoCompoundApe contract allowing attackers to borrow assets with less NFT collateral than required. Security firm BlockSec intercepted the attack and recovered approximately 2,900 ETH ($5M) of BAYC NFTs before the full attack executed.

name: Zeed Finance
description: Zeed Finance experienced an arithmetic error in reward distribution calculation. The vulnerability allowed the attacker to manipulate calculations to extract approximately $1M.

name: 1inch Swap
description: On October 30, 2024, attackers phished a LottieFiles npm account and published malicious lottie-player versions that injected an Ace Drainer wallet-connect prompt into every downstream site, including the 1inch web dApp. The 1inch frontend lacked npm package pinning or integrity checks, leaving it vulnerable to upstream compromise. One user lost 10 wrapped BTC ($723K) from an Avalanche wallet; only the web frontend was affected.

name: Concentric
description: On January 22, 2024, Concentric Finance on Arbitrum suffered a $1.72 million exploit. Attackers used social engineering to compromise the deployer private key, then upgraded vault contracts, minted unauthorized LP tokens, and drained assets. Lacked multi-sig or time-lock protections.

name: MONA
description: On April 14, 2026, an attacker created 25 accounts to farm MONA using a flash loan and Venus USDT borrow, exploiting flawed accounting in the deferred burn mechanism to drain 60,950 USDT from the liquidity pair.

name: Cryptopia
description: Cryptopia's dormant XSN token wallet, under liquidators' control, was compromised during the exchange's liquidation proceedings. Hackers stole NZD 62,000 (~$45,000) worth of XSN tokens from a $1.96 million address that had been inactive since the exchange's initial hack in 2019.

name: APC
description: APC token on BSC was exploited through a combined flash loan and price manipulation attack. The attacker used a flash loan to artificially inflate the token price, enabling profitable swaps.

name: Moonwell Lending
description: The attacker manipulated the spot price of the relatively illiquid MAMO token, increasing the collateral value recognized by Moonwell. The attacker used the inflated MAMO collateral to borrow liquid assets including cbBTC, ETH/WETH, USDC, and wstETH, leaving the lending markets with undercollateralized positions

name: 3Commas
description: 3Commas' API database containing ~100K API keys was breached and publicly leaked on December 28, 2022. Attackers used the stolen keys to access connected exchange accounts and drain cryptocurrency by performing unauthorized trades across Binance, KuCoin, and other platforms.

name: Bacon Protocol
description: Bacon Protocol NFT mortgage lending platform was exploited via reentrancy in the lend() function. The contract used ERC777 without considering callback security, allowing an attacker to reenter lend() to obtain excessive lending credits and drain ~$1M.

name: Rhea Lend
description: On April 16, 2026, Rhea Lend on NEAR was exploited via chained swap path that defeated margin module's slippage protection. Attacker spent April 13-15 deploying fake token contracts and eight Ref Finance pools, then executed complex swap reusing intermediate assets to drain reserves. Oracle accepted attacker-created pool prices as legitimate.

name: COLDCARD
description: Starting 30 July 2026 attackers drained BTC in four waves from thousands of addresses whose seeds were generated on Coldcard hardware wallets running firmware 4.0.0+ (March 2021 onward), where a firmware bug bypassed the dedicated hardware RNG during key generation, cutting effective key strength to as little as 40 bits and allowing offline brute-forcing.

name: MOKE
description: MOKE token on BNB Chain suffered a $907K exploit in early August 2026 via suspected liquidity pool manipulation, detected by TenArmor. The exact attack vector remains unconfirmed.

name: Rho Markets
description: Rho Markets on Scroll lost $7.6M on July 19, 2024 when a private key compromise allowed attacker to transfer oracle contract ownership and manipulate price feeds, draining all USDT and USDC.

name: Poloniex
description: An attacker discovered a race condition in Poloniex's withdrawal processing logic. By submitting multiple concurrent withdrawal requests, the attacker could deplete accounts to negative balances before the system updated withdrawal state, extracting 97 BTC without having that balance.

name: Tectonic
description: On February 22, 2024 Tectonic (lending protocol on Cronos) lost $250,000 to a flashloan exploit targeting newly added market functionality that lacked protection against flashloan-based manipulation in the deposit logic.

name: DuelBits
description: On February 13, 2024, DuelBits lost $4.6M when private keys to its hot wallets on Ethereum and BNB Chain were compromised. The attacker stole USDT, APE, and SHIB tokens, converted them to ETH, and laundered the funds through Tornado Cash.

name: RISEx
description: On August 3, 2026, a misconfigured withdrawal permission in RISEx's RWA strategy, deployed July 13, allowed an unauthorized address to withdraw 673,011.56 USDC. RISEx patched the contract within minutes and compensated XLP depositors from monthly fees.

name: Aftermath Perps
description: Aftermath Finance's perpetual futures on Sui exploited for $1.14M via missing validation in fee accounting. Attackers set negative builder code fees to inflate synthetic collateral, enabling unauthorized vault withdrawals.

name: Coinsbuy
description: On August 9, 2026, Coinsbuy’s wallet infrastructure was exploited via improper access control, allowing an attacker to drain approximately $7.9M across Ethereum and Tron. Flagged by PeckShield; no dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: xToken
description: An attacker used an $81M flashloan from dYdX to manipulate SNX price downward, then exploited an access control vulnerability in xToken's callFunction to purchase SNX at artificially depressed prices, stealing $4.5M in value.

name: DEUS Finance
description: DEUS Finance lost $3M to a flash loan attack that manipulated the USDC/DEI oracle, triggering incorrect liquidations due to insufficient price checks.

name: KICKICO
description: KICKICO ICO platform was exploited on July 26, 2018 when attackers gained access to the private key managing the KICK token contract. The attacker destroyed KICK tokens at 40 addresses and recreated them at 40 attacker-controlled wallets, stealing over 70 million KICK tokens worth $7.7 million. KICKICO regained control by switching to a cold-storage key.

name: pump.fun
description: pump.fun exploited on May 16, 2024 when a former employee retained access to a service account after leaving. The attacker flash-loaned SOL, used it to complete bonding curves to 100%, then drained the released liquidity (~$1.9M-$2M or ~12,300 SOL) to repay the loans.

name: Unizen
description: On March 8, 2024, the Unizen DeFi aggregator on Ethereum was exploited for $2.1M (primarily USDT and DAI) via an external call vulnerability introduced in a contract upgrade. The CEO reimbursed affected users starting March 11.

name: ACryptoS
description: On November 8, 2026, attackers exploited a missing input validation check in ACryptoS's concentrated-liquidity vaults across Arbitrum, BSC, Polygon, Base, and Optimism, stealing approximately $665,429 from 77 vaults. The vulnerable depositMulti() function accepted an incomplete token-amount array, causing the vault to undervalue its existing assets and mint disproportionately large amounts of shares for minimal deposits

name: pNetwork
description: On September 19, 2021, pNetwork's cross-chain bridge was exploited when an attacker crafted fraudulent peg-out event logs. The Rust event-log processor failed to validate that requests originated from authorized pNetwork contracts, processing the fake withdrawal requests. The attacker stole 277 BTC (wrapped to BSC) worth approximately $13M.

name: Mintpal
description: Mintpal's exchange was compromised and attackers gained control of internal features that allowed them to withdraw 8 million VeriCoin (30% of circulating supply at the time). VeriCoin developers executed a soft fork to roll back the blockchain, returning the stolen tokens to the exchange.

name: Tsuru
description: Tsuru on Base suffered a smart contract vulnerability due to insufficient validation, resulting in losses of 137.78 ETH. The vulnerability allowed unauthorized fund extraction from the protocol.

name: SUNRAY·FINANCE
description: On October 30, 2024, SUNRAY FINANCE on Arbitrum was attacked when a private key was compromised, enabling malicious contract upgrade and 200 trillion SUN token mint. Attacker swapped ~$2.1M for USDC, collapsing SUN to zero.

name: Moby
description: In January 2025, Moby Trade on Arbitrum suffered a $2.5M hack when an attacker compromised a private key controlling the proxy upgrade mechanism. The attacker performed a malicious upgrade and called emergencyWithdrawERC20() to steal stablecoins and wrapped assets, but a whitehat recovered $1.5M.

name: Soda Protocol
description: Hackers exploited a variable naming error in the WETHCalculator.sol smart contract, where 'amount' was used instead of 'lockedAmount', allowing unauthorized drainage of over 400 ETH from the liquidity mining pool.

name: Rari Capital
description: On December 10, 2025, Rari Capital Fuse lending pools (dormant after prior $80M+ hacks) were exploited for $2M via unprotected proxy upgrade vulnerability. Attacker hijacked implementation contract to gain admin privileges and enable uncollateralized borrowing.

name: KITE Foundation
description: Sixteen wallets associated with KITE Foundation were drained simultaneously in a coordinated private-key compromise. The transfers were ordinary ERC-20 transfer() calls authorized by the affected wallets rather than an exploit of the KITE token contract. KITE Foundation subsequently paused Ethereum KITE transfers and cross-chain bridges, then deployed a replacement ERC-20 and migrated legitimate balances 1:1 from a pre-incident snapshot while excluding attacker-controlled addresses

name: Proxy_b7e1
description: On November 24, 2024, a proxy-based contract on BNB Chain was exploited via a logic flaw, resulting in approximately $8.5K in losses. The vulnerability was in the contract's logic implementation.

name: FFGame
description: FFGame gambling DApp suffered exploitation via mirrored-randomness vulnerability in November 2018. Attackers predicted the random outcome by leveraging information from earlier blockchain blocks. The attack was part of a coordinated assault on eight EOS gambling platforms using randomness prediction vectors.

name: MEV-Boost Relay
description: A malicious Ethereum validator exploited a flaw in the mev-boost-relay implementation by crafting an invalid block header with zero parent and state roots, bypassing validation and gaining visibility of block contents. The attacker front-ran and replaced MEV bot transactions to drain approximately $20M over 24 transactions.

name: Ooki
description: On November 5, 2021 an unknown hacker sent a phishing email containing a Word document with embedded malware to a bZx protocol developer. The developer executed the malware, allowing the attacker to exfiltrate the private key used to drain $55 million across Polygon and BSC networks.

name: DKP
description: DKP token on BSC was exploited through flash loan price manipulation. The attacker leveraged the oracle's reliance on USDT-DKP pair ratios to manipulate token pricing, swapping small amounts to trigger massive price shifts and profiting from the arbitrage.

name: Cover Protocol
description: Cover Protocol's Blacksmith contract was exploited on December 28-29, 2020, due to incorrect memory/storage reference in reward calculation logic, allowing unbounded minting of approximately 40 quintillion COVER tokens. Funds were returned by a white hat hacker.

name: ChainSwap Bridge
description: On July 11, 2021, ChainSwap bridge was exploited when attackers identified a logical flaw in the cross-chain quota code. The vulnerability allowed invalid, non-whitelisted addresses to bypass authorization and increase the on-chain bridge quota. Attackers minted new tokens for multiple protocols and stole approximately $4.4 million across Ethereum and BSC, affecting Wilder World, Antimatter, Optionroom, and others.

name: Curve DEX
description: On August 9, 2022, Curve Finance's DNS provider (iwantmyname) was hijacked, redirecting users to a malicious frontend that injected token approval transactions. Curve's smart contracts remained secure; the team quickly identified and reverted the issue.

name: Levyathan
description: Levyathan developers stored private keys with minting capability on GitHub. The attacker used these to pass a timelock transaction on July 28 and execute an ownership transfer on July 30, minting 100 quintillion LEV tokens. The weak timelock controls lacked multisig authorization.

name: QuantMaster
description: QuantMaster smart contract drain via malicious backdoor embedded by an insider developer. The backdoor allowed the attacker to extract funds through a deliberately compromised contract.

name: HermesVault
description: On May 19, 2026, HermesVault, an Algorand privacy protocol, was exploited when an attacker bypassed ZK proof verification via a flaw in the withdrawal verification script's key reset defense logic, stealing 261,000 ALGO (~$29.5K).

name: Shibarium
description: On September 12, 2025 at 18:44 UTC, an attacker compromised 10 of Shibarium's 12 validator keys and used a 4.6M BONE flash loan delegated to Ryoshi Validator 1 to push past the two-thirds threshold, then co-signed a false L2 state and drained 17 tokens worth ~$4.1M from the canonical bridge. The dev team suspects key exposure from a developer machine or the server's KMS.

name: DeFiPie
description: On July 12-13, 2021, DeFiPie (now pieLABS) was exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability combined with an overborrowing flaw. The attacker created a malicious token contract with a modified transfer function and used reentrancy in the doTransferOut function to borrow more than their collateral, extracting approximately $125K in liquidity.

name: dForce Lending
description: An attacker exploited read-only reentrancy in dForce's Curve vault integration on Arbitrum and Optimism. During asset withdrawal, the attacker called back into the protocol to manipulate Curve's virtual price and liquidate wstETH/ETH positions.

name: Swapos V2
description: Swapos V2 was exploited through a broken k-value invariant in the swap pool, allowing attackers to drain approximately $468K from the protocol by manipulating the automated market maker's core pricing mechanism.

name: GoodDollar
description: GoodDollar's reserve contract contained a reentrancy vulnerability that allowed an attacker to repeatedly call withdraw functions before state updates completed. The Protocol Guardians paused contracts and applied a 100% transaction fee to hacker-held tokens to discourage transfers.

name: Pirate X
description: Pirate X gaming platform staking wallet was compromised. An attacker sold 9.6M PXP tokens from the protocol, profiting approximately 212 BNB. The team acknowledged bypassing security inspection before launching a vulnerable conversion feature.

name: SharedStake
description: An insider with access to a disclosed timelock vulnerability exploited it to bypass vesting contract protections and withdraw 500K SGT governance tokens. The vulnerability had been identified on April 26 and shared with the team, but the insider used this knowledge to drain locked tokens four times on June 19-23.

name: Allbridge Core
description: On July 20, 2026, Allbridge Core on Solana was drained of $1.65M. An attacker used a 1.12M USDC flashloan through Kamino to swap USDC/USDT and distort the pool ratio, then withdrew liquidity at the inflated rate.

name: Rocket Perp
description: An attacker exploited a dormant perpetual market on Rocket by placing artificially inflated orders and trading between accounts under their control. The trades generated artificial profits in one account while bankrupting a disposable counterparty. The profitable account withdrew approximately $287,666 through Rocket’s Bridge, leaving a deficit to be socialized across platform users. Rocket subsequently confirmed the full return of the withdrawn funds

name: BitBay
description: BitBay’s vault contained a vulnerability in _withdraw() that transferred the contract’s entire token balance whenever liquidity == 0, without restricting withdrawals to the user’s proportional entitlement. The attacker triggered this condition through reposition() and subsequently redeemed one minimal share unit, receiving approximately 14,838.47 DAI belonging to the vault

name: Panther Protocol
description: On August 6, 2026, Panther Protocol on Base was exploited via a malicious governance proposal, resulting in a loss of approximately $7,578. No dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: Altilly
description: Attacker gained access to Altilly's hosting provider account via compromised API keys lacking 2FA. The attacker rebooted servers in rescue mode, created new system user accounts, deleted all backups across hosting and offsite services, and rendered encrypted wallets inaccessible. The exchange permanently shut down with no fund recovery.

name: DeezNutz 404
description: A calculation flaw in the DeezNutz 404 ERC-404 token contract enabled infinite minting through self-transfer exploits. Attackers minted unlimited tokens and sold them for ~$170K.

name: UwU Lend
description: On June 10, 2024, UwU Lend was exploited for approximately $19.3-20 million. Attacker used flashloans (~$3.8B) to manipulate CurveFinance pools, corrupting 5 of 11 USDe price sources. A second attack on the same protocol followed days later, extracting an additional $3.7 million.

name: Eleven Finance
description: On June 22, 2021, Eleven Finance's NRV vaults were drained for $4.5M via a logic flaw in emergencyBurn(). The attacker used flashloans to obtain assets, converted them to Nerve-bridged tokens, and deposited them into MasterMind. The function failed to burn shares, allowing repeated withdrawals from the same position.

name: GDS
description: On January 3, 2023, the GDS protocol on BSC was exploited using a flash loan attack. The attacker borrowed $2.38M USD via flash loan, manipulated the LP mining reward calculation by exploiting a flaw in the _lpRewardAmount calculation, and created multiple attack contracts to withdraw excessive rewards. The attacker profited approximately $187K before repaying the flash loan.

name: OKX DEX
description: OKX DEX's proxy admin private key was leaked on December 12-13, 2023. Attacker upgraded the proxy contract to a malicious implementation and stole ~$2.7M in ETH, USDT and USDC from wallets with standing approvals to the old contract.

name: Lykke
description: Lykke cryptocurrency exchange hot wallet was compromised by Lazarus Group, resulting in the theft of 158 BTC and 2,161 ETH (~CHF 22.8M / ~$22.4M). The stolen assets represented approximately one-third of Lykke's total holdings, leading to the exchange halting all trading and eventually declaring bankruptcy.

name: BTC.com
description: BTC.com's custodial systems were compromised on December 3, 2022, exposing private keys and enabling the theft of 32.5 BTC and 1964 ETH. Approximately $700K belonged to client assets while $2.3M was company-owned. Stolen funds were transferred to Tornado Cash and CEX exchanges.

name: Neutrl
description: On March 18, 2026, Neutrl DeFi protocol experienced DNS hijacking redirecting the official domain to a malicious interface. Users accessing the spoofed frontend were prompted to approve token transfers, but no funds were stolen as user assets remained in custodial wallets.

name: Lumi Finance
description: On July 13, 2026, Lumi Finance on Arbitrum lost ~$270K through Sodium smart account ERC-1271 validation flaws. The exploit required two bugs: (1) Sodium accepted attacker-controlled contracts as valid signers and session keys, and (2) validateUserOp granted unlimited ERC-20 allowances via attacker-controlled paymasterAndData. Attackers systematically stripped tokens from user accounts, leaving persistent allowances.

name: ValueDefi
description: ValueDefi custom-weighted pools drained on May 7, 2021. Uninitialized contracts lacked the 'initialized = true' flag, allowing attacker to re-initialize, set themselves as operator/owner, and drain vBWAP/BUSD LP tokens via governanceRecoverUnsupported().

name: LendHub
