description: LendHub on Huobi Eco Chain was exploited on January 12, 2023 for ~$6M. The deprecated token remained active and priced identically to its replacement, allowing the attacker to exploit accounting flaws in mint/redeem operations.

name: Curve LlamaLend
description: Attacker flash-loaned 10M USDC and 15,986 WETH from Morpho Blue to manipulate sDOLA vault exchange rate, triggering liquidations of 27 borrowers in sDOLA/crvUSD market for ~$240K profit. Oracle vulnerability: CryptoFromPoolVaultWAgg used sDOLA.convertToAssets() as spot price without atomic-manipulation protection.

name: 0vix
description: On April 28, 2023, 0VIX on Polygon was exploited for $2M via flashloan-enabled oracle manipulation. Attacker obtained $6.12M flashloan, manipulated vGSHT/Curve pricing to inflate collateral value, triggered liquidation cascade ($4.33M net loss), and bridged 1,069 ETH to Tornado Cash.

name: Tropykus RSK
description: On June 14, 2023, Tropykus RSK was exploited via a rounding error vulnerability in the redeem counter affecting interest rate calculations, resulting in $150,000 in losses.

name: Cellframe
description: Cellframe suffered a flash loan attack exploiting calculation errors during liquidity migration. The attacker took flash loans to manipulate LP pools by injecting and withdrawing liquidity strategically across different pools, converting the resulting tokens through a new CELL-BUSD pool to extract value.

name: Mango Markets V3
description: Attacker used $5M initial capital to take a MANGO-PERP position and pumped spot price via large purchases on another account, creating artificial collateral worth $423M to borrow $110-116M. Protocol relied on liquidity-sensitive price feeds vulnerable to large single-account manipulation.

name: Liquid Network
description: An actor exploited a software vulnerability in Elements, the software underlying Liquid, to create approximately 4,000 L-BTC without corresponding BTC backing. The unbacked L-BTC was transferred to SideSwap’s peg-out service, where it was indistinguishable from legitimately backed L-BTC. SideSwap processed a valid peg-out and burned the L-BTC, causing the Liquid Federation to release approximately 3,996 BTC from its Bitcoin reserves. Liquid and SideSwap state that SideSwap’s Peg-out Authorization Key and the federation’s other keys were not compromised

name: Blastoff
description: BlastOff yield vault exploited for approximately 150 ETH (~$600K). Protocol team closed the vulnerable pool after 6 hours and offered 20% bounty for recovery. Cause under investigation and protocol being reaudited.

name: GYM Network
description: GYM Network's _autoDeposit function had no transfer check, allowing users to call deposit() and create_deposit_record() without actually transferring tokens. An attacker repeatedly 'deposited' 8 million GYMNET tokens without sending any funds, then withdrew the fake deposit balance.

name: Vertcoin
description: Vertcoin suffered a second 51% attack on December 1, 2019, with 603 VTC blocks replaced by 553 attacker-controlled blocks in a deep blockchain reorganization. Five double-spent outputs worth approximately 125 VTC (~$29) were redirected to the attacker. Attacker rented hash power for 0.5-1 BTC despite the attack being financially unprofitable; Bittrex suspended withdrawals during the attack.

name: dForce Lending
description: On April 19, 2020, dForce/Lendf.Me was exploited via ERC777 reentrancy; attacker repeatedly supplied and withdrew tokens before balance updates, stealing $25M. Funds were recovered by law enforcement and exchanges within days.

name: IRYS AI
description: IRYS AI token on BSC deployed with a backdoor admin function that allowed the deployer to bypass standard permission checks. The _taxWallet was given privileged drain capability, enabling extraction of $69.6K directly from user wallets in a single transaction.

name: Channels Finance
description: Channels Finance, a Compound V2 fork on BSC, suffered an inflation attack exploiting improper token accounting. The attacker manipulated the protocol's supply mechanics to mint unbacked tokens, draining approximately $320K.

name: Bitcoin Gold
description: On May 16-24, 2018, Bitcoin Gold suffered a 51% attack in which attackers stole approximately 388,000 BTG (~$18M) through double-spend transactions targeting cryptocurrency exchanges. The attacker sent coins to exchanges, sold them for other assets, then reversed the initial transactions to reclaim funds.

name: ALP
description: ALP contract vulnerability where a function intended to be internal was left public, allowing unauthorized calls. Documented in DeFiHackLabs vulnerability database; amount not disclosed.

name: Arcadia V1
description: On July 10, 2023, Arcadia Finance V1 vault was exploited via reentrancy in liquidation. Attacker registered a malicious contract as both router and whitelisted account, spoofing context to execute unauthorized withdrawals, draining ~$455-460K in LP tokens across Ethereum and Optimism.

name: Swap-LP
description: Swap-LP's factory contract contained a low-level function vulnerability that an attacker exploited to manipulate liquidity pools. The attacker extracted approximately $1.1M (609 ETH) by calling restricted factory functions to drain value from the protocol's liquidity.

name: Poloniex
description: Poloniex hot wallet private keys compromised on November 10, 2023, draining $126M across Ethereum, Tron, and Bitcoin. Compromise likely via malware or social engineering. Justin Sun committed to full reimbursement.

name: JokInTheBox
description: JokInTheBox staking contract had an unstaking vulnerability where the state variable was not properly checked, allowing attackers to unstake multiple times from the same balance. Exploiter continuously withdrew funds, draining ~$34K from affected users.

name: Penpie
description: Penpie was drained of ~$27M via a reentrancy attack. The attacker created malicious SY tokens mimicking Pendle yield tokens and exploited missing reentrancy protection in _harvestBatchMarketRewards() to claim real rewards using fake token tickets.

name: GMBL.COMPUTER
description: On September 6, 2023, hours after launch, GMBL.COMPUTER on Arbitrum was exploited when the off-chain signature server issued valid signatures for spoofed referral claims without verifying deposits, draining ~471 ETH.

name: GMX V1 EVM
description: On July 9, 2025, GMX V1 perpetuals on Arbitrum suffered a $42M exploit through reentrancy in executeDecreaseOrder(). Attacker exploited the assumption that _account is an EOA, using a contract to reenter, manipulate short positions, inflate GLP price, and profit via redemptions; attacker returned funds July 12, keeping a $5M bounty.

name: SubQuery Network
description: SubQuery Network Settings contract on Base was exploited on April 12, 2026 due to missing owner guard on functions, allowing attacker to drain 382.4M SQT from pooled staking, 272 individual staker wallets, RewardsBooster, and treasury across five transactions.

name: fcdep
description: On February 11, 2023, the fcdep (EPMAX) protocol on BSC was attacked using a flash loan exploit. The attacker manipulated token balances through improper balance accounting to extract approximately $350K from the protocol.

name: Tenderize V2
description: Tenderize V2 suffered an exploit involving its proxy upgrade mechanism, resulting in a small loss on Ethereum due to improper proxy upgrade validation.

name: StakeHound / Fireblocks
description: StakeHound's 38,178 ETH became inaccessible when a 3-of-4 threshold signature key backup procedure failed. Fireblocks lost custody of 2 key shards during a machine failure in March 2021, and StakeHound failed to execute disaster recovery or verify the backup through third-party services. The keys became permanently unrecoverable.

name: LABUBU/OLPC
description: On June 20, 2026, a PancakeSwap V2 pool pairing OLPC and LABUBI on BNB Chain was exploited when the OLPC token's _update function had a maliciously configured decimalsValue parameter (7326680472586200649), causing massive unintended burns. This desynchronized cached reserves, allowing an attacker to drain ~$1.115M USDT via LABUBI swaps.

name: Coreum Bridge
description: On August 9, 2026, the Coreum Bridge connecting XRPL and Coreum was exploited via a flaw in its bridge logic, resulting in a loss of approximately $200,000. No dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: Term Finance
description: Term Finance's tETH oracle update introduced a decimal precision mismatch between oracle components. The incorrect decimal handling caused tETH to be priced incorrectly, triggering unintended liquidations of ~918 ETH as positions were force-closed at wrong prices.

name: EigenLayer
description: Attackers gained access to email communications about investor token custody, then impersonated the legitimate party to direct EigenLayer team to send 1.67M EIGEN tokens to an attacker-controlled address. The tokens were swapped and moved to CEXs.

name: Bankr
description: Bankr paused on May 19, 2026 after $170K was drained from 14 user wallets on Base. Attackers exploited phishing of session tokens or signing keys to make direct transfer() calls, bypassing token approvals.

name: Mt. Gox
description: Mt. Gox, the world's largest Bitcoin exchange, collapsed when it revealed that 850,000 BTC belonging to customers and the company were missing. The exchange had been incrementally hacked since at least 2011 when attackers gained access to the hot wallet, with hackers siphoning BTC over several years.

name: Cashaa
description: Attackers deployed malware on an OTC transaction manager's computer at Cashaa. The malware remained dormant until the employee logged into the system, then initiated 8 separate Bitcoin transfers totaling 335.91 BTC to attacker-controlled wallets across two days.

name: Predy Finance
description: Predy Finance's PredyPool contract lacked adequate access control in the take() function, allowing attackers to manipulate the liabilities array and drain liquidity from existing trading pairs via flash loans.

name: NuNet
description: An attacker possessing NuNet’s deployer/mint authority directly called mint() on the NTX token and created 408,532,878.13 unbacked NTX in a single mint. Unlike the related Fetch.ai incident, NuNet’s converter was not the exploited component. Bitquery’s on-chain reconstruction finds that the attacker held the NTX token’s own mint role, allowing the unauthorized supply to be created directly. The same attack cluster compromised multiple project authorization/deployer keys and also drained Fetch.ai’s converter

name: Paribus
description: Paribus was exploited through a reentrancy vulnerability in a Compound V2 fork, where the transfer occurred before storage updates. An attacker used flash loans and the reentrant redeem function to borrow against collateral twice, draining USDT, WBTC, and ETH.

name: FilDA
description: FilDA's lending protocol was exploited on the Elastos Smart Chain (ESC) and REI Network on April 23. Attackers exploited abandoned zero-balance asset pools and manipulated deposit/borrow operations to drain approximately $700K. The exploit leveraged the bridging mechanism and targeted deprecated markets that only existed on ESC and REI, which were subsequently halted pending security review.

name: DIMO
description: On November 7, 2025, DIMO token was exploited when a compromised developer key held proxy-upgrade authority over a Wormhole bridge contract with no timelock or multisig. The attacker withdrew 30M DIMO tokens (~3% supply, ~$2.49M), dumped them on the market, then the proxy was reverted and ownership moved to a multisig.

name: Bitget
description: Bitget's market-making bot on the VOXEL/USDT futures pair malfunctioned on April 20, 2025, entering a predictable buy-low/sell-high loop. Traders exploited the pattern with high leverage to extract ~$100M before Bitget froze accounts and rolled back trades.

name: Polyhedra Network
description: Polyhedra Network's private key leaked, allowing attackers to drain 1.4M THENA tokens from BNB Chain. Team attributed the breach to human theft rather than smart contract vulnerability; zkBridge security unaffected.

name: Secured Finance Lending
description: Attackers manipulated the market-unit price used to value lending positions by self-trading both sides of Secured Finance’s order book. getMarketUnitPrice() derived its price from blockTotalAmount / blockTotalFutureValue for orders filled in the current block, allowing attacker-controlled trades to push the reported price near par. The resulting inflated lend position was accepted as collateral, enabling assets to be withdrawn from the lending pool. A block-reliability check did not prevent manipulation performed atomically with flash-loaned liquidity

name: Hegic
description: Hegic's options contract had a typographical error using options.length instead of optionIDs.length, locking user funds after options expired. The developers ignored security audit warnings from Trail of Bits about critical flaws and rushed the contract to mainnet without fixes. Funds were recovered and users were refunded.

name: warp.green
description: warp.green’s ERC-20 bridge was exploited through a vulnerability in the Chia-side bridge module, resulting in two malicious transactions totaling 93,000 USDC-denominated assets. The attacker subsequently converted the assets to ETH. warp.green said it verified that there were no additional malicious transactions and offered the attacker a 10% white-hat bounty in exchange for returning 90% of the funds within 48 hours

name: NFPrompt
description: NFPrompt's treasury and contract administrator wallets compromised, draining treasury and ecosystem fund. ~$3M net realized loss after token price impact; FBI involved; NFP price dropped 13.8% post-breach.

name: Turtle Dex
description: TurtleDex on BSC executed a coordinated rugpull on March 19-20, 2021 days after raising 9K BNB (~$2.5M). Team drained liquidity from PancakeSwap and Ape Swap pools, converted to ETH, and withdrew via Binance.

name: Zapper
description: Zapper's .fi domain registrar was compromised via social engineering of Netim's support team, allowing attackers to redirect traffic to a malicious domain. Users visiting the fake zapper.fi were exposed to credential harvesting and unauthorized transactions. Zapper immediately notified users to use only zapper.xyz while working to recover the domain.

name: UPCX
description: On April 1, 2025, UPCX payment platform was exploited when an attacker used a compromised private key to upgrade the ProxyAdmin contract, enabling execution of withdrawByAdmin to drain 18.4M UPC tokens (~$70M) from three management accounts.

name: Beanstalk
description: An attacker flashloaned $1B+ from Aave, Uniswap, and SushiSwap to gain 2/3 governance voting power and execute malicious proposals (Bip18 to drain the protocol, Bip19 to donate to Ukraine as cover), stealing $181M in non-Bean assets.

name: JaredFromSubway MEV Bot
description: On June 20, 2026, Ethereum's prominent MEV bot JaredFromSubway.eth was drained of $7.5M+ in WETH, USDC, and USDT when an attacker deployed 66 fake token contracts as profitable MEV opportunities. The bot automatically granted large spending approvals to malicious contracts over weeks, which were then swept in a coordinated transaction and laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: Aquifer
description: Aquifer allowed the caller to supply the input-side token program used during swaps instead of pinning it to the canonical SPL Token Program. The attacker supplied a malicious program that accepted Aquifer’s CPI transfer instruction and returned success without transferring the required input tokens. Aquifer failed to verify the actual input-token balance increase and consequently released real output tokens from its vaults without receiving payment

name: Thetanuts Finance
description: On April 20, 2026 Thetanuts Finance's vault contract on Ethereum was exploited for $50,000 via a first-depositor inflation flaw: an attacker minted 1 share, donated 1,000 ETH directly to the contract, then redeemed the share for nearly all vault assets when the next user deposited.

name: The DAO
description: The DAO hack of June 17, 2016 was the first major Ethereum reentrancy attack. Attacker recursively called splitDAO before balance updates, extracting 3.6M ETH (~$60M).

name: DogWifTools
description: DogWifTools, a Solana rug-pull generator tool, was compromised via supply chain attack. Attackers gained control of the GitHub repository token and inserted malware into versions 1.6.3-1.6.6. Updates delivered malicious updater.exe files that acted as Remote Access Trojans, stealing cryptocurrency wallet private keys and extracting $10M from users.

name: Vestra DAO
description: On December 4, 2024, Vestra DAO's staking contract was exploited less than a month after launch when the unStake() function failed to validate whether a position was still active. The attacker repeatedly extracted rewards from already-unstaked positions, stealing 73.7 million VSTR tokens (~$500K).

name: Crypto DAO
description: On July 28, 2026, an unprotected exec() function in Crypto DAO's vault on BNB Chain allowed any caller to execute transfers, draining $8.2M USDT.

name: DIP
description: DIP token on BSC was exploited on June 17, 2026 when missing return statement in _transfer function caused swap transactions through PancakeSwap to execute twice, allowing attacker to manipulate pool prices.

name: Uniswap (Phishing Attack)
description: On July 11, 2022, a phishing campaign targeted Uniswap users by airdropping a malicious ERC20 token to 73,399 UNI holders, promising a $2K airdrop. When users interacted with the token to claim it, they signed malicious approvals granting the attacker access to their Uniswap V3 LP tokens. The attacker siphoned 7,574 ETH (~$8M) and moved 7,500 ETH through Tornado Cash.

name: TAC
description: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in the shared Cosmos EVM precompile layer and transferred 2,985,651,403 TAC from a single account to another account without authorization. TAC states that the incident was a drain rather than a mint: no new TAC was created and total supply remained unchanged. The network was halted at block 24,671,475 to contain the incident

name: Nexera
description: Attackers compromised Nexera's token contract credentials via BeaverTail malware on an employee machine, then transferred 47.24M NXRA. They sold 14.75M tokens for ~$449K before Nexera paused the contract and zeroed the remaining 32.5M.

name: GHT
description: GHT smart contract exploited via business logic flaw. Proof-of-concept documented in DeFiHackLabs but specific vulnerability mechanism and loss amount not publicly detailed.

name: Harvest Finance
description: Harvest Finance exploited October 26, 2020 for $24-34M via Curve oracle manipulation. Attacker deployed $50M flashloan to skew the Curve y-pool USDT/USDC balance, then repeatedly minted fTokens at depressed valuation and redeemed at normal price (~30 times in 7 minutes).

name: Venus Protocol
description: Venus's snBNB oracle experienced a malfunction where Binance Oracle fed an incorrect price (snBNB spiked to $77B), allowing an attacker to buy snBNB at thin liquidity and trigger unintended liquidations. The protocol incurred a shortfall of ~$274K.

name: Loopscale
description: Loopscale was exploited two weeks after launch when an attacker manipulated RateX PT token pricing to obtain undercollateralized loans, draining 5.7M USDC and 1,200 SOL.

name: CheeseBank
description: On November 6, 2020, CheeseBank was exploited for $3.3M via price oracle manipulation. The attacker borrowed 21,000 ETH via dYdX flashloan, purchased Cheese tokens on Uniswap to pump the price, deposited LP tokens, and borrowed all available stablecoins (USDC/USDT/DAI) against the inflated collateral.

name: Dexible V2
description: Dexible V2's selfSwap function lacked router validation, allowing attacker to call token contracts with transferFrom targeting accounts with Dexible approvals, draining $2.047M from 17 user wallets.

name: ChainSwap
description: ChainSwap bridge suffered an access control vulnerability in its cross-chain quota code. The attacker exploited a logical flaw that allowed invalid, non-whitelisted addresses to bypass authorization, take control of target projects' BSC contracts, and mint tokens directly to the attacker's address for sale.

name: Rigoblock
description: RigoBlock's Dragos contracts lacked the onlyOwner modifier on the setMultipleAllowances function, allowing attackers to modify token allowances without authorization. An attacker exploited this to drain 160.86 ETH from the protocol's liquidity pools. The attacker later returned 90% of funds, retaining 10% as a bounty.

name: LunaFi
description: LunaFi's reward claiming mechanism lacked a time lock in the claimRewards() function, allowing an attacker to repeatedly claim rewards using a malicious contract. The vulnerability enabled depositing, claiming, and withdrawing within a single transaction, generating profits while depleting the reward pool.

name: R0AR
description: R0ARStaking contract contained a backdoor embedded by an external developer during deployment. The backdoor directly modified storage slots to set a falsified balance for the attacker's address, which was then extracted using the emergency withdrawal function.

name: 8ightDAO
description: On December 6, 2021, 8ight Finance (Harmony-based OHM fork) lost ~$1.75M from treasury when admin private keys transmitted via unencrypted channels (Facebook group, Google Drive) were compromised.

name: Quicksilver Zone
description: On June 21, 2026, Quicksilver Zone was exploited via unchecked ZK proof verification in the minting function. An OLPC token owner had previously set malicious parameters and renounced ownership, allowing an attacker to forge proofs and mint ~505K unbacked qATOM and ~10M qOSMO.

name: IEXCBP
description: IEXCBP's reward withdrawal logic valued USD-denominated rewards using Pancake's live spot price quotes. An attacker flash-loaned WBNB and USDT, posted WBNB as collateral on Venus to borrow larger USDT amounts, then recycled capital through helper accounts interacting with IEXCBP. Each attacker-driven IEX token sale affected subsequent accounts' payout calculations, allowing complete reward pool draining through Pancake spot price manipulation.

name: LPC
description: LPC's _transfer function incorrectly calculated balances when sender and recipient addresses were the same. Attackers used a flashloan to exploit this logic error and extract value.

name: BYC Token
description: BYC token on BSC was exploited through a vulnerability in its autoBurnLiquidity function. The attacker manipulated the lpBurnFrequency parameter by performing large USDT-for-BYC swaps to inflate the parameter value, then called autoBurnLiquidity to reduce the BYC reserve to 1, enabling drainage of all USDT from the liquidity pool.

name: Coffer
description: Coffer’s BTC pool incorrectly rounded tiny deposits to zero while still minting LP tokens, allowing an attacker to repeatedly obtain shares without providing equivalent assets. The attacker submitted thousands of minimal deposits, diluting existing liquidity providers and minting approximately $18 in illegitimate LP tokens. Coffer paused its pools on October 18, preventing further withdrawals, and deployed a fix on October 19

name: Future Protocol
description: On July 2, 2025, Future Protocol (FPC) on Binance Smart Chain was exploited via a flash loan attack combined with token burn manipulation. The attacker borrowed 23M USDT, swapped it all for FPC to manipulate the pool price, then leveraged the tokenomics that burned FPC from the pool to create a price imbalance and extract approximately $4.6 million.

name: VeChain
description: VeChain's buyback wallet was compromised on December 13, 2019, at 12:27 AM GMT, resulting in theft of 1.1B VET tokens (~$6.5M). Internal misconduct was suspected, with a trojan-infected machine containing keylogging software enabling attacker access to private keys. The VeChain Foundation issued an emergency patch causing Authority Masternodes to vote and freeze the stolen funds. On December 30, the community voted to permanently destroy 727M of the frozen VET.

name: Dream Health Chain
description: A flaw in Dream Health Chain’s award state machine allowed the same fixed award to be claimed repeatedly. createAward() recorded a reward without reserving collateral for that award, while participateAward() allowed an already claimed award (status=2) to be reset to claimable (status=1). The attacker repeatedly reset and reclaimed awards for as little as a 0–1 wei transfer, draining funds from the contract’s shared proxy balance

name: Balancer V2
description: On November 3, 2025, Balancer V2's Composable Stable Pools were exploited for $128M via a rounding-down flaw in batchSwap invariant calculation. Minuscule discrepancies in each transaction compounded across rapid successive swaps, gradually deflating pool reserves across chains.

name: Qubit
description: On January 27-28, 2022 an attacker drained $80 million from Qubit Finance's QBridge cross-chain bridge by calling the deposit function with a zero address token and no ETH, exploiting improper use of call() instead of SafeERC20 verification to bypass input validation. The attacker minted 77,162 qXETH and borrowed $37.6M in wETH, $28.5M in BTC-B, and stablecoins.

name: MooCAKECTX
description: On November 7, 2022, MooCAKECTX on BSC was exploited via a flashloan attack targeting the reward settlement logic, where the attacker borrowed 50,000 CAKE, pledged twice in the same transaction without reward settlement, and withdrew to profit approximately $143,921. The contract failed to settle previous rewards before reinvesting.

name: Livecoin
description: Attacker gained control of Livecoin's backend servers and nodes via compromised credentials. Once in control, hackers manipulated exchange rates to absurd levels (Bitcoin to $450K, ETH to $15K) and drained multiple assets from hot wallets. The exchange shut down permanently and never recovered.

name: Numa
description: Numa on Arbitrum was exploited when the protocol's cNuma collateral valuation logic lacked protection against spot price manipulation. The attacker flash-minted nuBTC to artificially inflate synthetic liabilities and deflate collateral valuations.

name: Seedify
description: On September 23, 2025 at 12:05 UTC, attackers linked to North Korean 'Contagious Interview' operation used a compromised developer key to reconfigure Seedify's Avalanche bridge contract, enabling unauthorized SFUND minting across Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base. The attacker sold ~$1.2M on BNB Chain before ~$200K was frozen at an exchange.

name: Garden
description: On October 30, 2025, one of Garden Finance's solvers was compromised, enabling an attacker to control cross-chain interactions and drain over $10M in a coordinated exploit across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and Solana.

name: Demex
description: Demex's Nitron lending market was exploited via donation-based oracle manipulation targeting a deprecated dGLP vault. An attacker donated a small amount of fsGLP to inflate the GLP redemption rate, which Nitron's oracle accepted as accurate pricing for dGLP. The attacker then used the falsely inflated dGLP value as collateral to borrow legitimate assets.

name: GriffinAI
description: GriffinAI on BSC lost $3M on September 24, 2025 when misconfigured LayerZero peer validation let attacker initialize a fake peer on Ethereum and mint 5B unauthorized GAIN tokens on BSC. Attacker swapped ~150M tokens before GAIN crashed 90%.

name: Dough Finance
description: On July 12, 2024 Dough Finance on Ethereum was exploited for approximately $1.96 million via unvalidated call data in the ConnectorDeleverageParaswap contract, where attackers combined a flashloan with the arbitrary external call vulnerability to manipulate data and transfer WETH. Stolen funds were swapped to ETH and 600 ETH (~$1.8M) was later deposited into Tornado Cash; a white-hat recovered 69.12 ETH.

name: CoinTiger (PTT)
description: CoinTiger's cold wallet was breached on July 1, 2019, but the theft was only announced on August 17, 47 days later. Attackers stole 401,981,748 PTT tokens (~$9.2M), which they distributed across markets (120M PTT entered trading, causing the price to crash nearly 100%) while 280M were frozen by the Proton Chain project. CoinTiger's lack of multi-signature security on cold storage enabled the compromise.

name: ZetaChain
description: On April 26-27, 2026, ZetaChain's GatewayZEVM contract was exploited due to missing access control in call() and unrestricted external calls in GatewayEVM.execute(). Attacker drained $333,868 in USDC/USDT across four chains from team wallets by leveraging standing token approvals.

name: MM Finance Cronos
description: On May 4, 2022, MM.Finance's DNS infrastructure was compromised, allowing attackers to inject a malicious contract address. Users interacting with swap, add liquidity, or remove liquidity functions had their funds siphoned to the attacker's wallet. Approximately $2M in CRO was stolen and laundered through Tornado Cash to OKX.

name: LaunchZone
description: On February 27, 2023, LaunchZone on BSC suffered a $700,000 exploit via missing access control on the transferFrom() function in the Bscex SwapX contract. The attacker manipulated LZ token prices and executed arbitrary token transfers from liquidity pools.

name: GSS
description: On August 24, 2023, GSS token on BSC was exploited via a vulnerability in its _transfer() function. An attacker flash-loaned 30,000 BUSDT from DODO and swapped to 725,246 GSS tokens. By transferring tokens to specific pair addresses and calling skim(), the attacker caused 707,162 tokens to be withdrawn twice from the liquidity pool, an arithmetic error in the custom transfer logic.

name: NovaBox
description: On June 9, 2026, NovaBox suffered a timing flaw where dividend calculations executed before stake balance updates were finalized, allowing an attacker to claim phantom dividends and drain 99.86% of the reward pool (~$107K).

name: Caterpillar Coin
description: On September 10, 2024, the CUT token on BSC was exploited via a flashloan attack that manipulated its price on PancakeSwap. The attacker used flash-loaned USDT to repeatedly add and remove liquidity, earning rewards based on inflated CUT prices, then drained the pair for approximately $1.4M with 99% slippage.

name: Renegade
description: On May 10, 2026, Renegade V1 on Arbitrum was exploited for $209K via unprotected initializer function and proxy version counter desynchronization. Attacker injected malicious logic via delegatecall to drain 27 ERC-20 tokens; whitehat recovered ~$190K within 45 minutes.

name: FixedTokenBSwap
description: FixedTokenBSwap swap contract was exploited on June 15, 2025 via attacker-supplied path parameters combined with a fake token's transferFrom bypass, circumventing the on-chain price check and allowing extraction of fixed RTV amounts per transaction.

name: WXETA
description: On September 16, 2024, an attacker reinitialized the WXETA contract through its unguarded initialize function, granted themselves minting permissions, and drained USDT/WXETA liquidity pools for $110,000.

name: EtherCrash
description: EtherCrash's cold wallet, claimed to be the most mature Ethereum gambling game, was compromised on October 27. Two large withdrawals totaling ~$2.5M were made and exchanged to DAI on Uniswap. The single-key wallet design left it vulnerable with no recovery options.

name: Arcadia V2
description: On July 15, 2025, Arcadia V2 RebalancerSpot was exploited through an unvalidated router address parameter. Attacker registered a malicious router, flash-loaned $1.5B from Morpho Blue, bypassed health checks, and drained LP positions for $2.5M-$3.6M profit.

name: Maestro
description: A vulnerability in the Maestro Router 2 contract behind a Telegram trading bot allowed attackers to execute arbitrary external calls, pulling tokens from user wallets that had granted the router approvals. Maestro identified and fixed the exploit within about 30 minutes and paused trading.

name: Gatecoin
description: Between May 9-12, 2016, Hong Kong-based Gatecoin suffered a breach where attackers exploited a server reboot disruption to reroute deposits from cold multi-signature wallets to a vulnerable hot wallet. Approximately 250 BTC and 185,000 ETH (~$2M) were stolen, representing 15% of exchange assets.

name: Ocean Protocol
description: Ocean Protocol's SideStaking-managed BPool clones on Polygon were exploited via asymmetric join/exit math. An attacker flash-borrowed mOCEAN tokens, cycled them through eight BPool clones, and extracted a net profit by exploiting the single-sided liquidity operation calculations.

name: BTER
description: BTER's cold wallet storage system was breached, resulting in the theft of 7,170 BTC. The fact that offline cold storage was compromised suggested a possible insider threat, though the full mechanism was never disclosed. The exchange suspended operations immediately.

name: Grand Base
description: On April 15, 2024, Grand Base, a real-world asset tokenization platform on Base, was exploited when a developer PC was hacked, exposing the deployer wallet with token minting and LP control. The attacker minted 808.57 ETH worth of GB tokens (~$1.7-2.5M) and sold them, causing a >99% price crash.

name: MultiversX
description: An attacker exploited a VM-level atomicity issue in MultiversX that allowed invalid state changes to occur because of an order-of-operations error in edge cases. Validators paused network progression to contain the incident. MultiversX prepared a protocol correction and coordinated hard-fork recovery from a known-good checkpoint. A September 23 restart attempt failed because insufficient Shard 1 validators synchronized and transitioned into the new epoch within the activation window, so the mainnet remained paused while recovery software was updated for another restart attempt

name: MyAlgo
description: Between February 19-21, 2023, MyAlgo wallet on Algorand suffered a breach where 19.5M ALGO and 3.5M USDC (~$9.6M) were stolen from high-value accounts. The root cause was unclear: either the website was compromised to exfiltrate private keys or users' seed phrases were compromised via phishing. ChangeNow froze an additional $1.5M.

name: Phantom Galaxies
description: Hackers compromised Phantom Galaxies' Discord server using malware that bypassed 2FA on admin accounts. Attackers created a fake NFT minting page charging 0.1 ETH as a 'minting fee' that directed funds to their wallet. In three hours, fraudsters stole 265 ETH before Animoca Brands discovered and halted the scam, later covering all losses.

name: WAX Multi-Chain Bridge
description: WAX’s eth.token::withdraw function failed to validate that max_fee was nonnegative. By setting max_fee = -quantity, the attacker reduced the total account debit to zero while retaining the full withdrawal amount. Because the configured withdrawal fee was zero, the fee check did not reject the transaction. The resulting withdrawal logs triggered real payouts from the bridge on Solana and Ethereum

name: AutoChain Global
description: AutoChain Global smart contract was exploited on June 14, 2024, resulting in ~$113K in losses. Technical details of the vulnerability remain limited in public sources.

name: Odin.Fun
description: On August 12-13, 2025 Odin.Fun (Bitcoin-based memecoin launchpad on ICP) lost 58.2 BTC (~$7 million) to attackers who deposited worthless tokens (SATOSHI, ODINPEPE), used overweighted deposits and self-trading to artificially inflate token value in the protocol's internal AMM logic (which lacked external oracle validation), and drained the pool.

name: Badger DAO
description: On December 2, 2021, Badger DAO suffered a $120M hack when an attacker used a compromised Cloudflare API key to inject malicious code into the frontend. Users unknowingly approved token transfers via spoofed UI, allowing the attacker to drain approximately 2,100 BTC and 151 ETH from ~200 accounts.

name: Paid Network
description: PAID Network's token contract was compromised on March 5, 2021 when an attacker gained access to the deployment wallet's private key. The attacker upgraded the contract to enable unlimited token minting, creating 59.4M unauthorized PAID tokens.

name: BeautyChain
description: On April 22, 2018, BeautyChain token suffered an integer overflow in the batchTransfer function, allowing attackers to generate 10^58 BEC tokens. Though face value was astronomical, the actual loss was limited by exchanges halting BEC/SMT trading on April 25 in response to the vulnerability.

name: Rari Capital
description: Rari Capital's Fuse lending pools were exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability in exitMarket() when an attacker used a Balancer flashloan to deposit collateral, then recursively borrowed assets and withdrew collateral before borrow records were updated, stealing approximately 28,380 ETH and related assets.

name: MakerDAO
description: During the March 12 ETH crash (43% in one day), the Maker Medianizer oracle failed to update due to network congestion and high gas fees, leaving the system with stale prices. Liquidators exploited this by bidding zero DAI for collateral worth millions, acquiring 62K ETH for free. 36% of liquidations resulted in zero-bid auctions, causing a $6M DAI shortfall and $4M bad debt before governance intervention.

name: Resolv USR
description: Resolv's AWS KMS-hosted SERVICE_ROLE private key was compromised, enabling the minting of 80M unbacked USR stablecoins. The attacker swapped USR to wstUSR and then to ETH, extracting $24.5M before the protocol depeg.

name: MetaDragon
description: MetaDragon's NFT contract lacked ownership verification on minted NFTs, allowing attackers to claim and convert over 4,000 NFTs belonging to other users. The attacker sold the stolen META tokens for 321.5 BNB.

name: CoinDash
description: CoinDash's ICO website was compromised on July 17-18, 2017 within 13 minutes of launch. Attacker replaced the deposit address with their own; 2,000+ investors sent 37K ETH (~$7M) to the attacker before the ICO was pulled. Hacker retained ~13.4K ETH (~$11.7M).

name: four.meme
description: Four.Meme's launch feature improperly restricted token transfers before public listing. An attacker used a low-level function to bypass MODE_TRANSFER_RESTRICTED, creating unauthorized trading pairs for pre-launch tokens and extracting liquidity at attacker-controlled prices.

name: EOS Max
description: EOS Max gambling DApp was exploited via a rollback attack on December 19, 2018, where attackers used EOS's blacklist functionality to revert blockchain transactions after betting outcomes were determined. The attack allowed players to recover bets even after losing. Multiple EOS gambling DApps were targeted simultaneously via this vector.

name: XBridge
description: XBridge cross-chain bridge built by SaitaChain was exploited on April 24, 2024 on Ethereum and BNB Chain when unprotected listToken and withdrawTokens functions allowed attacker to register as token owner and drain bridge-held assets.

name: DMM Bitcoin
description: On May 31, 2024, DMM Bitcoin lost 48 billion yen ($305M) in bitcoin when North Korean Lazarus Group attackers compromised an employee, intercepted legitimate transactions, and drained the hot wallet. The exchange ultimately shut down and transferred to SBI VC Trade.

name: Swan Treasury
description: On July 30, 2026 an attacker used Swan Treasury's leaked off-chain signer key to generate valid signatures with the discount parameter set to 1, buying ~687,000 STY on BNB Chain at roughly 1/100 of intended price using a ~19,700 USDT PancakeSwap flash loan, then dumping the tokens for a ~$625K protocol loss.

name: Chain Fusion
description: Fusion's swap wallet (0x8e6bDa71f3f0F49dDD29969De79aFCFac4457379) was compromised on September 28, 2019, with attackers stealing 10M native FSN and 3.5M ERC20 FSN tokens (~$6.4M total). Investigation determined the private key was stolen and suggested potential inside involvement. Some stolen tokens were wash-traded across exchanges before being frozen, causing FSN price to crash 50% within hours.

name: BtcTurk
description: BtcTurk lost $54-55M on June 22, 2024 when attackers compromised private keys to 10 hot wallets targeting Avalanche holdings. Binance froze $5.3M of recovered funds.

name: Ledger
description: Phishing campaign targeting Ledger users with fake data-breach alert emails claiming security compromise and urging firmware updates. Attackers used Punycode domain spoofing (e.g., ledģėr.com) to disguise malicious URLs and trick users into compromising their hardware wallet recovery phrases.

name: Transit Finance
description: Transit Finance, a cross-chain aggregation protocol, suffered an exploit draining approximately $257.8K via an unauthenticated swap callback mechanism. The exploit allowed unauthorized parties to trigger callback functions during swap operations without proper authorization, enabling fund extraction from the protocol.

name: BGM
description: On November 10, 2024, BGM token on BNB Chain was exploited via a price manipulation attack. The contract's reliance on spot price allowed the attacker to manipulate the price oracle and extract over $450K.

name: BNBX
description: On April 27, 2024, the BNBX token on BSC was exploited via a precision loss vulnerability in arithmetic operations, allowing attackers to manipulate token accounting and extract value. The exact amount extracted was not publicly disclosed.

name: KiloEx
description: On April 14, 2025, at 18:53 UTC, KiloEx was exploited for $7.5M via ETH/USD price oracle manipulation across Base, BSC, and opBNB. The attacker opened positions at artificially low prices and closed at real high prices without the oracle system validating feed freshness or enforcing rate limits.

name: Ratio Finance
description: On December 3, 2022, Ratio Finance on Solana experienced a developer private key compromise. Attacker accessed protocol accounts and drained user collateral; exact loss not specified. Incident disclosed January 17, 2023.

name: Duelbits
description: Duelbits suffered unauthorized transfers from hot wallets across Ethereum, BSC, Bitcoin, and Tron. Stolen assets were rapidly moved, bridged and largely consolidated into ETH and DAI on Ethereum. Duelbits took its platform offline while investigating and stated that user funds were safe. Security researchers suspect compromise of hot-wallet private keys, but Duelbits has not yet published a technical root cause

name: AurumCoin
description: AurumCoin suffered a 51% attack in November 2018 where an attacker gained majority network hashpower. The attacker performed a double-spend attack, sending 15,752.26 AU to the Cryptopia exchange worth approximately $500,000, selling them for other cryptocurrencies, then rolling back the transaction. The attack rendered the blockchain inactive as of November 29, 2018.

name: ULME
description: On October 25, 2022, ULME on BSC was exploited via a parameter validation flaw that lacked access control, allowing an attacker to use a flashloan, iterate through authorized spenders, drain their BUSD, manipulate ULME price, and extract approximately 50,646 BUSD (~$250K) before repaying the loan.

name: PRXVT
description: On January 1, 2026, attacker exploited PRXVT staking contract on Base via Sybil attack; deployed numerous CREATE2 addresses to bypass per-address limits and farm rewards, draining 32.8 ETH (~$97K). No cost/identity constraints protected the per-address logic.

name: Polydex
description: A reentrancy vulnerability in the PLX Locker smart contract exploiting ERC777 token callbacks allowed an attacker to recursively call withdraw functions and drain 500K worth of assets. The attacker bridged stolen funds to Ethereum before the team could patch the timelock-delayed fix.

name: Cryptopia
description: On January 14, 2019, Cryptopia's hot wallet private keys were compromised, enabling theft of approximately 10 percent of platform holdings in ERC-20 tokens across 17,000 customer accounts.

name: DAppSocial
description: DAppSocial's lockTokens() function lacked validation that tokens were actually transferred, allowing an attacker to call deposit and create_deposit_record without sending funds. The attacker deployed a helper contract, deposited 2 USDT, set lock duration to 0, and withdrew without depositing tokens, exploiting the broken balance check.

name: Fetch.ai
description: Unknown fraudsters gained access to Fetch.ai's Binance account and sold FET tokens at significantly reduced prices to associated entities for profitable resale. On June 6, 2021, approximately 2.6M USD worth of tokens were extracted. Fetch.ai successfully obtained a London High Court order requiring Binance to trace and freeze the attacker's accounts.

name: OmniEstate
description: On January 17, 2023, the OMNI Real Estate Token (ORT) staking pool on BSC was exploited due to insufficient parameter validation. The StakingPool contract's _Check_reward function returned an incorrect value when durations was 0. An attacker invested 1 Wei with durations set to 0, bypassing verification, and repeatedly called withdrawAndClaim to extract 236 BNB (~$70.7K).

name: NowSwap
description: NowSwap DEX on Ethereum was exploited on September 15, 2021 when K constant value mismatch (updated in 2 of 3 code locations during upgrade) allowed attacker to swap 1 wei for 98% of pool reserves.

name: DLMC
description: DLMC on BSC was exploited via flash loan price manipulation. The attacker used a flash loan to manipulate the protocol's internal token price, allowing redemption of referral rewards at an inflated rate. Referral rewards were minted and immediately sellable, providing efficient value extraction without holding positions.

name: Auctus
description: Auctus options protocol had a beta contract allowing arbitrary low-level calls with controlled calldata. An attacker exploited this to drain approved user funds from wallets, targeting those who had granted unlimited approval to the contract.

name: Ramses Exchange
description: Ramses' reward distribution mechanism failed to decrease tokenTotalSupplyByPeriod after reward claims, allowing attackers to claim rewards repeatedly across multiple NFT positions and drain accumulated incentives and fees.

name: Saga
description: Saga DAO, a community-run fan club for Solana's mobile phone, lost ~$60,000 (750 SOL) when zkRedDevil's personal wallet was compromised, allowing unauthorized drainage of both personal and DAO treasury funds. The multisig wallet had never been properly activated, requiring only 1 of 12 confirmations for fund transfers.

name: Gnosis Pay
description: On June 1, 2026, Gnosis Pay's Zodiac modules were exploited via a flawed ERC-1271 signature verification check that failed to validate contract call success. The attack affected 5,281 wallets, but Gnosis detected it within 2 hours and refunded users 100%.

name: VTSwapHook
description: VTSwapHook on Uniswap V4 was exploited through a pricing curve approximation error where the hook used midpoint averages instead of proper logarithmic curve integration, combined with fee accounting bugs that inflated virtual reserves.

name: Full Sail
description: Full Sail’s automated vaults suffered losses following abnormal or compromised Switchboard oracle data on Sui. Full Sail uses Switchboard as an external oracle and has safeguards intended to cross-check oracle prices against on-chain pool prices, but it has not yet disclosed how the compromised feed bypassed or interacted with those protections

name: Sharwa.Finance
description: Sharwa.Finance lost $32.85K on May 1, 2026 on Arbitrum via oracle price manipulation. Attack leveraged incorrect oracle price data to extract value from the protocol.

name: Maya Protocol
description: A multi-bug interaction in MayaChain’s outbound/slashing and pool-accounting flow caused a staged ARB.LINK pool to be credited with approximately 49.45M CACAO that was never actually transferred into the pool. Multiple messages sharing one native transaction ID caused the final DONATE message to overwrite outbound tracking state, making legitimate LINK outbounds appear missing. MayaChain consequently treated them as unauthorized vault outbounds and invoked slashing. During the resulting subsidy calculation, pool state was updated with an uncapped CACAO credit before the corresponding Reserve-to-Asgard transfer was attempted. That transfer failed because the Reserve lacked sufficient CACAO, but the inflated pool state was not rolled back. The attacker then added liquidity to the effectively asset-empty ARB.LINK pool, obtained nearly all pool ownership, and withdrew approximately 48.87M CACAO from Asgard liquidity

name: RocketSwap Base
description: RocketSwap's farm contract on Base was drained of 471 ETH ($865K) when attackers used brute force to compromise server-hosted private keys and gain control of the proxy contract with overly permissive transfer permissions.

name: BonkDAO
description: On July 6, 2026, attacker purchased enough BONK to control ~99.88% of governance votes, then passed proposal BIP #76 to drain 4.43T BONK from treasury. Missing timelocks and 1% quorum threshold enabled the attack.

name: Heco Bridge
description: On November 22, 2023, the HECO Chain bridge to Ethereum was drained of $86.6M when the operator's account was compromised, enabling unauthorized asset withdrawals.

name: Dot.Finance
description: On August 25, 2021, Dot.Finance on BSC was exploited via a flash loan attack that manipulated the VaultPinkBNB contract's token pricing. The attacker injected Cake tokens to inflate the performanceFee parameter, enabling the mintFor function to create excessive pink tokens worth approximately $429.7K.

name: Chainge Finance
description: On April 15, 2024, ChaingeFinance on BSC was exploited via arbitrary external call in the swap function. Both the target contract and callData parameters were controllable, allowing attackers to execute unauthorized transferFrom calls on victim accounts, draining all approved tokens.

name: BCE
description: BCE token's flawed burn mechanism was exploited to manipulate AMM reserves via malicious contracts that triggered burns inside the PancakeSwap pool, distorting the BCE-USDT balance and enabling reserve extraction.

name: KipCoin
description: KipCoin's Linode-hosted servers were compromised when attackers gained access to the wallet.dat file in May 2014. The attacker remained dormant until December 2014, when they began moving the 3,000+ stolen BTC.

name: Scallop Lend
description: Attacker exploited deprecated V2 contract from November 2023; uninitialized 'last_index' variable in rewards logic allowed unbounded claims. Using flashloan and oracle manipulation, attacker drained the sSUI rewards pool.

name: Yapeswap
description: YapeSwap’s WorkersUnion governance contract allowed proposals to pass with zero quorum, enabling an attacker controlling approximately 0.000055% of voting power to transfer YapeFactory’s feeToSetter role to themselves. The attacker then installed a malicious Registry that returned fake vault addresses through latestVault(), while vaults() continued listing legitimate vaults. This redirected deposits into attacker-controlled destinations while YapePair incorrectly accounted for them as farming assets, resulting in approximately $21,900 in losses

name: TesseraDAO
description: An attacker gained control of TesseraDAO's core contract and used ownership privileges to mint 99M TSR tokens from nothing, swapping them for $2.49M USDT. The attacker reassigned roles, seized ownership, and drained the treasury by dumping the freshly-minted tokens on Uniswap before withdrawing through Tornado Cash. The exploit went undetected for 19 hours after the mint.

name: Gamma
description: On January 4, 2024, Gamma Strategies' hypervisors on Arbitrum were exploited for ~$4.5M via flashloan-induced price manipulation. The vault deposit thresholds were set too high (-50% to +100% price swings), allowing attackers to manipulate underlying asset prices and drain vault positions.

name: ether.fi Liquid
description: Veda’s AtomicQueue allowed the caller of solve() to supply an arbitrary solver address without authenticating that the address had consented to participate as the solver. The settlement logic then executed want.safeTransferFrom(solver, user, amount). The attacker created a worthless token, submitted a self-request offering that token in exchange for liquidETH, and supplied existing liquidETH holders as the solver. Because those holders had previously approved AtomicQueue, the contract used their allowances to pull liquidETH directly from their wallets and transfer it to the attacker’s request. Eleven users were drained in a single transaction

name: AlphaPo
description: AlphaPo's hot wallets were drained of ~$60M across Ethereum, Tron, and Bitcoin on July 23, 2023 after private key exposure.

name: Local Traders
description: On May 23, 2023, Local Traders protocol on BSC was exploited when an attacker called an unprotected function (0xb5863c10) to become the contract owner, then manipulated token pricing to purchase LCT tokens at artificially low prices and resell them.

name: Denaria vAMM
description: Denaria's perpetual exchange was exploited through virtual AMM manipulation where an attacker used a flash loan to provide one-sided liquidity, skew the price ratio, and execute oversized trades that inflated PnL calculations without any manipulation guard.

name: Royal.io
description: Royal.io's legacy royalties contract (Royal1155LD) on Polygon was exploited via a flash loan combined with 100 zero-value ERC1155 transfers that manipulated the beforeLdaTransfer reward accounting hook through a logic flaw in the pro-rata royalty accounting function.

name: Orbit Bridge
description: Orbit Bridge was drained for ~$81.5M across its Ethereum vault when 7 of 10 multisig signer private keys were compromised, enabling fraudulent withdrawal signatures.

name: Wintermute
description: On June 5, 2022, Wintermute lost 20 million Optimism governance tokens when an Ethereum L1 multisig address was provided for L2 deposit but had not been pre-deployed on Optimism. An attacker deployed the Gnosis Safe contract and took control of the address before Wintermute could recover the tokens.

name: Unilend V2
description: Unilend V2 lost $197.6K when attacker used a flash loan to deposit 60M USDC, then exploited stale balance references in the userBalanceOfToken function to manipulate health factor calculations and withdraw 60 stETH.

name: Quixotic
description: On July 1, 2022, Quixotic NFT marketplace on Optimism was exploited due to a missing signature check in the fillSellOrder() function. The attacker minted NFTs, listed them for sale, and used the vulnerability to swap any victim's wallet tokens for the attacker's NFTs. The team paused all activity and reimbursed affected users.

name: Gravity Bridge
description: On May 30, 2026, Gravity Bridge suffered a $5.4 million exploit via compromised validator signing key. Stolen assets included $4.3M USDC, 274 ETH (~$553K), and $434K USDT; attacker laundered most through ChangeNow and Binance.

name: Mirror
description: Mirror Protocol was exploited from October 8, 2021 through May 17, 2022 (discovered) via duplicate ID vulnerability in collateral unlock logic, allowing excessive unlocks without proportional validation. Over seven months, attackers siphoned $89.7M before detection due to limited Terra monitoring.

name: CREAM Lending
description: On August 30, 2021, CREAM Finance suffered a reentrancy attack losing 418M AMP tokens and 1,308 ETH (~$18.8M). Using a 500 ETH flash loan as seed capital, the attacker exploited a reentrancy vulnerability in the AMP token callback handler to self-liquidate and withdraw more collateral than deposited.

name: GANA Payment
description: On November 20, 2025, an attacker obtained GANA Payment's private keys, manipulated reward rates and the unstake function to drain approximately $3.1 million in tokens, then laundered 1,140 BNB and 346 ETH through Tornado Cash.

name: FPR
description: FPR protocol on BSC suffered an access control vulnerability allowing unauthorized calls to privileged functions. The exploit drained $29K in protocol assets through improper permission checks.

name: USDGambit and TLP
description: Attackers compromised a shared deployer account that managed both USDGambit and TLP contracts, likely through key theft or credential compromise. This allowed them to deploy a new ProxyAdmin contract with full control over both protocols, draining $1.5M before moving funds to Ethereum and depositing into Tornado Cash.

name: Ragnarok Online Invasion
description: Ragnarok Online Invasion's ROI token contract on BSC was exploited on September 8, 2022 when an attacker called the unprotected transferOwnership function. Despite the contract having an onlyOwner modifier, it was not applied to the ownership transfer function, allowing unauthorized ownership changes and theft of ~158 BNB.

name: Slope Wallet
description: On August 2-3, 2022, attackers drained 9,231 Solana wallets when Slope Finance's mobile apps shipped user seed phrases in plaintext to an external logging service, exposing credentials outside the device. Every affected address had been created, imported, or used in the Slope iOS/Android apps.

name: Yearn Finance
description: On February 4, 2021, attacker used flashloans to acquire 215,000 ETH, then deposited borrowed USDC/DAI into Yearn's yDAI vault at manipulated exchange rates without sufficient slippage protection. The vault lost $11M; attacker profited ~$2.7M after $3.5M in fees.

name: Paraluni Masterchef
description: Paraluni MasterChef lost $1.7M on March 13, 2022 to a flashloan-funded reentrancy attack. Attacker borrowed 157K USDT and 157K BUSD via PancakeSwap, exploited depositByAddLiquidity's missing pool ID validation, and triggered reentrancy via malicious transferFrom before state updated.

name: FENGSHOU
description: On April 25, 2024, the FENGSHOU (NGFS) token on BSC was exploited via a public delegateCallReserves function with insufficient access control. An attacker set their own contract as the UniSwap proxy and executed arbitrary code within the vulnerable contract, extracting approximately $191K.

name: BV-7X
description: Two BV7X team wallets were compromised through phishing approvals on September 20, allowing an attacker to transfer approximately 6.18 million BV7X using Permit2 and an unlimited token allowance. One approval remained active for 27 days, enabling the attacker to steal another 149.06 million BV7X after liquidity was withdrawn into the affected wallet on October 17. The team subsequently deployed a replacement token contract and initiated a migration intended to exclude the stolen holdings

name: QANX Bridge
description: Bridge authority credentials were compromised, allowing extraction of 4.4M QANX tokens (370 ETH, ~$707K at time of exploit). The attacker traded stolen tokens through DEX, achieving significant liquidation of the position.

name: DRLVaultV3
description: DRLVaultV3, a USDC-WETH rebalance vault, was exploited by an attacker who manipulated the Uniswap spot price. The attacker first borrowed 14M USDC from Morpho Blue and bought WETH to spike its price, then triggered the vault's swapToWETH function to force it to buy WETH at the inflated price, and finally sold the pre-purchased WETH back into the pool to capture the profit spread. A whitehat hacker (c0ffe.babe.eth) captured the approximately $100K in USDC that should be recoverable.

name: Spectral Labs
description: On December 1, 2024, Spectral Labs' Syntax V2 was exploited for 14,793 SPEC (~$250K) via an unintended infinite ERC-20 approval in AgentToken.sol's tax-calculation path. The attacker used a flashloan and an insufficiently restricted deposit() function to shift token balances and misprice the XYK bonding curve, extracting disproportionate value from the pool.

name: EraLend
description: On July 25, 2023, EraLend on zkSync suffered a read-only reentrancy attack in code borrowed from SyncSwap, where an attacker repeatedly called a vulnerable function to manipulate asset prices via the internal oracle, draining $3.4M. Only USDC deposits were affected.

name: Raga Finance
description: No credible sources found documenting a specific Raga Finance hack on November 22, 2025. Raga Finance operates on Hyperliquid L1, but no evidence of a direct exploit was found.

name: WhaleBit
description: WhaleBit's staking system was exploited through same-transaction spot price depression via flash loan, where the attacker dumped CES tokens into the Algebra pool to depress price and inflated staking redemption payouts by 14.4-15.7%.

name: Patricia
description: Nigerian crypto exchange Patricia suffered a security breach compromising Bitcoin and Naira assets, resulting in $2M in losses. Although the breach occurred in January 2022, it was only disclosed in May 2023. Patricia committed to a 2-5 year repayment plan for affected users starting December 2024.

name: Safemoon
description: On March 28, 2023, SafeMoon suffered an $8.9 million exploit via a publicly-accessible burn function left unprotected after an upgrade. The attacker destroyed SFM tokens to inflate their value, deposited, and withdrew disproportionate BNB. The attacker returned 80% of the funds ($7.2M) on April 20, keeping 20% as a claimed bug bounty.

name: Compound V2
description: Compound V2's Comptroller had a conditional logic bug when Proposal 62 activated on September 29-30, 2021. An off-by-one error (> instead of >=) in the COMP distribution calculation allowed users to claim far more tokens than intended.

name: Hegic(old contract)
description: A deprecated Hegic WBTC Puts Pool contract (deployed January 4, 2022) was drained through its unprotected withdrawWithoutHedge() path, which did not decrement share balances. The attacker deposited liquidity, bought put options, withdrew the liquidity, then exercised the options.

name: GemPad
description: On December 17, 2024, GemPad's token launchpad was exploited via reentrancy in the collectFees function across Ethereum, Base, and BNB Chain. Attacker stole $1.9 million from multiple liquidity locker instances using a vulnerable template that 27 projects had deployed.

name: Flexcoin
description: Flexcoin's exchange had a race condition in its transfer code. An attacker sent thousands of simultaneous transfer requests between user accounts, moving coins from one account to another until the sending account was overdrawn before balances were updated, stealing 896 BTC.

name: vETH
description: On November 14, 2024, vETH on Ethereum was exploited through a vulnerable price dependency mechanism. The protocol's reliance on a manipulable oracle allowed attackers to extract value.

name: Monoswap
description: MonoSwap developer was lured on July 24-25, 2024 by fake venture capitalists into installing a malicious 'Kakao' video-call app that stole private keys. Attacker used the keys to withdraw ~$1.3M in staked liquidity and protocol funds from the Blast-based DEX.

name: Galaxy Fox
description: Galaxy Fox token's setMerkleRoot function was publicly accessible without access control, allowing attackers to manipulate the merkle root and falsely claim 108 ETH from the contract's funds.

name: Yala
description: During Yala's deployment of its Solana Layer Zero OFT bridge, attackers compromised temporary deployment keys. They used this access to create unauthorized bridge contracts and establish a backdoor for later exploitation. Over a month later, the attacker deployed this infrastructure to mint 120M unauthorized $YU tokens and extract $7.64M in real value. Thai authorities arrested the attacker approximately 45 days after the exploit, and most funds were clawed back.

name: Ankr Bridge
description: On November 9, 2026, an attacker exploited Ankr's cross-chain bridge on Ethereum by submitting five forged withdrawal receipts referencing a single Optimism deposit that had already been redeemed. The attacker modified the recipients, assets, and withdrawal amounts, while presenting valid signatures from the bridge's trusted consensus signer. The bridge accepted the falsified receipts and released approximately $304,500 in assets, including ankrETH, ankrPOL, ANKR, and other staking tokens. The origin of the unauthorized signatures remains under investigation

name: Kalax
description: On October 14, 2024, Kalax founders executed a $350K rugpull by suddenly draining vaults, deleting the website and social accounts, and abandoning the protocol.

name: Rodeo
description: Rodeo Finance suffered first exploit on July 5, 2023 via a logic flaw in the mintProtocolReserves function, losing ~$89K. A second exploit on July 11 via TWAP oracle manipulation resulted in an additional $1.53M loss (810+ ETH). Stolen funds bridged to Ethereum then partially mixed via Tornado Cash.

name: Crypto-com
description: Crypto.com's 2FA system vulnerability allowed attackers to bypass authentication and withdraw $33.7M (4,836 ETH + 444 BTC + $66.2K USD) from 483 user accounts without entering 2FA codes.

name: Abracadabra Spell
description: Abracadabra.Money suffered a $13M exploit on March 25, 2025 via a flash loan attack on cauldrons accepting GMX V2 LP tokens as collateral. The attacker manipulated liquidation logic to self-liquidate and extract liquidation incentives.

name: Bitcurex
description: On October 13, 2016, Poland's largest Bitcoin exchange Bitcurex shut down after losing 2,300 BTC (~$1.5M) to attackers. The platform cited 'external interference in automated data collection' but later investigation revealed security compromises. The exchange attempted to restart but permanently closed weeks later.

name: Garden
description: On July 26, 2026, Garden Finance lost $450K across Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and BSC when an attacker breached an independent solver's off-chain database and inserted fraudulent transaction records to trigger unauthorized HTLC fund releases.

name: Citizen Finance
description: On July 12, 2022, Citizen Finance suffered an attack where an unauthorized party obtained access to private keys for BNB and Polygon chains. The attacker transferred 244 BNB (~$55K), 57,637 MATIC (~$32.3K), and 7,000 USDC for a total of ~$94.3K, causing the CIFI token to plummet over 50%.

name: OcelotDex
description: Shezmu's vault contract vulnerability allowed unauthorized minting of ShezUSD stablecoin without collateral, bypassing required checks and enabling attackers to mint unlimited ShezUSD and borrow assets to drain $4.9M. After negotiation, 80% was recovered.

name: DragonEx
description: Lazarus Group compromised DragonEx infrastructure through phishing attacks using a fake Worldbit-bot trading software, obtaining private keys and API access to drain 20 cryptocurrency wallets including 135 BTC, 2,738 ETH, and other assets.

name: Abracadabra Spell
description: Abracadabra's MIM stablecoin exploited for $6.5M via precision loss in collateral calculations. An attacker used rounding errors to bypass collateral validation, inflating borrow amounts. Funded with 1 ETH from Tornado Cash, the attack caused MIM to depeg to $0.76.

name: ZB Exchange
description: ZB Exchange's hot wallet was compromised, resulting in the theft of multiple cryptocurrencies including USDT and others. The attacker converted stolen tokens to approximately 2,224 ETH on decentralized exchanges.

name: Zilliqa X-Bridge
description: Zilliqa confirmed a security incident affecting its X-Bridge and ZRC2 proxy contracts associated with certain liquidity pools, including PlunderSwap. The affected assets include zUSDT, SEED, kUSD, and Zoge, while native ZIL and the Zilliqa EVM network reportedly remain unaffected. X-Bridge remains paused while operational keys are rotated and investigations continue

name: Vulcan Forged
description: On December 13, 2021, Vulcan Forged's NFT marketplace suffered a $140M hack affecting 96 high-value wallets when Venly's semi-custodial servers were compromised. The attacker extracted credentials and exfiltrated ~4.5M PYR tokens from customer wallets. Vulcan Forged refunded 100% of losses within 24 hours.

name: Kame Aggregator
description: On September 13, 2025 Kame Aggregator on the Sei network was exploited due to missing validation in the swap() function that allowed arbitrary executor calls, affecting 830 users who had granted unlimited token spend permissions to Kame contracts and draining approximately $1.325 million in total value.

name: Zunami Protocol
description: On May 15, 2025, Zunami Protocol's stablecoin collateral (zunUSD and zunETH) was drained for $500K via the god-mode withdrawStuckToken() function using a compromised admin key. The exploit occurred 7 minutes after the admin role was granted on May 14, suggesting key theft. Stolen funds were laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: SpiritSwap V3
description: Attacker socially engineered a GoDaddy employee to hijack SpiritSwap's domain, then deployed a phishing site with modified swap parameters. Before detection and shutdown on May 14, ~$18K was extracted (from 252 BNB total redirected).

name: LABUBU Token
description: LABUBU token's transfer function allowed the same address to be both sender and receiver, enabling balance inflation. The attacker borrowed tokens via a PancakeSwap V3 flash loan, repeatedly executed this flawed transfer to compound their balance, then swapped through multiple chains and mixed the proceeds.

name: Polygon
description: White-hat hackers discovered a critical vulnerability in Polygon's PoS genesis contract MRC20 token where the transfer function lacked balance/allowance checks. This would have allowed stealing ~9.3 billion MATIC tokens. Before the fix was deployed, threat actor stole 801,601 MATIC tokens. White hat received $2.2M bug bounty for the disclosure.

name: MetaSea
description: MetaSea's redeemPosition function overpaid SEA yield from a shared distributor without blocking just-in-time openings and redemptions in the same block. An attacker used Aave flash loans to atomically deposit USDT into the settlement adapter, redeem disproportionately large SEA amounts (17-27M vs 1.2M input), and sell the SEA back for USDT. Running 8 identical attacks back-to-back, the attacker extracted $110K aggregate across multiple blocks.

name: OKX NFT Aggregator
description: OKX's NFT aggregator on BSC was exploited on June 20, 2024 due to an access control vulnerability in withdrawal/transfer functions that had existed for approximately one year. $14K in user funds were stolen.

name: Drift Trade
description: On May 11, 2022, Drift Protocol on Solana experienced three interconnected bugs: users could withdraw positive PnL without realizing losses, leverage increased with long-short imbalance, and insurance funds weren't isolated per market. LUNA collapse exposed these issues, causing $8.72M net withdrawal and $14.5M shortfall.

name: Libertify
description: A reentrancy vulnerability in LibertiVault's deposit function allowed attackers to mint excess shares by re-entering before totalSupply was updated. The attacker used flash loans to deposit funds, called deposit() recursively, and claimed inflated rewards before the state was finalized.

name: Voltage V3
description: An attacker compromised the SimpleChefStaking proxy contract, replacing its implementation with a malicious one. The attacker then used the forceWithdraw function to drain collateral from the Simple Staking pools, extracting USDCE and WETH. Voltage offered a $50k bounty for recovery of the remaining funds.

name: Lever
description: Attacker exploited Lever's liability calculation to execute a flash loan attack using two malicious contracts. Contract A borrowed 2,100 BNB and deposited 2,000 into Lever's vault for interest-bearing tokens, then borrowed 1,500 BNB. Contract B received the collateral without Lever verifying that the xWBNB wasn't already used as collateral, allowing repayment with uncollateralized borrowed funds.

name: TeleSwap
description: TeleSwap's Bitcoin hot wallet was compromised, resulting in suspicious outflows of over $735K. The wallet ceased processing transactions shortly after discovery, with stolen funds subsequently moved toward Tornado Cash mixer.

name: LOOPSDAO
description: On August 2, 2026, LpdFi (LOOPSDAO's lending product on BNB Chain) was drained of ~$690K when an attacker flash-borrowed USDC and manipulated the PancakeSwap LPD/USDC pair price via donate-and-sync. The inflated price was used to compute interest owed, which the protocol paid by burning its own LP position and forwarding 99% of the USDC proceeds to the attacker.

name: ZKsync
description: ZKsync airdrop contracts were compromised on April 15, 2025 when attacker obtained admin private key with inadequate key management. Attacker minted 111M ZK tokens ($5M) via sweepUnclaimed() function; core protocol and user funds remained unaffected.

name: Galxe
description: An attacker impersonated a Galxe team member and contacted Dynadot, the domain registrar, with forged documentation to gain access to the Galxe.com domain account. The attacker redirected the domain to a phishing site and induced approximately 1,120 users to sign transactions to malicious contracts, resulting in $270K in losses before the domain was recovered.

name: Bond Protocol
description: On October 21, 2022, attacker deployed counterfeit bond tokens on Bond Protocol's OlympusDAO market and redeemed them for legitimate OHM collateral, draining $300K before returning funds hours later. Fixed-Expiry Teller lacked token validation.

name: THORChain DEX
description: On July 16, 2021, an attacker exploited an override function in THORChain's Bifrost bridge, wrapping the router contract to repeatedly extract value from liquidity pools by manipulating reported deposit amounts, draining approximately $4.9-7.4 million.

name: Zoth ZeUSD
description: Zoth's collateral accounting incorrectly calculated LTV (Loan-To-Value) after swapping collateral via Uniswap V3. An attacker used flash loans to manipulate V3 exchange rates, making a minimal deposit swap for far fewer tokens than should be received, then minting ZeUSD against the phantom collateral difference.

name: TheStandard.io
description: TheStandard.io was exploited when an attacker initiated a CDP with 10 WBTC collateral to mint 290K EUROs, then forced a manipulated swap in the WBTC/PAXG pool. Lack of slippage protection (amountOutMinimum = 0) combined with low liquidity enabled the attack.

name: ApeRocket
description: On July 14, 2021 ApeRocket (DeFi yield farming aggregator) suffered two coordinated flashloan attacks on BSC and Polygon within hours when attackers borrowed massive amounts of AAVE and CAKE (representing >99% of vault holdings), deposited them to inflate share counts, and dumped minted SPACE tokens for profit, causing SPACE to crash 63% because reward calculation lacked flashloan protection.

name: Samudai
description: Samudai's multisignature wallets and founder's personal wallet were compromised, draining 1.25M USD in ETH. The attacker moved funds through Tornado Cash mixer to obfuscate the theft.

name: Sirio Finance
description: Sirio Finance, the first lending protocol on Hedera, exploited for $2M on February 1, 2025 via flashloan attack. Specific technical details of the vulnerability are not publicly available.

name: Miner
description: A double-transfer vulnerability in the Miner ERC-X token allowed attackers to bypass validation on destination addresses. The lack of input validation enabled transfers of 168.8 ETH from the project.

name: Mirror
description: Mirror Protocol was exploited starting October 8, 2021, via inadequate access control on collateral unlock functions, allowing attackers to withdraw ~$90M over 7 months before discovery in May 2022. A follow-up $2M exploit in May 2022 exploited oracle misalignment during the LUNC-LUNA2 transition.

name: Roll
description: On March 14, 2021, an attacker obtained Roll's hot wallet private key and stole approximately $5.7 million in social tokens (WHALE, RARE, PICA), selling them on Uniswap and laundering proceeds through Tornado Cash.

name: ONTR
description: When ONTR's creator renounced ownership to signal trustworthiness, the onlyOwner modifier contained a flawed require statement that treated owner == address(0) as permission rather than denial. This turned the ownership renunciation into a backdoor, allowing anyone to reclaim ownership and drain the contract of $98.2K in funds within minutes.

name: Balancer V1
description: An attacker exploited a previously disclosed pricing vulnerability in deprecated Balancer V1 pools, extracting approximately $250,000. The attack was financed through flash loans and temporary collateral positions across three Aave V3 lending markets

name: Unistreets
description: On August 5, 2026, Unistreets on Ethereum was exploited via an arbitrary external call vulnerability, resulting in a loss of approximately $17,750. The exploiter address and transaction were identified on-chain.

name: BlackHole Token
description: BlackHole Token on BSC was exploited when an attacker used a flash loan to manipulate liquidity pool prices. The attacker swapped 22 million USDT through the trading pair to artificially inflate the token price before draining funds from the protocol.

name: Hope Finance
description: On February 20, 2023, Hope Finance (Arbitrum stablecoin protocol) was exploited by an insider who modified the TradingHelper contract to redirect GenesisRewardPool funds to an attacker address. ~$2M was stolen; ~$1.86M was laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: Picostocks
description: Picostocks lost 5,896 BTC from both hot and cold wallets. Because the offline cold storage was somehow accessed, the theft was suspected to be an inside job or the result of compromised key storage, suggesting an internal actor or breach of key management.

name: HTX
description: On November 22, 2023, Huobi HTX suffered a breach of three hot wallets when an attacker gained access to private keys stored on exchange servers. User assets and reserves were converted to Ether and transferred out, with initial hot wallet losses of $13.6M and additional impact from related HECO Chain bridge losses.

name: Predict Fun
description: Several Predict.fun users experienced unauthorized wallet transfers totaling approximately 400,000 USDT. Preliminary findings suggest a possible compromise of the project’s API documentation website, which was hosted by a third-party provider. Predict.fun took the documentation site offline as a precaution and committed to reimbursing affected users

name: ShadowFi
description: ShadowFi's SDF token contract had flaws allowing unauthorized token burning. Attackers exploited the access control vulnerability in a two-phase attack to burn all SDF tokens in the liquidity pool and drain liquidity.

name: Trust Wallet Wallet
description: The Shai-Hulud npm worm compromised developer accounts and harvested Trust Wallet's Chrome Web Store API key. On December 24, 2025, the attacker published a malicious Trust Wallet Browser Extension v2.68 to the Chrome Web Store, exfiltrating private keys from users until December 26 at 11:00 UTC.

name: Warp Protocol
