description: On December 17-18, 2020, an attacker exploited Warp Finance's gameable oracle by flash loaning 2.9M DAI and 344.8K WETH from dYdX to manipulate DAI/Uniswap prices, inflating LP collateral value to borrow 3.86M DAI and 3.9M USDC, draining $7.76 million total.

name: Fox Market
description: On August 15, 2026 Fox Market was exploited through its FoxLpBondsPool.stake() bond minting path. The contract read the FOX spot price from the PancakeSwap V2 FOX/USDT pool before allowing the same transaction to move that pool. The attacker used flash liquidity to buy almost all FOX from the pool, while the mint calculation continued using the pre-swap price snapshot, resulting in approximately 88.66M sFOX and 91.3M FOX of reported issuance. The attacker then sold an immediately unlocked ~2.66M FOX referral allocation into the USDT-heavy pool, repaid the flash liquidity, and retained approximately $120K in realized profit

name: Harmony Bridge
description: Harmony's Horizon Bridge was hacked on June 23, 2022, stealing ~$100M across ETH, BNB, USDT, USDC, and DAI on Ethereum and BSC. Lazarus Group / APT38 (North Korea-affiliated) compromised validator private keys; the insufficient 2-of-5 validator quorum enabled the theft.

name: Hyperliquid
description: In June 2023, an attacker manipulated SNX prices on centralized exchanges to exploit Hyperliquid's vault system through its reliance on easily-manipulated CEX spot prices, leveraging the discrepancy between real and inflated prices.

name: BetterBank
description: On August 26-27, 2025, BetterBank on PulseChain was exploited via its reward mechanism using flash loans to manipulate liquidity pools, create a fake ERC20 paired with PDAIF, and trigger ESTEEM minting. ~$5M was stolen; the attacker later returned $2.7M, leaving net losses of ~$1.4M. The issue had been flagged during audit but dismissed.

name: AES
description: AES, a deflationary token on BSC, was exploited through abuse of its skim function. The attacker repeatedly sent AES tokens to the AES-USDT pair to break the pool balance, then called skim to extract surplus tokens. Each cycle burned additional AES tokens, allowing profitable conversion of small token amounts into large USDT payouts.

name: flash.sx / vaults.sx
description: A reentrancy vulnerability in vaults.sx's flashloan contract allowed an attacker to recursively extract 1.18M EOS and 462K USDT. The attacker distributed funds across 246 accounts attempting to evade recovery. EOS BPs froze accounts by supermajority consensus and the attacker was social-engineered into nulling their keys; all users were made whole.

name: BoostHook
description: BoostHook was exploited via a flash loan attack that manipulated the ETH/PERP Uniswap v4 pool price. An attacker used a 120 WETH Morpho flash loan to temporarily push the pool price upward, opened nine leveraged long positions at the inflated price through BoostHook.openLong(), then reversed the price move. The protocol's hard-capped MAX_LIQS_PER_BLOCK limit prevented liquidation of all toxic positions, leaving four 8 ETH-debt positions open and causing significant bad debt.

name: Raft
description: On November 10, 2023, an attacker exploited a precision error in Raft's divUp function during share token minting to mint ~$6.7M unbacked R tokens via a 6000 cbETH flash loan from Aave, causing a ~$3.3M net loss.

name: Aztec Connect
description: Aztec Connect's proof verification failed to match L1 state updates, letting attacker submit unvalidated transactions crediting themselves with value. They withdrew $2.1M in ETH, DAI, wstETH and other tokens.

name: Palmswap
description: On July 24, 2023, Palmswap's PLP vault was exploited for $901,000. The attacker used flashloans to purchase USDP at 1:1, inflated the pool value, then redeemed at the manipulated 1:1.9 rate by exploiting incorrect exchange rate calculations in PlpManager.

name: VinDAX
description: VinDAX, a Vietnamese exchange launched in March 2019, was hacked on November 5, 2019, with attackers stealing $500K in digital assets across 23 small-cap cryptocurrencies from insecure hot wallets. After discovery, VinDAX immediately contacted the projects involved and froze or recovered the stolen tokens due to the small-cap nature of the assets. The platform later fully recovered the stolen value through coordination with affected projects.

name: Coinsecure
description: In April 2018, Coinsecure's chief security officer Dr. Amitabh Saxena exposed the exchange's private keys while attempting to distribute Bitcoin Gold to customers. The keys were exposed online for over 12 hours, allowing attackers to steal 438 BTC (~$3.3M). Saxena was arrested as a prime suspect.

name: Earning.Farm
description: On August 9, 2023 Earning.Farm (yield farming platform on Ethereum) was exploited for approximately $528,000-$540,000 via a reentrancy vulnerability in the withdraw() function where flawed share-burning logic allowed the attacker to reenter the contract and drain additional funds.

name: LocalBitcoins
description: A third-party discussion forum platform running on LocalBitcoins was compromised and used to phish user credentials including 2FA codes. Attackers gained access to six user accounts and transferred 7.9 BTC before the forum was disabled.

name: SteamSwap
description: SteamSwap (STM) on BNB Chain was attacked via price manipulation allowing the attacker to abuse reserve balance calculations and drain approximately $105K from the DEX.

name: Defrost
description: On December 24, 2022, Defrost Finance on Avalanche suffered two coordinated attacks: V2 flashloan drained $173K via LSWUSDC price manipulation; V1 admin key compromise allowed minting 100M H20 and draining ~$12M USDT via fake oracle. All funds were later returned.

name: Bilaxy
description: On August 28-29, 2021, cryptocurrency exchange Bilaxy's hot wallet was compromised, resulting in the theft of approximately $21.7 million in various ERC20 tokens including USDT, USDC, and UNI. The attacker transferred 200 ETH to Tornado Cash to mix the stolen funds.

name: WazirX: India
description: WazirX Indian exchange was hacked on July 18, 2024, losing $234.9M in 190+ tokens from a Liminal-custodied multisig wallet. Attackers created a fake WazirX account, accessed the hot wallet, then exploited the smart contract controlling the multisig to gain full control without the original keys.

name: Superfluid
description: On February 8, 2022 Superfluid (money streaming protocol on Polygon) suffered an exploit of approximately $8.7 million via a vulnerability in the CTX (context) validation mechanism where the attacker injected a forged context containing an arbitrary sender address, allowing agreement contracts to execute transfers on behalf of other accounts.

name: LeetSwap
description: LeetSwap on Base lost ~$624K (~342 ETH) on August 1, 2023 when an attacker exploited the _transferFeesSupportingTaxTokens function lacking access controls to move LP fees and manipulate pool prices.

name: RPP
description: On November 5, 2024, RPP protocol on BNB Chain was exploited through a logic flaw, resulting in approximately $14.1K in losses.

name: Vether
description: An attacker paid a 128 Vether exclusion fee and exploited an access control flaw in the V3 contract to gain control of all remaining Vether. They claimed 900,000 Vether and liquidated 150,000 on Uniswap for approximately 15 ETH.

name: EGD Finance
description: EGD Finance's reward calculation directly relied on token price without flash loan protection. Attackers used a flashloan to manipulate the USDT/EGD ratio in the PancakeSwap pool, artificially inflating EGD price and claiming excessive rewards.

name: SynapLogic
description: A business logic flaw in SynapLogic's referral system allowed attackers to mint 144k SYP tokens without proper validation. The exploit involved 193 suspicious transactions where attackers repeatedly called the referral function with flashloan-backed ETH, receiving 10% referral rewards for each fraudulent transaction.

name: Bybit
description: On February 21, 2025, Lazarus Group phished Bybit's DevOps engineer and spoofed the Safe UI to trick signers into blind-signing a masked transaction that deployed a rogue hot-wallet policy. This drained approximately $1.4-1.5 billion in ETH and assets.

name: The Internet Token
description: The Internet Token’s privileged LiquidityUnifier contract had INT minting authority and exposed a permissionless swapV3(token, pool) function accepting a caller-supplied pool. Its validation only required the supplied address to contain code, not be excluded, and report INT and the requested token through token0()/token1(). The attacker supplied a malicious fake pool satisfying these checks. swapV3() stored that address as currentPoolV3 and called its swap(), allowing the fake pool to invoke uniswapV3SwapCallback() with an attacker-selected amount. Because the callback trusted currentPoolV3, it caused the privileged contract to mint INT to the fake pool. The attacker bypassed the surrounding supply-increase check by converting the newly minted INT through the project’s Convertor during the call, reducing supply before the check, and converting it back afterward. Approximately 161.3M counterfeit INT was then sold into the genuine INT/WETH pool for 5.85 WETH

name: CrediX
description: On August 4, 2025, CrediX on Sonic suffered $4.5M loss when attacker gained admin access via ACLManager, minting unbacked acUSDC and draining pools. Funds were moved to Ethereum via Tornado Cash. The team vanished August 8.

name: TronCrush
description: TronCrush's transfer function did not validate that the 'to' and 'from' addresses must be different, allowing an attacker to create tokens without foundation through self-transfers. Over 20 smart contracts and dapps were vulnerable to this same pattern.

name: Nomic
description: A vulnerability in Nomic’s custom forwarding mechanism allowed an attacker to double-spend nBTC and generate false cross-chain vouchers that were sent to Osmosis. These vouchers resulted in unbacked nBTC entering Osmosis and becoming part of Alloyed BTC’s backing. Osmosis and IBC were not compromised. After detecting the issue, Osmosis froze Nomic and Alloyed BTC inflows and outflows and coordinated an emergency upgrade with validators that froze 22.65 BTC in the attacker’s address

name: Florence Finance
description: On November 30, 2023, user sent 1,456,162 USDC to poisoned address 0xB087... instead of Florence Finance's legitimate address. Attackers had seeded the user's address book with lookalike addresses; victim relied on autofill. Funds were bridged to Ethereum and swapped for ETH.

name: WiseLending
description: WiseLending was exploited through a flash loan attack that leveraged rounding errors in the _calculateShares function. The attacker used strategic deposits and withdrawals to artificially inflate share prices, with a white-hat MEV bot front-running the exploit to recover funds.

name: Rubic
description: On November 2, 2022, an attacker compromised an administrator's private key for Rubic's bridge, which controlled the RBC/BRBC bridge and staking rewards. The attacker stole approximately 34M RBC tokens and sold them on Uniswap and PancakeSwap, with realized losses estimated at ~$1.2M. The token price collapsed 98% following the mass liquidation.

name: AM
description: AM token's deferred burn mechanism was exploited where accumulated toBurnAmount caused unbounded burns on the next sell transaction. Flash loan-funded attackers inflated pair USDT reserves before triggering the deferred burn to sell at exaggerated effective prices.

name: DefiTuna Lending
description: DefiTuna Lending on Solana exploited for $580K on July 16, 2026. Attackers created a highly illiquid TUNA/USDC pool and routed borrowed USDC through it. The negligible swap output caused position value to round to zero, bypassing the solvency check.

name: QANplatform
description: QANplatform's bridge deployer wallet was compromised on October 11, 2022 due to the profanity vulnerability in the vanity address generator. The attacker recovered the private key and drained ~$2M from the Ethereum and BNB cross-chain bridges in multiple withdrawals.

name: QuickSwap Market
description: On October 24, 2022, QuickSwap's Market XYZ lending market on Polygon was exploited for $220K via a read-only reentrancy vulnerability in the Curve LP Oracle. An attacker used a flash loan to manipulate spot prices, inflating collateral values to drain assets from the market. The exploit affected LDO, MATIC, and staked MATIC tokens, leading QuickSwap to shut down its lending service.

name: Zentra Finance
description: Zentra’s Aave V3-based lending implementation contained a boundary-condition accounting flaw in repayWithATokens. The attacker borrowed assets and requested repayment of the outstanding debt plus exactly one base unit. The debt-token path’s ceil-rounding cleared the debt in full, while the aToken burn path’s rounding safeguard reduced the required burn to the caller’s available aToken balance. Because the attacker held no corresponding aTokens, the burn was reduced to zero. The Pool therefore recorded the debt as repaid without receiving equivalent value, allowing the attacker to withdraw the original flash-funded collateral while retaining the borrowed reserve assets. The sequence was repeated against ctUSD and USDC.e

name: AirDAO
description: AirDAO partner compromised via malicious email attachment carrying malware. Attackers gained access to liquidity pool keys and drained AMB tokens and ETH from Uniswap LP, netting approximately 125.51 ETH at realized prices.

name: SudoRare
description: SudoRare NFT AMM platform operated for 6 hours before founders used admin privileges to drain 519 ETH ($800K) from the liquidity pool and disappeared.

name: ShapeShift FOX Colony
description: An attacker exploited the EtherRouterCreate3 contract's meta-transaction mechanism by abusing the arbitrary self-call capability combined with DSAuth's automatic authorization logic for address(this). The attacker bypassed the auth modifier, replaced the contract's core routing component (resolver) with a malicious version, then used delegatecall to drain all ERC20 assets. A second related exploit shortly after brought total losses to $182.7K.

name: OPSEC
description: A private key controlling the OPSEC staking contract was compromised, allowing the attacker to change ownership from the team wallet to attacker-controlled addresses. Although $800K in tokens were accessible, the attacker was only able to convert ~59 ETH (~$100K at time of sale) to cash due to illiquid pool conditions.

name: Triple-A
description: On July 24-25, 2026, Triple-A's hot wallets were drained across 7 blockchains (TRON, Ethereum, Arbitrum, TON, Solana). The initial $9.7M loss was revised to $11.8M as attackers maintained access for 31+ hours.

name: Yearn Finance
description: On April 13, 2023, Yearn Finance's yUSDT vault was exploited through a misconfigured oracle reference pointing to Fulcrum's USDC contract instead of USDT. Attacker exploited the incorrect contract pointer to manipulate share prices, minting 1.2 quadrillion yUSDT by depositing only 10,000 USDT, then selling for $11.54 million.

name: NEKO
description: On August 13, 2021, Neko Network's MainPool smart contract was exploited via an improper access control vulnerability. The attacker exploited a mismatch between the account being mortgaged for a loan (onBehalfOf) and the account receiving borrowed funds, allowing them to mortgage other users' assets while receiving funds to their own address, stealing over $2.2M in stablecoins.

name: Agave
description: On Gnosis Chain, attackers exploited xDAI's non-standard _callAfterTransfer() callback reentrancy; using flashloans to stack borrows before balance updates, they withdrew amounts far exceeding collateral value.

name: FriesDAO
description: On October 28, 2022, FriesDAO's deployer wallet generated using the Profanity vanity-address tool was compromised, allowing an attacker to calculate the private key and steal approximately $2.3M in FRIES governance tokens and other assets from the staking pool. Profanity had a known critical flaw enabling private key derivation for vanity addresses.

name: Across
description: Between 05:07 and 06:14 UTC on 17 July 2026 an attacker submitted 1,627 forged Solana deposits (face value ~$41.7M) from single-use wallets across 18 destination chains; Risk Labs' relayer filled 581 of them, paying out roughly $4.5M of its own capital before Solana was disabled as an origin chain. No user funds were affected.

name: Asterix
description: Asterix exploited June 9, 2026 for ~$40K, replicating the same DN404 vulnerability that hit Flooring Protocol the day before. The vulnerability stems from DN404's inherent design flaw in interlinked ERC20/ERC721 mechanics. Downstream forks inherited this flaw without re-auditing.

name: Coinbin
description: Coinbin's former CEO (previously from acquired exchange Youbit) used his new position to steal over 100 ETH from an Ethereum wallet, claiming the key had been lost. The employee embezzlement forced the exchange into bankruptcy.

name: ChainSwap
description: On July 2, 2021, ChainSwap, an Ethereum-BSC bridge protocol, was exploited via a bridge logic flaw where attackers bypassed signature verification by exploiting incorrect authQuotaOf implementation, allowing them to mint tokens across multiple protocols using the bridge and steal approximately $800K.

name: WonderHero
description: WonderHero's hot wallet private keys were compromised, likely via phishing targeting the seed phrase, resulting in theft of approximately $320,000 in BNB.

name: Bonzo Lend
description: On July 11, 2026 at 00:51 UTC, an attacker deposited 250 SAUCE tokens (~$5 worth) as collateral on Bonzo Lend on Hedera. Attacker pushed a fabricated SAUCE price into Supra's oracle inflated by ~12 orders of magnitude, then borrowed 6.63M USDC and 34.5M WHBAR. Bonzo's TVL fell 77%; Hedera's network TVL dropped 40% within 24 hours.

name: Raydium AMM
description: On December 16, 2022, Raydium AMM private keys were compromised by trojan malware; attacker gained admin access and modified SyncNeedTake pool parameters to extract $4.4M without burning LP tokens. Raydium patched within 4 hours and recovered governance.

name: ValueDefi
description: ValueDefi's vSwap pool on BSC was exploited via reinitialization vulnerability in access control. Attacker re-initialized pool, set themselves as operator, called governanceRecoverUnsupported() to drain 10,839.16 vBWAP/BUSD LP tokens and associated collateral.

name: Bitget
description: Bitget detected unauthorized transfers involving a limited number of hot wallets at 18:31 UTC on September 24. Subsequent tracing identified approximately $387.5M transferred to attacker-controlled addresses across Ethereum and other EVM networks, XRP Ledger, Zcash and Tron. Bitget states that the incident has been contained and no further unauthorized transfers are possible

name: SolvBTC
description: Solv Protocol BRO vaults were exploited on March 6, 2026 when ERC-3525 NFT deposit triggered callbacks that minted tokens before parent transaction completed, allowing double-minting. 135 BRO inflated to 567M tokens (~38 SolvBTC, ~$2.7M).

name: Projekt
description: Projekt reward vault attacked July 25, 2026 for $560K via flashloan exploit. Attacker flash-loaned 14K WETH from Morpho to create fake purchase records in the unvalidated trackPurchase function, inflating reward allocations and draining ~301.7 ETH via massWithdraw.

name: BRA
description: On January 10, 2023, the BRA token on BSC was exploited through a tax-sharing loophole in the transfer mechanism. The attacker exploited a logic flaw where if sender and recipient formed a pair, the transfer function would double rewards. This created 1.6 million additional BRA tokens that were sold for approximately 819 WBNB (~$225K).

name: Quant
description: A QNT reserve pool on Ethereum was drained of 1,988.5 QNT (~54.93 ETH, ~$138K) on 28 April 2026 via an EIP-7702 delegation chain: the pool's admin EOA delegated its code to a BatchExecutor which trusted an open, permissionless BatchCall helper; BatchCall.batch() had no caller check, allowing any address to execute arbitrary calls with admin authority.

name: Moonwell Lending
description: On November 4, 2025, Moonwell on Base and Optimism was exploited for $1 million when the Chainlink oracle incorrectly priced wrapped restaked Ethereum (wrstETH) at ~$5.8M instead of actual value, allowing a flash loan attack to repeatedly borrow against false collateral.

name: New Free DAO
description: New Free DAO was exploited via flash loans when the reward calculation relied solely on deposited balance without protection. The attacker repeatedly flash-loaned funds to claim disproportionate rewards and drain ~$1.25 million in WBNB.

name: Squid Games
description: SQUID token (November 1, 2021) was a honeypot that allowed buying but blocked most holder sells. Price rose to $2,800, but developers withdrew the ~$3.38M SQUID/BNB pool and abandoned the project, leaving 43,000+ buyers with unsellable tokens.

name: Permapod
description: Permapod confirmed that an exploit affected its smart contracts and subsequently secured the affected contracts and halted the protocol. The team has not yet disclosed the vulnerability, exploitation mechanism, affected markets, or amount lost

name: Nostra Money Market
description: An attacker manipulated the price of NSTR in an illiquid onchain market, causing the manipulated price to enter NSTR’s Pragma oracle response. The attacker then used NSTR at the inflated valuation as collateral in Nostra’s money market to borrow approximately $3.5M of other assets. Pragma says NSTR had limited liquidity and source coverage, the affected oracle response had only two contributing sources, and the manipulated input reflected an onchain pool price rather than a decimals or median-calculation error. Nostra paused its money market following the incident

name: Portal
description: On February 2, 2022, attackers exploited Wormhole Portal by using a deprecated insecure signature verification function to mint 120,000 wrapped ETH on Solana without locking equivalent collateral on Ethereum, then redeemed for real ETH.

name: BasketDAO
description: BasketDAO's BMIZapper contract lacked input validation in the _primitiveToBMI function, allowing arbitrary external calls. The attacker passed a malicious address to drain all approved crypto assets held by the contract.

name: NORMIE
description: NORMIE meme coin was exploited through a flash loan attack that manipulated the contract's tax logic. The attacker extracted 224.98 ETH by disabling taxes and triggering automatic token dumps. The exploiter offered 90% recovery.

name: mySwap CL
description: On June 19, 2026, at 7:15 AM UTC, mySwap's concentrated liquidity pools were exploited when an attacker created a fake EVIL token to manipulate pool accounting and share calculations. The attacker drained approximately $305K in liquidity (137.96 ETH, 45K USDC, 19.9K USDT, 230K STRK).

name: Texture
description: Texture's Solana lending protocol lost $2.2M to a vault access control vulnerability. Attacker returned $1.98M after being offered a 10% bounty.

name: HarryPotterObamaSonic10Inu
description: A liquidity pool attack on HarryPotterObamaSonic10Inu 2.0 token exploited price manipulation via the pool reserves. The attacker stole 84.7 ETH through manipulation of the pool's price function.

name: XSTABLE Protocol
description: XSTABLE Protocol suffered an exploit due to incorrect logic checks in its smart contract. The attack caused the XST token price to drop 98.4% and led to the protocol's website and social media channels being taken down.

name: Indexed Finance
description: On October 14, 2021, Indexed Finance's DEFI5 and CC10 pools were drained of $16M via a sophisticated flashloan attack. The attacker used massive flashloans to knock pool balances out of equilibrium, purchased component assets at heavily discounted rates, and executed the entire attack within a single transaction.

name: JB
description: JB token gateway contract on BNB Chain was drained of 49,958 USDT on June 18-19, 2026. Attacker flash-borrowed WBNB, borrowed 70M USDT from Venus as collateral, and exploited poolTransferToDeadAndSync/tradeRouterBurnPool/poolRewardTransfer functions that sync the PancakeSwap pair after each manipulation, allowing repeated arbitrage of skewed reserves until USDT released exceeded costs. Venus loan was repaid in the same transaction.

name: LiFi Finance
description: On July 16, 2024 LI.FI protocol was exploited via insufficient input validation in GasZipFacet.sol, where the depositToGasZipERC20 function allowed user-controlled _swapData parameters to reach low-level calls with malicious transferFrom() calldata, draining $8-11M from 153 wallets with infinite approvals across Ethereum and Arbitrum.

name: New Market Trading
description: On May 25, 2026, New Market Trading's SquidRouterModule was exploited across 88 user Gnosis Safes on Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum. The module validated permissions against caller-supplied delegate addresses instead of msg.sender, allowing attackers to route assets through attacker-controlled pools, stealing ~$3.98M.

name: Grim Finance
description: Grim Finance's GrimBoostVault lacked reentrancy guards. Attackers exploited this via nested calls during safeTransferFrom to accumulate false collateral through repeated deposits.

name: EtherDelta
description: Between December 19-26, 2017, EtherDelta suffered DNS hijacking attacks by Anthony Nashatka and Elliott Gunton. Users were redirected to a phishing site where credentials were captured. The attackers stole ~$600K from Dec 19-21 and an additional $800K from a single user on Dec 26, totaling ~$1.4M.

name: LeadBlock's Morpho Blue Market
description: Morpho Blue PAXG/USDC market October 13-14, 2024 misconfigured oracle SCALE_FACTOR to value gold at 10^12x. Attacker deposited $350 in PAXG and withdrew ~$250K via decimal mismatch (USDC 6 vs PAXG 18 decimals).

name: Exmo
description: EXMO detected suspicious withdrawal activity on December 21, with attackers stealing approximately 5% of the exchange's total assets from compromised hot wallets. Multiple cryptocurrencies including BTC, ETH, XRP, ETC, ZEC, and USDT were transferred out during a coordinated withdrawal.

name: Kinto Bridge
description: Kinto K token contract on Arbitrum was exploited on July 10, 2025 via hidden/uninitialized proxy implementation slot (CPIMP-class vulnerability), allowing attacker to mint ~110K counterfeit tokens and drain ~577 ETH from lending pools; K token lost ~95% value.

name: Smoofs
description: A reentrancy vulnerability in the Smoofs staking contract allowed attackers to drain funds through unsafe external calls that enabled state to be manipulated during transaction execution.

name: ACB
description: ACB token exploited through staking reward manipulation via spot price oracle manipulation on Binance Smart Chain. Attacker manipulated oracle prices to artificially inflate reward calculations.

name: Silo Finance
description: On June 25, 2025, Silo Finance lost $546,000 when an experimental leverage contract was mistakenly deployed to mainnet. Attacker exploited unchecked borrow() return values, using a malicious token (MalCoin) that reported constant balance=1 to drain ETH without repaying.

name: Rubic
description: Rubic lost $1.4M on December 25, 2022 when USDC was mistakenly added to the router whitelist and routerCallNative lacked input validation. Attacker exploited user pre-approvals to RubicProxy by calling arbitrary contracts, draining USDC directly from user wallets.

name: The Sandbox
description: The Sandbox’s SAND cross-chain bridge was exploited after an attacker abused approveAndCall on the Base SAND OFT contract to hijack LayerZero delegate permissions. The attacker changed trusted cross-chain configuration, minted unbacked SAND on Base and BNB Chain, and used the compromised bridge path to extract approximately 14.75M backed SAND from the Ethereum OFT adapter. The Sandbox disabled bridging on Base and BNB Chain and stated that SAND on Ethereum and Polygon was unaffected at the token-contract level

name: Hunny Finance
description: An incorrect calculation in the Hunny Minter contract allowed an attacker to execute a malicious contract 91 times, locking 1.1M in tokens via incorrect accounting logic. While the team disputed token theft, significant value was locked and dumped to markets.

name: EOS.WIN
description: EOS.WIN gambling DApp was exploited on November 12, 2018 via a randomness prediction attack. An attacker conducted 165 test transactions the day prior, then executed 10 successful attacks in one minute gaining 9,180 EOS. The attacker predicted the random number by controlling the ref block num parameter.

name: Atomic Wallet
description: On June 3, 2023, Atomic Wallet users lost over $100 million when attackers compromised the wallet application through a supply chain attack that injected malicious code to exfiltrate private keys. Approximately 5,500 wallets were affected across multiple chains.

name: Meerkat Finance
description: Meerkat Finance was drained one day after launch on March 4, 2021 when vaults containing $31M were compromised. The attacker exploited permissionless proxy initialization to gain admin control and drain funds, with the team later launching a 95%+ refund program.

name: Atlantis Loans
description: On June 7, attacker exploited weak governance controls to pass malicious proposal ID 52, gaining admin access to token proxy. Attacker modified ABep20Delegate with backdoor to extract funds from users with active token approvals.

name: AARK (Aark Digital)
description: On October 25, 2024, AARK (a perpetual DEX on Arbitrum) suffered a $1.9M exploit through a conversion-script decimal inflation vulnerability in its vault contracts. The protocol offered a 15% bounty for the return of stolen funds.

name: Gamdom
description: Gamdom suffered a multichain hot-wallet compromise following unauthorized access to an automation server. Investigators traced approximately $4.21M in stolen assets across eight networks. The attacker subsequently bridged, swapped, and distributed funds through multiple wallets and services, including Mayan, Hyperliquid, and THORChain. The precise mechanism used to obtain control of the wallets remains unconfirmed

name: Float Protocol
description: Float Protocol's pool on RariCapital was exploited through oracle manipulation of the FLOAT/USDC Uniswap V3 pool. Insufficient liquidity in the pool allowed an attacker to create a fake position marking FLOAT at trillions of USDC per token. The exploited Uniswap V3 oracle reported this manipulated price, allowing the attacker to use FLOAT as infinite collateral to borrow all available assets.

name: Dexmax AI
description: Attackers exploited the DMT token airdrop claiming process by tricking users into signing additional authorization transactions. After users claimed the airdrop, attackers triggered secondary signatures to approve asset transfers. Thieves stole from thousands of users and cross-chain bridged over $130K in assets to Ethereum, with most funds flowing through HitBTC.

name: Mercado Bitcoin
description: On November 2, 2026, attackers compromised a system at Mercado Bitcoin and transferred more than $40 million in crypto from exchange-associated wallets across various blockchains. The exchange contained the incident and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while investigating the transfers. Tether froze more than $4.5 million USDT associated with the theft. Mercado Bitcoin stated that customers would not incur losses and that no customer data was exposed

name: dTRINITY
description: The dTRINITY swap adapter suffered a missing authorization check in its swapLiquidity() function. The attacker called the swap function using addresses of victims who had previously approved the adapter during testing. Malicious swap routes sent collateral deposits directly to attacker-controlled addresses while returning minimal amounts to pass validation, draining $56K.

name: Audius
description: On July 23-25, 2022, Audius governance contracts were compromised when an attacker exploited a missing initialization guard allowing repeated invoke() calls. The attacker drained 18 million AUDIO tokens (~$6M) from the treasury and attempted to delegate 10 trillion tokens to controlled wallets.

name: zkLink Nova
description: An attacker exploited zkLink’s Arbitrator contract, which failed to clear a previously authenticated message hash after processing a claim. By reusing that hash through the publicly accessible SyncL2TxHashRelayer, the attacker impersonated an authorized gateway message and installed a malicious L2 logs root. The attacker then submitted forged withdrawal proofs against the compromised root to drain approximately $783,100 from zkLink’s Ethereum bridge

name: Port3 Network
description: Port3 Network's CATERC20 bridge from NEXA was exploited on November 22, 2025, via missing signature verification on mint function and unset owner address, allowing attacker to mint 1 billion PORT3 tokens.

name: XCarnival
description: On June 26, 2022, XCarnival NFT lending protocol was exploited via a vulnerability in collateral tracking where the orderID remained open after withdrawal. The attacker generated multiple contract addresses, used the same BAYC NFT as collateral, and repeated the deposit-borrow-withdraw cycle to obtain an infinite number of loans, siphoning 3,087 ETH (~$3.8M).

name: Magpie Protocol
description: On April 23, 2024, Magpie Protocol's MagpieRouterV2 was exploited for $129K affecting 221 wallets. The router validated selector presence but not position, allowing attackers to embed selectors in call data to bypass access controls.

name: Giddy
description: On April 23, 2026, GiddyVaultV3 on Ethereum was exploited for $1.3M via incomplete EIP-712 signature coverage. Unvalidated parameters (aggregator, fromToken, toToken, amount) in SwapInfo structure allowed attackers to manipulate transaction approvals.

name: MAP Protocol
description: On May 20, 2026 MAP Protocol's Butter Bridge suffered a critical exploit enabling attackers to mint 1 quadrillion MAPO tokens via a collision in the bridge's retry message verification using keccak256(abi.encodePacked). The attacker triggered unauthorized minting on Ethereum and BSC, extracting approximately 52.2 ETH (~$110,000) in value before the MAPO token crashed 96%.

name: BGLD
description: BGLD, a deflationary token on BSC, was exploited through a flash loan price manipulation attack. The attacker used a flash loan to artificially inflate the token price, enabling a profitable swap on PancakeSwap.

name: Hedgey
description: Hedgey Finance drained for $44.7M (USDC, NOBL, MASA, BONUS) from Arbitrum and Ethereum vaults. Attacker exploited missing validation in createLockedCampaign, using flashloans to bypass access controls and create fraudulent approvals.

name: MonaCoin
description: Between May 13-15, 2018, MonaCoin suffered a selfish mining attack where the attacker commanded up to 57% of hashrate. By mining blocks secretly and releasing them strategically, the attacker invalidated legitimate blocks and stole approximately $90K in MONA coins through exchange manipulation.

name: LW Token
description: An attacker exploited the LW token on BSC using a flashloan-based price manipulation attack. The marketAddr account held 173,272 USDT which was used to artificially manipulate the LW price on the PancakeSwap LW-BUSD pair, enabling the attacker to extract approximately 48,415 USDT through price distortion. The LW token price collapsed 69% following the exploit.

name: BTER
description: BTER's servers were compromised and 50 million NXT tokens (valued at ~$1.65M) were stolen from the exchange's hot wallets. The exchange suspended operations and implemented security partnerships to prevent further losses.

name: Level Perps
description: Level Finance on BSC lost $1.1M in May 2023 when attackers exploited missing epoch reuse prevention in the referral claims contract. Flashloans inflated reward tiers, allowing multiple claims per epoch via the unprotected claimMultiple() function.

name: Ankr
description: A vulnerability in Ankr’s ankrFLOW liquid-staking contract allowed an attacker to create approximately 8.6M unbacked ankrFLOW. The attacker supplied the unbacked tokens as collateral on MORE Markets and borrowed approximately 15.5M WFLOW from its lending reserve. MORE Markets’ contracts operated as designed; Flow identified the originating vulnerability as Ankr’s ankrFLOW contract

name: EXcommunity
description: EXcommunity was attacked through an undisclosed smart contract vulnerability, resulting in $37,000 in losses. The project team continued operations and announced plans for enhanced security measures.

name: Wise Lending V1
description: On January 12, 2024, Wise Lending was drained of $464K via a flashloan that exploited precision loss in _calculateShares() (division before multiplication), allowing accumulation of excess shares to withdraw more than deposited.

name: TronBank
description: TronBank's invest() function did not validate that msg.tokenId was the legitimate BTT token, allowing attackers to use counterfeit tokens and artificially inflate their BTT balance. Nearly 200M counterfeit BTTs were minted.

name: PancakeSwap / Cream Finance
description: Both Cream Finance and PancakeSwap had their GoDaddy-hosted DNS records hijacked simultaneously. Attackers redirected users to phishing sites requesting seed phrases and private keys. Both teams regained DNS control within hours on March 15, 2021 (by 17:30 UTC for PancakeSwap).

name: Coincheck
description: On January 26, 2018, Coincheck announced hackers stole 523 million NEM coins from its internet-connected hot wallet, which lacked adequate security controls. The exchange began reimbursing approximately 260,000 affected users.

name: Evoq Finance
description: On BNB Chain, Evoq Finance's smart contract was compromised when an attacker stole the owner's private key. The attacker transferred contract ownership, deployed a malicious upgrade, and drained approximately $420K from the protocol and user-approved token accounts.

name: XDX Swap
description: On July 2, 2021, XDX Swap on the HECO chain was exploited via a suspected backdoor in the cross-chain decentralized exchange code, allowing an attacker to extract approximately $176K (85.17 ETH). Most funds were subsequently recovered with support from Star Labs and the HECO White Hat Security Alliance.

name: LML/USDT staking protocol
description: On April 1, 2026, the LML/USDT staking protocol on BSC was exploited for $950K via price manipulation. Attacker purchased nearly all LML supply from PancakeSwap using 309.5M USDT, burned tokens, and manipulated TWAP to claim rewards at artificially inflated rates, causing LML to crash 99.6% to $0.1758.

name: BounceBit
description: BounceBit Chain was exploited through an authorization flaw in a protocol-level module inherited from the Evmos stack. A function supporting vesting/lockup operations allowed the caller to specify another account as the source of funds without correctly verifying that the source account had authorized the debit. The attacker used this flaw to transfer 286.54M BB from nine accounts without stealing private keys or forging signatures. BounceBit subsequently halted the chain and decided to retire its Layer 1 and reissue BB on BNB Chain from a pre-exploit snapshot

name: Poolz Network
description: Poolz Finance was exploited through an integer overflow vulnerability in the unaudited LockedControl contract. The attacker manipulated the CreateMassPools function and GetArraySum method to trick the vesting contract into believing large amounts were deposited while actually depositing minimal tokens.

name: Drop
description: Neutron governance proposal 9 reassigned administration of Drop’s dATOM converter and withdrawal-manager contracts to the attacker. After the proposal passed, the attacker migrated both contracts to previously uploaded malicious code exposing a withdraw_all function and swept their entire balances. Drop’s liquid-staking or redemption logic itself was not exploited; the contracts were taken over through Neutron chain governance

name: Bloom
description: Bloom was exploited through a mint vulnerability on the Blast blockchain, resulting in $540,000 in losses. The team negotiated with the exploiter who offered a 10% bug bounty, recovering 90% of stolen funds for redistribution to liquidity providers.

name: iVest
description: On August 12, 2024, iVest token on BSC was exploited via a business logic flaw in its custom ERC20 transfer function. The __MakeDonation function, invoked during token transfers, had vulnerabilities that allowed attackers to manipulate token prices and extract value through the donation mechanism.

name: Mozaic
description: Rogue developer stole a core team member's private key, gaining access to the bridgeViaLifi function. Attackers drained $2.4M, with 90% recovered after funds were frozen on MEXC exchange.

name: Nerve
description: Attacker exploited the same MetaPool vulnerability in Nerve Finance that previously affected Synapse Bridge. Using flash loan attacks on fUSDT and UST MetaPools, the attacker exhausted pool liquidity by exploiting the inconsistent calculation of LP token value between swap and swapUnderlying functions.

name: Bitcash
description: Bitcash.cz was compromised and bitcoins from up to 4,000 customer wallets were stolen. The attack appeared to use phishing emails sent from compromised Bitcash staff accounts to lure victims into sending BTC for supposed recovery.

name: unshETH
description: A developer leaked private deployment keys to GitHub, which an attacker exploited to drain $375K from the unshETH staking protocol. The attacker transferred ownership of smart contracts to themselves before the protocol emergency-paused withdrawals and the keys were secured.

name: Ledger (Supply Chain)
description: Attackers purchased genuine Ledger hardware wallets, installed concealed components capable of capturing recovery phrases, and redistributed the modified devices through resellers. The implants monitored the wallets’ displays during initialization and transmitted captured recovery phrases through cellular connections. Attackers subsequently derived users’ private keys and drained their cryptocurrency holdings. Ledger confirmed that its Secure Element, operating system, and internal infrastructure were not compromised

name: BNS
description: BitBNS exchange in India was hacked on February 1, 2022, via AWS cloud storage misconfiguration exposing private key backups. Attacker drained hot wallets for $7.5-8M; incident was concealed until March 2023.

name: New Gold Protocol
description: New Gold Protocol (NGP) was exploited on its launch day when the attacker exploited a flashloan-powered price oracle manipulation. The protocol relied on DEX pair reserves to calculate the NGP token price, allowing a single Uniswap pool to be manipulated. The attacker used a flash loan to distort pool balances, artifically lowering the reported price to bypass transaction limits and acquire massive amounts of tokens at unrealistic prices. Stolen assets were bridged to Ethereum through Tornado Cash.

name: IPOR Fusion
description: On January 6, 2026, Fusion PlasmaVault on Arbitrum was exploited via EIP-7702 delegation; missing instantWithdraw validation allowed malicious fuse contracts to execute arbitrary code and drain $336K USDC. ~$267K was moved to Tornado Cash.

name: Magnate Finance
description: On August 25, 2023, Magnate Finance team rug-pulled Base depositors by deleting communication channels (Telegram/website), manipulating the price oracle, and draining all assets. The deployer had previously executed Solfire rug ($4.8M) in 2022.

name: EosRoyale
description: EosRoyale gambling platform was exploited via a prior-block randomness vulnerability on October 26, 2018. Attackers calculated future random numbers by analyzing information from previous blocks, predicting game outcomes. 11,000 EOS were stolen from the operational wallet, valued at approximately $60,000 at the time.

name: EAC
description: EAC token on BSC was exploited via a flash loan attack. The attacker used a DODO X flash loan to artificially inflate EAC price, executed large swaps on Pancakeswap to increase token price beyond fair value, then sold the inflated position for profit after repaying the loan.

name: Volo Vault
description: On April 21, 2026, Volo Protocol on Sui was exploited when a high-privilege admin key was compromised, likely via social engineering. The attacker drained three vaults: WBTC (~$2.1M), XAUm (~$0.9M), and USDC (~$0.5M). The team recovered ~$3.44M (90%) of funds after blocking a $500K bridge attempt.

name: Hyperliquid Malaysia
description: On August 6, 2026, a wallet associated with Hyperliquid Malaysia was exploited via a compromised private key on Solana. The exploiter address was identified on-chain; the loss amount was not disclosed and no dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: DEXX
description: On November 16, 2024, DEXX memecoin trading terminal suffered a security breach affecting at least 900 users when attackers gained access to private keys and drained wallet contents across Solana. Post-investigation estimates reached $30M, with SlowMist linking 8,620+ wallets to the attacker and one user losing over $1M.

name: PolyNetwork
description: On August 12, 2024, an undisclosed vulnerability in Poly Network's Cross-Chain Management Contract drained $4-5M in wrapped assets on Neo N3, de-pegging Flamingo's f- and p-assets. Poly Network suspended the bridge and Flamingo paused cross-chain features; Neo Global Development relaunched and took over in September. This was the third Poly Network compromise.

name: Bizness
description: Standing on Bizness protocol on Base was exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability in its contract logic. The attacker repeatedly called functions before state was properly updated, enabling them to drain funds through reentrant calls.

name: Sorra Finance
description: Sorra Finance's staking contract had a critical flaw in the getPendingRewards() function that failed to track and deduct previously claimed rewards. The attacker deposited 122,868 SOR tokens with a 14-day lockup, then repeatedly called withdraw() to claim the same rewards multiple times before the state was updated.

name: FinNexus
description: The private key to the FinNexus contract deployer account was compromised, allowing the attacker to assume contract ownership. The attacker minted 323M FNX on Ethereum (~$6M) and 60M FNX on BSC (~$1.6M), then immediately dumped tokens on markets. FNX price collapsed from $0.356 to $0.0272 (92% decline).

name: 88mph
description: A critical initialization bug in the 88mph NFT contract allowed anyone to call initialize() multiple times, enabling arbitrary contract owner takeover and unrestricted NFT minting. An attacker could have stolen all underlying assets by minting/burning user NFTs. Reported via Immunefi with $42,069 bounty; 88mph patched within 2 hours.

name: AnubisDAO
description: AnubisDAO collected 13,556 ETH (~$60M) from investors in October 2021 but redirected all funds to attacker wallets within 20 hours. Funds were later laundered through Tornado Cash in July 2023.

name: PancakeSwap
description: An insider with admin lottery access exploited a predictable block-hash-based RNG by orchestrating multiple transactions in the same block with varied gas prices. This allowed manipulation of the random number generator to predict winning tickets and withdraw 59,765 CAKE (~$1.8M) from the lottery prize pool.

name: Minterest
description: An attacker flash loaned USDY tokens, triggering a reentrancy attack during the transfer fallback function. Exchange rate updates executed immediately after borrow operations, allowing the attacker to manipulate rates and liquidate user positions for mETH and WETH.

name: Overnight Finance
description: OverNight protocol on Avalanche suffered a flash loan attack on December 2, 2022. The attacker exploited protocol logic to drain funds using a flash loan.

name: Dexodus Finance
description: On May 26, 2025, Dexodus Finance's leverage module was exploited for ~$291K via a stale Chainlink oracle report. The attacker used the valid but outdated data to enter a 100x leveraged long position at artificially low ETH price, then closed at the correct price within the same transaction. Dexodus recovered 100% of affected liquidity within 24 hours.

name: BSC TMM/USDT
description: On April 4, 2026, attacker used flashloans to burn ~850M TMM tokens, reducing the TMM reserve to 1 token in the TMM/USDT pool. This price distortion allowed swapping for 272M USDT, netting $1.665M profit after flashloan repayment. Inadequate access controls enabled the large-scale burn.

name: Cyrus Finance
description: On March 22, 2026, Cyrus Finance on BSC was exploited through price manipulation. Attacker abused reliance on live PancakeSwap V3 spot price in withdrawal logic, with no TWAP or oracle resistance, to extract liquidity and tokens.

name: Brahma Finance
description: On November 9, 2022, Brahma Finance's TopGear vault on Ethereum was exploited via an arbitrary external call vulnerability in the Zapper contract, where the swapTarget parameter was not validated, allowing an attacker to construct malicious call data and drain 89,343 USDC from three authorized user accounts.

name: Fantasm Finance
description: Fantasm Finance's mint function validated msg.value instead of the actual FTM amount transferred, allowing attackers to mint XFTM without collateral. The attacker drained the reserve of 1,008.5 ETH (~$2.62M), swapped it through Tornado Cash, and XFTM fell ~98%.

name: Swarm Markets
description: A vulnerability in Swarm Markets' xTokenWrapper contract allowed unauthorized access to withdraw assets. While a MEV bot intercepted most of the attacker's attempts, the first hacker secured 472.8K SMT plus DAI and USDC.

name: Bitfinex
description: Bitfinex suffered a security breach when an attacker compromised hot wallet private keys, stealing 119,756 bitcoins (~$72 million). The exchange halted trading and withdrawals while investigating.

name: TronWow
description: TronWow gambling game's random number generation was exploitable, allowing attackers to predict game outcomes. Attackers launched 1,203 attacks and extracted 2,167,377 TRX in profits.

name: TopGoal
description: TopGoal's hot wallet was compromised, leading to the theft of over 4.8 million TMT tokens used for TopPrize rewards distribution. The attacker swapped TMT tokens for BNB on PancakeSwap and used Tornado Cash to obscure the transfer. User assets and NFTs remained secure as they were stored separately.

name: OKEx
description: Attackers conducted a 51% attack on Ethereum Classic to execute a double-spend against OKEx. They deposited ETC, withdrew it, then reorganized the blockchain to erase the deposit transaction while keeping their funds, resulting in a net $5.6M theft via unconfirmed transaction reversal.

name: SIR
description: On March 30, 2025, SIR.trading on Ethereum was exploited for $355K via callback validation flaw. Vault contract's callback did not validate Uniswap pool address, allowing replacement with attacker-controlled address via transient storage manipulation (one of first Dencun-targeted exploits).

name: Yearn Finance
description: Yearn Finance's legacy V1 TUSD vault was exploited for $300K via a donation attack. Attackers deposited Fulcrum sUSD tokens to artificially inflate share price, allowing Yearn TUSD tokens to be minted at minimal cost before the price collapsed.

name: Raydium AMM
description: Raydium on Solana lost $1.34M on June 10, 2026 in its deprecated AMM V3 program when attacker bypassed LP token validation using a fake token address. Attacker drained inactive pools containing USDC, SOL and RAY by bypassing proportion checks.

name: RRWallet
description: On August 6, 2026, RRWallet was exploited via weak key generation on Bitcoin, allowing an attacker to derive private keys and steal approximately $2,000,000. Flagged by Coinspect; no dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: Ola Finance
description: Voltage Finance on Fuse was drained of ~$4.67M via a reentrancy attack. The attacker funded a flash loan, borrowed against collateral, then used ERC677's transfer callback to reenter and withdraw collateral without repaying, repeating until markets were empty before bridging to Ethereum and BNB Chain.

name: UvToken
description: On October 27, 2022, UvToken's mining pool contract on BSC was exploited via a logic error in the withdrawal mechanism where input validation failed to authenticate the caller, allowing an attacker to make malicious calls and seize approximately 1,078 BNB and 1,161,991 BUSD (~$1.5M) from the vault.

name: Ambient
description: An attacker exploited Ambient Finance's single-contract architecture by transferring 50 ETH to a newly created contract and extracting ~83.72 ETH via insufficient access controls in the deposit/withdrawal logic.

name: DEUS Finance
description: Deus Finance derivatives platform was exploited via oracle manipulation. A flash loan was used to move prices in Solidly and Spirit pools, causing the Muon oracle to report inflated prices. This triggered cascading liquidations rendering users insolvent.

name: Flamincome
description: Flamincome’s VaultYUSDT strategy valued its Convex-staked Curve USDP LP position using the strategy’s BaseRewardPool.balanceOf() multiplied by Curve’s spot get_virtual_price(). The attacker used approximately $18M USDT of Morpho flash liquidity to acquire USDP and imbalance-mint USDP metapool LP, then permissionlessly staked LP for the strategy through Convex. This temporarily increased the strategy’s reported holdings/NAV. VaultYUSDT immediately incorporated the manipulated valuation into its share price, allowing the attacker to redeem shares at an inflated value and force the strategy to withdraw real aUSDT liquidity from Aave

name: Liquid Global
description: On August 19, 2021, Japanese cryptocurrency exchange Liquid Global's warm wallets were compromised, resulting in the theft of approximately $91-97 million in various cryptocurrencies including BTC, ETH, TRX, and XRP. The attack leveraged data from a prior November 2020 breach to compromise the MPC wallet system.

name: Multichain
description: Multichain lost ~$126M on July 6-7, 2023 from bridge reserves on Fantom, Moonriver and Dogechain (WBTC, WETH, USDC, USDT, DAI, LINK and more). CEO Zhaojun, who held the MPC signing keys, had been detained since May 2023; project shut down days later.

name: MixedSwapRouter
description: MixedSwapRouter on Arbitrum was exploited through an arbitrary external call vulnerability that allowed unauthorized token transfers from the protocol.

name: NerveBridge
description: Attacker exploited a flaw in Nerve Bridge's MetaPool swap function where the swap function underestimated LP token value compared to swapUnderlying. Using a flash loan attack, the attacker received inflated LP tokens for deposited fUSDT, then removed BUSD liquidity and used swapUnderlying to extract additional fUSDT for a total profit of 900 BNB.

name: Keplr Wallet (Web3Auth)
description: In November 2026, attackers conducted unauthorized transactions from Keplr wallets created using Google or Apple social login, affecting accounts that relied on Web3Auth's third-party authentication and key-management infrastructure. Keplr and Web3Auth launched a joint investigation and suspended affected login services. Wallets created using recovery phrases or hardware wallets were not believed to be affected. The exact vulnerability, total funds stolen, and affected blockchain networks remained undisclosed

name: LuckLambo104
description: A rollback attack exploited the LuckLambo104 smart contract on February 3, 2020, one day after deployment. Attackers created attack contracts that executed transaction rollbacks, causing 6,588 TRX to be improperly redistributed from the contract. The attack highlights the importance of thorough security testing before mainnet deployment.

name: Truebit
description: Truebit Protocol suffered $26.44M exploit on January 8, 2026 from integer overflow in token purchase logic (Solidity 0.6.10 unpatched). Attacker minted TRU at negligible cost and sold to bonding-curve for ~$26M; TRU crashed 99.9%.

name: The Idols
description: The Idols NFT contract had a flaw in the _beforeTokenTransfer function that incorrectly handled reward distribution when sender and recipient were the same address. By repeatedly calling safeTransferFrom with identical from/to addresses, an attacker exploited the logic flaw to drain 97 stETH from the reward pool.

name: Affluent
description: Affluent’s lending vaults reportedly suffered unauthorized share minting that allowed attackers to redeem vault assets without providing corresponding deposits. The supplied analysis identifies suspicious transactions on September 30, October 12, and October 16, 2026, involving multiple wallets. Extracted assets were reportedly transferred through exchanges, swaps, and cross-chain services

name: ApolloX
description: On June 8, 2022, ApolloX on BSC was exploited when a hacker accumulated 255 signatures using a flaw in the Trading Rewards Contract and used them to withdraw 53 million APX tokens from the Withdrawal Contract without proper verification. The tokens were swapped for ~$2.15M BUSD via PancakeSwap.

name: BigONE
description: On July 16, 2025, BigONE crypto exchange suffered a supply chain attack where an attacker gained access to production infrastructure and modified critical backend logic to automatically approve fraudulent withdrawal requests. The attack drained approximately $27 million across five blockchains before being detected.

name: Ethervista
description: EtherVista’s EtherVistaPair.swap() contained an integer overflow vulnerability in its constant-product invariant check. Because the contract multiplied two uint112 reserves without sufficient overflow protection, the calculation could wrap around and incorrectly validate swaps that reduced the pool’s actual reserve product. An attacker registered a malicious contract as an authorized router and executed two crafted swaps to withdraw WETH and VISTA from the pool

name: Meter
description: On September 23 at 21:14 UTC, an attacker exploited a block-validation flaw on Meter mainnet that allowed unbacked MTR and MTRG to be created. The attacker dumped the counterfeit assets through DEXs and bridged proceeds out of Meter. Meter paused both mainnet and its bridge and warned that transactions after block 100731417 may not be honored. The team preserved chain state and is determining a recovery method

name: Beluga
description: Beluga Protocol's multichain AMM on Arbitrum was exploited through pool balance manipulation, resulting in approximately 175K USD in losses. Beluga is a Layer 3 infrastructure aggregating liquidity across multiple chains.

name: Thetanuts Finance
description: A deprecated Thetanuts Finance Index Vault was exploited through an integer-division rounding flaw in its mint accounting. Using a flash loan, the attacker reduced the index token supply to a minimal level and repeatedly minted replacement shares while required underlying-token deposits rounded to zero, allowing the attacker to retain assets redeemed from the vault. The attacker extracted 105,471.499078 USDC plus residual option-token positions. About one hour later, a whitehat used the same vulnerability to secure approximately $2M of assets from another vulnerable legacy vault

name: Keep3r Network
description: On June 12, 2023, an attacker compromised Keep3r Network's governor private key (an insecure vanity address). Attacker reset pool governors and launched a reentrancy attack, harvesting ~4,084 KP3R (~$200K); attacker was funded via Tornado Cash.

name: SpookySwap
description: SpookySwap's frontend domain was compromised on November 18, 2023, with malicious phishing code injected to impersonate legitimate contract interactions. Users accessing the compromised domain were tricked into signing transactions draining their wallets. The attack resulted in $5K in realized losses before the team identified and removed the malicious code.

name: ZKSwap
description: On July 9, 2025, ZKSwap's Ethereum Layer 1 bridge was exploited through its emergency withdrawal mechanism (Exodus Mode). The attacker exploited a critical flaw where the verifyExitProof() function failed to perform actual cryptographic verification of zero-knowledge proofs. By forging withdrawal proofs, the attacker artificially inflated their balance and withdrew approximately $5 million in assets.

name: Anchor
description: After Luna 2.0 launch, Chainlink froze LUNC price updates while the oracle maintained a hardcoded $0.10 minimum. An attacker deposited bLUNA at vastly inflated collateral value and borrowed 40M UST for a net $800K profit. Anchor froze markets immediately upon discovery.

name: OpenSea
description: OpenSea users received phishing emails impersonating the platform and requesting wallet connection for a contract migration. Attackers tricked users into approving malicious transactions that transferred NFTs to attacker-controlled wallets. The attack stole approximately 640 ETH worth of NFTs from 28 wallets.

name: Indodax
description: On September 10, 2024, Indodax Indonesian crypto exchange suffered a $25.47 million hack affecting its hot wallet. Attackers obtained approximately 5,204 ETH ($12.37M) along with Polygon, Tron, Bitcoin and various ERC-20 tokens without compromising private keys, suggesting the breach involved the withdrawal protocol itself.

name: Zerogoki
description: On August 8, 2021, Zerogoki was exploited for approximately $670K when an attacker provided a price oracle signed by legitimate private keys but containing crafted token swap amounts, bypassing normal validation and allowing unauthorized fund extraction.

name: Movie Token
description: Movie Token's extractFromPoolForLpMining function burned tokens directly from the PancakeSwap MT/WBNB LP pair without the pair's knowledge. Combined with a flash swap callback, this allowed the attacker to collapse the pool's MT reserve from 6.76M to 21K, enabling massive sell orders at inflated prices.

name: ZenCash
description: On June 2, 2018, ZenCash (now Horizen) suffered a 51% attack resulting in double-spend losses of over $500K. The attacker gained majority hashrate control and reorganized 38 blocks, executing double-spends of 13,000 and 6,600 ZEN across exchanges. The attack likely involved rented hashpower from NiceHash.

name: X100
description: X100’s governance system allowed an attacker to obtain two of three Senate seats using flash-loan-funded X tokens. The attacker immediately used this majority to approve and execute a malicious treasury proposal within the same transaction. The proposal forced the Freezer to swap 400,000 X tokens into an attacker-controlled liquidity pool with zero minimum output, allowing the attacker to extract treasury value through a manipulated trade

name: FFIST
description: FFIST's _airdrop() function used predictable randomness via manipulable parameters (last airdrop address, block number). Fixed airdrop amounts (1 token) created pool imbalances, collapsing FFIST price to $1 and allowing attackers to swap small token amounts for disproportionate USD value.

name: Wemix
description: An attacker stole authentication credentials for Wemix's Nile NFT platform service monitoring system and used them to gain access to the Play Bridge Vault. The attacker executed 13 successful withdrawals over two months of preparation, extracting 8.65 million WEMIX tokens and selling them on external exchanges. Wemix delayed disclosure by one week citing precautionary measures.

name: Dango
description: On April 13, 2026, Dango Protocol was exploited for $1.9M via missing validation on donation amounts. Attackers donated negative amounts to manipulate protocol balances, cashing out $410K before the team recovered $1.49M in tokens.

name: Ravencoin
description: On August 7, 2026, the Ravencoin network was affected by a missing input validation issue. Flagged by the Ravencoin project; the loss amount was not disclosed and no dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: BBXToken
description: BBXToken's transfer function includes a burn mechanism that transfers liquidity pool tokens to a dead address before calling sync(). An attacker exploited this to artificially manipulate PancakeSwap's pool reserves, creating an imbalance that allowed extraction of value from the pool.

name: LCX
description: On January 8, 2022 at 10:23 PM GMT, attackers compromised LCX's Ethereum hot wallets and transferred $7.94 million in assets including ENJ, LINK, SAND, and stablecoins. Funds were converted within 45 minutes; LCX recovered ~60% through law enforcement.

name: Echo Bridge
description: Echo Protocol's Monad bridge was compromised on May 18, 2026 when attacker obtained admin key with minting privileges, minting 1,000 eBTC and executing swaps to extract 385 ETH (~$821K realized).

name: NewDex
description: Newdex decentralized exchange was exploited on September 14, 2018 when hackers created one billion fake EOS tokens named 'EOS'. The platform's lack of smart contract validation and reliance on personal accounts for settlement allowed attackers to purchase real EOS (4,028) and other tokens (BLACK, IQ, ADD) using the counterfeit tokens. The exchange compensated all users.

name: pNetwork
description: A governance key leaked in pNetwork's pGALA bridge contract on BSC allowed 55.6B pGALA tokens to be minted and sold on PancakeSwap. The pNetwork team executed a white-hat intervention to drain $4.3M from PancakeSwap and limit losses.

name: Aethir
description: On April 9, 2026, attacker took over AethirOFTAdapter on BNB Chain and drained ~423K ATH via unprotected ownership/admin function with no multisig or timelock. Funds were bridged to TRON via Symbiosis; Aethir disconnected contracts and coordinated blacklisting with major exchanges.

name: Crosswise
description: Crosswise's MasterChef contract had public exposure of privileged functions, allowing an attacker to gain unauthorized access. The hacker exploited this to set a trusted forwarder, compromise owner privileges, and withdraw 692K CRSS tokens. After swapping to WBNB, the attacker laundered 547 WBNB through Tornado Cash.

name: Qubic
description: An attacker exploited predictable wallet seeds generated with insufficient randomness in Qubic’s wallet software, compromising 1,404 user wallets and stealing approximately 2.94 trillion QU. The vulnerability affected certain wallets created on Apple devices and Safari browsers. Qubic halted its network at tick 85,371,949, while MEXC froze the account receiving the remaining stolen funds. Seed generation was corrected in wallet version 4.26.4

name: BEVO
description: On January 30, 2023, the BEVO reflection token on BSC was exploited. The attacker took a flash loan of 192.5 WBNB, swapped for BEVO tokens, and invoked the deliver function which decreased the _rTotal value. This manipulation of the deflationary mechanism allowed the attacker to profit approximately $45K.

name: Thoreum Finance
description: On January 19, 2023, Thoreum Finance on BSC was exploited through a logic flaw in the transfer mechanism. An attacker deposited BNB to gain WBNB, then used the swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens function to exchange for THOREUM tokens, exploiting a branch in the transfer logic to profit approximately 2,260 BNB (~$65.5K).

name: Goledo
description: Goledo Finance, a lending protocol on Conflux eSpace, was exploited when an attacker borrowed 11M CFX via flash loan and purchased 24.6M PPI tokens to artificially inflate the price. The attacker then used the inflated PPI price as collateral to borrow 7.9M CFX from Goledo's lending pool. The attacker later contacted Goledo to negotiate.

name: Revest Finance
description: On March 27, 2022, Revest Finance was exploited via ERC1155 reentrancy when the fnftId counter was incremented after the external callback. The attacker re-entered the mint function to create multiple FNFTs pointing to the same pool, then redeemed all to drain ~$2M in BLOCKS, ECO, and RENA tokens.

name: MANTRA Chain
description: MANTRA Chain halted its network after detecting an exploit involving its Cosmos EVM module. The incident was isolated to two MANTRA-controlled wallets and was traced to a vulnerability in an upstream dependency. MANTRA contained the immediate threat, prepared a patched release, and stated that no user funds were exploited

name: Spartan
description: On May 1, 2021, Spartan Protocol on BSC suffered the first flashloan attack on the chain, losing $30M. An attacker obtained a 100k WBNB flashloan, inflated the liquidity pool's asset balance through multiple transactions, then burned pool tokens to withdraw an unfair share because the contract checked current balance instead of cached balance.

name: Matez
description: On November 21, 2024, the Matez protocol on BNB Chain was exploited via an integer truncation vulnerability in its arithmetic operations, resulting in approximately $80K in losses.

name: xBlast
description: On April 9, 2024, the xBlast protocol's main wallet was compromised and the attacker transferred XBL tokens worth approximately 22 ETH (~$84.5K) to an alternate address and sold them. xBlast responded with plans to deploy new XB tokens and provide fair compensation to affected users.

name: Dominion
description: An attacker exploited Dominion’s treasury wallet associated with SILV, Dominion’s tokenized silver product on Solana. Sunrise confirmed the incident originated with Dominion and was not a compromise of Sunrise infrastructure. Sunrise subsequently removed the SILV market from its UI and warned users not to interact with the SILV token while Dominion and its security partners investigate. The exact mechanism through which the treasury wallet was compromised has not yet been disclosed

name: Bungee
description: Socket's Bungee bridge aggregator was exploited on January 16, 2024 when missing validation of the swapExtraData parameter allowed over 700 users to lose $3.3M via injected unauthorized transferFrom calls.

name: TrustedVolumes
description: An attacker exploited missing access control in TrustedVolumes' RFQ swap proxy to add themselves to the order signer allowlist, forge trade orders, and drain funds across 85 transactions in WETH, WBTC, USDT, and USDC.

name: Eminence
description: Eminence, an incomplete unaudited DeFi project by Andre Cronje, was exploited less than 3 hours after launch. The attacker borrowed 15M DAI from Uniswap, bought EMN, burned half for eAAVE to artificially inflate the price, then withdrew from the bonding curve at the manipulated price, draining the protocol.

name: Sumer.money
description: On April 12, 2024, SumerMoney (a Compound fork) on Base was exploited via reentrancy vulnerability. An attacker used a flashloan and reentrancy call to manipulate exchange rates and redeem collateral at inflated rates, extracting approximately $310K worth of assets while bypassing proper accounting.

name: MU&MUG
description: MU&MUG tokens on Avalanche were exploited through a flash loan price manipulation attack. The attacker used a flash loan to artificially inflate the token price, enabling profitable swaps that drained $57K.

name: YieldCore-3rd-deal
description: YieldCore's RWAVault overrode ERC4626 withdraw() and redeem() functions but removed the standard authorization check when msg.sender ≠ owner. Any caller could specify an arbitrary depositor as owner and direct withdrawn assets to an arbitrary receiver. An attacker drained 392,764 USDC of principal from eight depositors across multiple calls.

name: dTRINITY dLEND
description: On March 17, 2026, dTRINITY dLEND was exploited for ~$257K through an empty market vulnerability. The attacker manipulated the liquidityIndex via repeated flashloan premium accrual on a newly-deployed cbBTC reserve with near-zero liquidity, inflating collateral valuations and enabling borrowing of the entire dUSD supply.

name: Juice Finance
description: Juice staking contract drained of 1.3M tokens via exploit of reward distribution logic. Attacker swiftly sold tokens on Uniswap, netting ~54 ETH. Team recovered by airdropping stakers their stake plus 10% bonus.

name: Mt. Gox
description: Mt. Gox's auditor's computer was compromised, giving attackers access to the exchange's admin credentials. Attackers manipulated the exchange price to $0.01 BTC and used the access to drain customer accounts, transferring approximately 2,000 BTC while 650 more were purchased at the artificially low price.

name: Ooki
description: On February 18, 2020 during ETHDenver, bZx was exploited via multi-protocol oracle manipulation across Kyber, Uniswap, dYdX, and Compound in a single transaction. Attacker manipulated sUSD pricing and front-ran liquidations, resulting in ~$645,000 in losses from dependence on unvalidated on-chain price oracles.

name: Robinhood
description: On January 25, 2023, Robinhood's social media accounts (Twitter, Instagram, Facebook) were compromised and used to promote a fake RBH token on the BNB Chain. Attackers made off with 26.95 BNB (~$8,200) from users who fell for the scam, with the account believed to have been compromised via a third-party vendor.

name: Ionic Protocol
description: Attackers impersonated Lombard Finance members to trick Ionic Money into listing counterfeit LBTC. Attackers then minted 250 fake LBTC as collateral to borrow $8.6-8.8M in legitimate tokens, bridging ~$3.5M to Ethereum. Inadequate identity verification enabled the social engineering.

name: Veil Cash
description: On February 20-21, 2026, Veil Cash on Base was exploited for 2.9 ETH (~$5.7K). Attacker exploited a misconfigured Groth16 SNARK verifier with identical delta and gamma parameters, breaking the soundness equation and enabling proof forgery to withdraw 29 times from the privacy pool without depositing.

name: MicDao
description: MicDao was exploited when an attacker manipulated token supply by burning tokens to artificially reduce total supply and inflate the token price, then sold MicDao tokens for profit and converted the funds to BSC.

name: Quickswap V3
description: Attackers hijacked QuickSwap's GoDaddy DNS, redirecting swaps to their address. Users unknowingly traded through the attacker's proxy contracts, losing $107.6K before the domain was recovered on May 18.

name: DungeonSwap
description: DungeonSwap and Launch Zone protocols were exploited through excessive user permissions in the implementation contract. An attacker abused insufficient access controls to manipulate DND token pricing and drain approximately $728K from liquidity pools.

name: 1inch Swap
description: On March 5, 2025, 1inch disclosed a $5M exploit in Fusion v1 resolver contracts when a buffer overflow in _settleOrder() allowed an attacker to trigger integer underflow and hijack control flow to impersonate resolvers and execute unauthorized swaps. Most funds were recovered after negotiation.

name: ETHTrustFund
description: ETHTrustFund, an Olympus DAO fork on Base, suffered a rug pull on July 20-22, 2024 when the developer transferred the entire treasury (607 ETH, $2.1 million) to Tornado Cash and Railgun mixers and deleted all project websites and social media, executing an exit scam.

name: Unleash Protocol
description: On December 30, 2025, Unleash Protocol was exploited when an attacker compromised the multisig governance system and deployed a malicious contract. The attacker siphoned $3.9M in assets, bridged them to Ethereum, and laundered them via Tornado Cash.

name: Verus-Ethereum Bridge
description: On July 23, 2026 (second of two exploits in 66 days), Verus-Ethereum Bridge was drained of $7.54M via the import path; a small 0.01 VRSC transaction triggered unbacked ETH/tBTC payouts due to missing deposit verification. The vulnerability repeated from May and was never patched.

name: CivFund
description: CivFund had unrestricted token approvals that allowed an attacker to drain users' approved funds. The exploit abused callback functions to execute unauthorized fund transfers to Uniswap for liquidation.

name: NFT Trader
description: NFT Trader's old smart contracts contained reentrancy vulnerabilities that allowed attackers to drain NFT collateral. Multiple actors exploited the flaw to steal 13 Mutant Apes, 37 Bored Apes, and other high-value NFTs worth ~$3M total.

name: Saddle Finance
description: On April 30, 2022, Saddle Finance metapool was exploited via flash loan-assisted swaps manipulating LP token pricing. The attacker exploited inconsistencies in price calculations in the sUSD/saddleUSD-V2 metapool, which used the incorrect MetaSwapUtils library, enabling extraction of ~$11M.

name: Sovryn Lend
description: On October 31, 2026, attackers exploited Sovryn's lending and margin contracts on Rootstock through three transactions, extracting approximately $914,000 in XUSD and WRBTC. Sovryn paused its core protocol and lending pools after detecting the incident. A 24-hour withdrawal delay enabled the team to block seven additional withdrawals totaling approximately 66,134 XUSD before the funds reached the attackers. The underlying vulnerability remains undisclosed while the team completes security repairs and reconciles affected positions

name: Omm
description: On January 21, 2023, Omm protocol on Icon was exploited for $1.891M when the Redeem function accepted arbitrary collateral addresses without ownership validation. The attacker could withdraw collateral from any pool regardless of whether they owned positions in it.

name: Hyperbridge
description: On April 13, 2026, Hyperbridge's Token Gateway was exploited via unbound Merkle proof verification and a zero-second challenge period. Attacker forged a cross-chain message, minted 1 billion bridged DOT, and liquidated for approximately $2.5M in ETH and incentive pool losses; funds traced to Binance and partially frozen.

name: Orion Pools
description: On February 2, 2023, Orion Protocol on BSC and Ethereum was exploited via reentrancy in swapThroughOrionPool. Attacker created a fake token (ATK) and used reentrancy to hijack deposit logic, extracting $3M.

name: Conic Finance
description: Conic Finance exploited twice on July 21, 2023 for ~$4.2M ($3.3M ETH Omnipool, $934K crvUSD Omnipool) via read-only reentrancy in CurveLPOracleV2. Price manipulation extracted value from asset pools; audit findings hadn't covered this contract.

name: Swell
description: An attacker gained control of approximately 30 Swell operational keys across multiple networks, including the swETH/rswETH oracle bot. The attacker drained wallet balances, artificially increased swETH and rswETH exchange rates by submitting unbacked reserve values, and redirected EigenLayer reward claims. They also deployed malicious upgrade contracts capable of draining approximately 2,513 ETH, although these upgrades had not been approved or executed when the investigation was published

name: Onyx V2
