description: On September 26, 2024, Onyx Protocol (Compound v2 fork) was exploited for $3.8M via decimal precision vulnerability in its low-liquidity VUSD market. Attackers used a Balancer flashloan to manipulate exchange rates by minting and redeeming oETH, then exploited missing validation in the NFTLiquidation contract to drain value through self-liquidation rewards.

name: BitoPro
description: BitoPro exchange hot wallets compromised through malware deployment on a cloud operations team member via social engineering. Unauthorized withdrawals executed across multiple blockchains during a system update. Attackers attributed to North Korean Lazarus group based on attack patterns and methodology.

name: IoTeX
description: On February 21, 2026, ioTube bridge's Ethereum-side Validator contract private key was compromised via social engineering targeting an employee. The attacker performed a malicious upgrade bypassing validation and signature checks, gaining control of TokenSafe and MintPool. Approximately $4.3M in USDC, USDT, IOTX, WBTC, and BUSD were drained within hours. Attackers were credited to the same group behind the Infini exploit.

name: One Ring Finance
description: One Ring Finance was exploited via flash loan price manipulation when the protocol's LP token price calculation lacked time-weighted averaging. The attacker pre-positioned assets through Celer Network's cBridge and deployed a contract to drain liquidity.

name: Gate
description: Gate.io lost ~$230M on April 21, 2018 when North Korean hackers compromised exchange private keys. Attacker drained ~10.8K BTC, ~219K ETH, ~100M DOGE and other tokens. Gate concealed the breach until ZachXBT revealed it in 2024.

name: Melo
description: The Melo protocol on BSC was exploited via an access control vulnerability. An attacker gained unauthorized access to critical protocol functions, draining approximately $90,000 from user accounts. The incident highlighted insufficient access control checks on sensitive contract functions.

name: Fortress Trust
description: Attackers executed a phishing campaign against ReTool, a third-party vendor providing portal access for Fortress Trust customers to manage cryptocurrency custody. The compromise leaked Fortress operator credentials, allowing attackers to initiate unauthorized fund transfers from customer accounts.

name: Inverse Finance Frontier
description: On April 2, 2022, an attacker injected ~$3M in ETH into SushiSwap INV/ETH to artificially inflate the Keep3r price feed, then borrowed $15.6M (DOLA, ETH, WBTC, YFI) from Inverse Finance's Anchor market using inflated INV collateral.

name: Elrond
description: A newly deployed VM function executeOnDestContextByCaller allowed attackers to steal 1.65M EGLD (~$113M) and convert 917k to WEGLD, creating unbacked WEGLD in circulation. The team recovered the illegal WEGLD and burned it, restoring the 1:1 backing ratio with two mainnet upgrades.

name: AFX Bridge
description: On July 22, 2026, AFX Trade's Arbitrum bridge was exploited when the attacker obtained 5 of 7 validator private keys, bypassing the 2/3 multisig threshold and draining $24.15M in USDC. The attacker converted funds to ETH and consolidated them in a single wallet. AFX offered a 30% bounty for fund recovery.

name: TrustPad
description: TrustPad's receiveUpPool() function on BNB Chain failed to verify msg.sender, allowing an attacker to repeatedly call the function and harvest pending rewards by manipulating lock periods through untrusted external calls.

name: Carson DeFi
description: Carson DeFi token on BSC was exploited via a flash loan-based price manipulation attack. The attacker used borrowed assets to artificially move prices on connected pools, then captured value from the temporary price imbalance.

name: Terra 2.0
description: A June 2024 upgrade to Terra Phoenix reintroduced an unpatched ibc-go 7.3.x fork, reintroducing a reentrancy bug in ibc-hooks timeout callback. An attacker exploited this to mint tokens and swap them through Astroport before the chain halted.

name: SKP
description: An attacker exploited SKP's transfer hook that called pair.sync() prematurely during token transfers, before the router completed the corresponding swap. This allowed the attacker to manipulate reserve ratios mid-transaction by calling sync() from inside the transfer flow. The attacker assembled $204M in capital from flash loan sources and nearly completely drained the SKP/USDT pair, extracting $212K.

name: N00dleSwap
description: On October 26, 2022, N00dleSwap on Ethereum was exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability in the token's ERC777 callback mechanism, allowing an attacker to drain approximately $29K in tokens by reentering during token transfers.

name: Truflation
description: Malware exfiltrated private keys from Truflation's operational systems, enabling attacker to drain treasury and personal wallets across Ethereum and seven other blockchains for $3.89M in TRUF tokens, $1.07M ETH, and $236K DAI from multisig and personal accounts.

name: BitMart
description: On November 2, 2026, attackers breached BitMart and transferred approximately $391,000 in cryptocurrency from exchange-associated wallets on Base, Arbitrum, and Optimism. Blockchain investigators traced portions of the stolen funds to addresses associated with the Mercado Bitcoin exploit, which occurred on the same day. BitMart founder Sheldon Xia confirmed the breach and said the exchange had investigated the incident and strengthened its security measures. The initial access method remains unidentified

name: WUSD.fi/Glove
description: WUSD.fi's GLOVE reward system lacked Sybil protection. On May 25, 2026, attackers created Sybil wallets and used flashloans to repeatedly collect rewards, draining ~$200K from Uniswap V3.

name: DGLD
description: DGLD (gold-backed stablecoin) cross-chain bridge on Base was exploited on February 23, 2026. Attackers discovered they could mint over 100M unbacked DGLD tokens on Base within 2.5 hours, where legitimate circulation was ~70.8M. Economic impact was ~$250,000, absorbed by DGLD as the primary liquidity provider.

name: RFB
description: RFB protocol on BSC was exploited through predictable random number generation. The attacker predicted the random numbers used by the protocol's randomness mechanism, allowing them to manipulate outcomes.

name: dYdX V3
description: On November 17-18, 2023, dYdX V3's insurance fund lost $9M via coordinated market manipulation in less-liquid SUSHI and YFI markets. The attacker built leveraged positions on dYdX, orchestrated spot market price surges, and triggered a liquidation cascade worth $38M notional to drain the insurance fund.

name: Cozy V2
description: Cozy Finance lost $427K on August 29, 2025 on Optimism when completeWithdraw function lacked caller verification, letting attacker complete withdrawals using only a user's redemption ID.

name: SEAMAN
description: SEAMAN token on BSC was exploited through a business logic flaw in its protocol mechanics. The vulnerability allowed attackers to manipulate token flows.

name: zkLend
description: zkLend lost $9.57M on February 11, 2025 on Starknet via an integer division rounding vulnerability. Attacker exploited truncated rounding in withdrawal calculations with precise wstETH deposits to inflate their raw_balance to 1724, draining all tokens from other pools. Attacker returned ~$3.2M after negotiation but lost remaining to a Tornado Cash scam.

name: TIME
description: TIME token's integration of ERC-2771 with an unprotected multicall mechanism allowed arbitrary address spoofing. An attacker executed a delegatecall with malicious data, burned massive amounts of tokens from the LP, inflating the token price to extract ~$190K.

name: BlueBerry
description: On February 22-23, 2024, BlueBerry's lending market was exploited when borrowing was accidentally enabled early. A user obtained a 1 WETH flashloan from Balancer, deposited it into the lending contract to manipulate oracle prices, and overborrowed 457 ETH (~$1.34M). Whitehat c0ffeebabe.eth front-ran the exploit and recovered ~366 ETH (~$1.07M).

name: 402bridge
description: On October 27, 2025, 402bridge on Base was compromised just days after mainnet launch, affecting over 200 users and losing 17,693 USDC. Attackers accessed private keys stored on servers with excessive authorization permissions in the x402 mechanism.

name: CoinPoker
description: On November 8, 2024, CoinPoker's hot wallet was compromised, resulting in the loss of approximately 2000 ETH (~$2M). The attacker performed a series of transactions testing the system before executing 82 transactions within 50 minutes, each under $25K to avoid detection. Funds were laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: Hedera
description: Hedera Token Service (HTS) precompile bug March 9-11, 2023 allowed attacker to impersonate DEX pool accounts via delegatecall, draining ~$600K from Saucerswap, Pangolin, and Heliswap before network halted.

name: RES Token
description: On October 6, 2022, RES Token was exploited via a flash loan attack that manipulated the pool price. The attacker used the thisAtoB function to swap tokens multiple times at artificially inflated prices, extracting ~$290K in repeated transactions.

name: LI.FI
description: LI.FI's swap aggregator was exploited via unchecked external calls in the swap contract. The attacker drained $600,000 from 29 user wallets that had granted infinite token approvals.

name: SmartMesh
description: On April 25, 2018, SmartMesh token suffered an integer overflow in the transferProxy function, allowing attackers to generate massive quantities of counterfeit tokens (~65.3 trillion). Though no direct USD loss is documented, ~16.6M counterfeit tokens were actually traded on exchanges before being halted.

name: Rico
description: On April 20, 2024, the Rico protocol on Arbitrum was exploited via an arbitrary external call vulnerability. An attacker was able to execute unauthorized calls within the vulnerable contract, extracting funds. The exact amount was not publicly disclosed.

name: TSR
description: On June 1, 2026 TesseraDAO's mint function was exploited via inadequate access control, allowing an attacker to mint approximately 99 million TSR tokens, immediately selling them on PancakeSwap for ~2.5M USDT, then bridging to Ethereum and laundering funds via Tornado Cash.

name: KuCoin
description: On September 25-26, 2020, attackers obtained the private keys to KuCoin's hot wallets and stole approximately $280 million. The Lazarus Group, working on behalf of North Korea, was attributed as the attacker. KuCoin recovered $235 million (84%) through on-chain tracking, contract upgrades, and law enforcement cooperation.

name: FireToken
description: FireToken's transfer function automatically burned tokens sent to Uniswap pools and immediately updated reserve balances, allowing attackers to artificially inflate ETH price by reducing FireToken reserves, then repeatedly swapped FireTokens for overpriced ETH.

name: Merlin
description: On May 26, 2021, Merlin Lab (PancakeBunny fork) was exploited for ~$680K via reward calculation flaw. Attacker deposited small amount, sent 180 CAKE to LINK-BNB vault, exploited getReward() function that calculated rewards from contract balance rather than user deposit, and repeated process 36 times. Second $550K attack followed 8 hours later.

name: Acala Network
description: A misconfiguration in Acala's iBTC/aUSD liquidity pool (deployed August 14, 2022) allowed minting of 1.28 billion unbacked aUSD tokens. The network halted swaps, burned the tokens, and limited realized losses to ~$1.6M despite the massive depeg.

name: Art Coin
description: An exploiter identified and leveraged a flaw in the Art Coin presale and Uniswap V3 LP configuration on May 7. By investing just 0.1 ETH in the presale, the attacker could withdraw at a highly favorable exchange rate due to misconfigured LP parameters. The attacker extracted 181 ETH (worth $331,000) by selling their presale allocation immediately after launch, exploiting the LP setup vulnerability.

name: BTCPay Server
description: On November 1, 2026, attackers exploited a vulnerability in BTCPay Server versions 2.4.1 and earlier to compromise self-hosted installations and steal BTC and LTC from their hot wallets. The vulnerability had been patched in version 2.4.2 in August, but outdated installations remained exposed. BTCPay Server urged affected operators to take their servers offline, migrate to fresh installations, replace compromised wallet seeds, and rotate potentially exposed credentials. Wallets whose spending keys were held off-server, including hardware wallets, were unaffected

name: Erc20transfer
description: An unverified Ethereum contract intended as an ERC20 transfer utility lacked access control in its erc20TransferFrom function, allowing anyone to transfer tokens from users who had granted approval, draining USDC across multiple victims.

name: Velodrome
description: An attacker used social engineering to compromise the domain registrar account for both Velodrome and Aerodrome, bypassing 2FA protections. Nameserver records were altered to redirect legitimate traffic to malicious protocol clones. Users were tricked into approving transactions on fake contracts, losing funds to attacker wallets. ChainSec and ZachXBT estimated losses at over $100K-$250K across both protocols.

name: US Government Crypto Wallet
description: A dormant US government wallet holding $20M from 2016 Bitfinex seizures had its private key compromised on October 24, 2024. Attacker drained $20M in ETH, USDC, aUSDC and USDT, but $19.3M was recovered within 24 hours; ~$700K went to instant exchanges.

name: Arrakis V1
description: The attacker flash-loaned 1,800 WETH and swapped approximately 145 WETH for ENS to manipulate the ENS/WETH Uniswap V3 pool’s instantaneous spot price. The Arrakis V1 vault used pool.slot0() to value its Uniswap V3 position during mint() and burn() without a TWAP or price-deviation guard. The attacker minted vault shares while the price was distorted, restored the pool price, then burned the shares for a more valuable token mix, resulting in approximately 2.94 WETH profit

name: SUPERFORTUNE AI
description: An attacker exploited insufficient verification controls in the multisig transaction process to redirect an airdrop transfer. A lookalike address was substituted for the GUA token claim contract, allowing the attacker to intercept the transfer.

name: SheepFarm
description: On November 16, 2022, SheepFarm gaming token on BSC was exploited via a register function that failed to update user timestamps after registration, allowing an attacker to call it multiple times to increase gems yield and drain approximately 262 BNB (~$72K). The attacker then converted the accumulated yield to BNB and withdrew.

name: SQ Protocol
description: SQ Protocol was exploited when an attacker used EIP-7702 authorized transactions to call privileged staking functions via a hardcoded owner backdoor, minting fake positions and draining USDT.

name: Coinbase
description: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Coinbase's SMS-based account recovery process to bypass 2FA on 6,000+ customer accounts. Threat actors leveraged phishing campaigns to obtain email, password, and phone number combinations, then used the SMS recovery flaw to intercept 2FA tokens and drain accounts. Coinbase reimbursed affected customers.

name: WLEO
description: Attacker gained access to the WLEO token contract's issuing mechanism and minted unlimited tokens. The attacker swapped the minted WLEO for ETH on Uniswap's liquidity pool, extracting ~$42K worth of Ethereum from the pool and causing a complete rug pull.

name: Goldfinch
description: A flaw in Goldfinch's legacy collectInterestRepayment() function permitted transfers from any approved address without proper safeguards. An attacker deposited USDC to manipulate share price, then repeatedly withdrew inflated amounts, draining the victim's holdings through the contract's misconfigured approval logic.

name: Gain
description: An unauthorized mint function allowed attackers to create 5 billion GAIN tokens without proper access control. The tokens were immediately sold, crashing the token price 95%.

name: Osmosis
description: On June 7-8, 2022, Osmosis suffered a $5M liquidity pool exploit where the JoinPoolNoSwap function allowed liquidity providers to withdraw 50% more than they should have. The chain halted for 2 days to prevent complete pool drainage. Osmosis Labs covered all losses using strategic reserves.

name: Multichain
description: On July 10, 2021, Anyswap/Multichain bridge was exploited when an attacker identified two V3 router transactions with identical ECDSA R values. This signature collision enabled reverse-calculation of the MPC private key, allowing unauthorized extraction of ~$7.8M across Ethereum, BSC, and Fantom.

name: Siren
description: On September 3, 2021, the SIREN protocol on Polygon was exploited via reentrancy in withdrawCapital, allowing repeated withdrawals before balance updates. The attacker drained ~$3.5M across multiple AMM pools (KNC, SUSHI, USDC, WETH, WMATIC), affecting 26 LP addresses.

name: ElevateFi
description: An attacker manipulated the EFI/DAI Uniswap V2 pair's spot price mid-transaction using flash-loan-funded buying pressure, then exploited ElevateFi's staking vault which relied on raw pair reserves without any time-weighted or external oracle guard. By inflating EFI's spot price during staking, the attacker received disproportionate staking positions: creating $2.5M recorded staking principal for only 713.5 EFI of actual principal, repeated 100 times.

name: Polynomial
description: Polynomial Protocol on Optimism suffered a missing input validation vulnerability. The flaw affected a select number of users in a contract variant not used for all functionality. The protocol compensated affected users.

name: Synthetix v1+v2
description: An oracle price feed reported Korean Won at 1000x higher than actual rate due to API outage reducing redundancy. A trading bot exploited the misconfiguration to generate over 37M sETH in profits within an hour. All funds were recovered through white-hat negotiation and bug bounty.

name: Binance Bridge
description: On October 4-6, 2022 the BNB Chain's BSC Token Hub bridge (connecting BEP2 and BEP20) was exploited via incomplete Merkle proof verification in the bridge contract, allowing an attacker to forge proofs and mint 2 million BNB (~$570 million). Binance paused the chain on October 6; roughly $137M bridged out before containment; $433M remained frozen.

name: Parity
description: On July 19, 2017, a vulnerability in Parity's multisig wallet library allowed an attacker to reset ownership of wallets and drain them. The attacker stole 153,037 ETH (~$30M) from Swarm City, Edgeless, and Aeternity. A white-hat group subsequently used the same exploit to rescue ~$166M in additional vulnerable wallets.

name: SushiSwap
description: SushiSwap's RouteProcessor2 contract was exploited due to missing validation of route parameters across Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, and Optimism. Attacker created malicious routes directing users to attacker-controlled pools, stealing ~$3.3M.

name: DxSale
description: Attacker exploited unprotected owner key in DxSale's legacy 2021 locker contract on May 26-27, 2026, draining over 1,400 liquidity pools on BNB Chain for $7.3M using EIP-7702 batch delegation. Key had no timelocks or multisig controls.

name: Little Boy Plus
description: On June 17, 2026, Little Boy Plus was exploited for ~$377.6K USDT when a zero-value transferFrom call bypassed authorization checks in the custom transfer logic. This enabled the attacker to mint LBP tokens directly into the PancakeSwap pair, creating a reserve imbalance exploitable via swap.

name: INX Digital Company
description: INX's third-party vendor serving one of the company's subsidiaries was compromised, allowing a malicious actor to execute unauthorized trades on the vendor's servers. The attacker drained approximately $1.6M from the subsidiary before being discovered.

name: Themis Protocol
description: Themis Protocol relied on DEX spot prices without flashloan protection. Attackers used flashloans to manipulate BLP prices via large wstETH swaps, borrowing assets at inflated collateral values.

name: GoonFi
description: GoonFi v2's WSOL/USDC pool on Solana was drained of ~$254,000 in March 2026 via a program configuration bug in the AMM pricing logic.

name: Ajna V2
description: Attackers exploited Ajna’s internal liquidation accounting across multiple lending pools. Current on-chain analysis shows liquidation operations could be sequenced to extract collateral while returning insufficient quote assets to the pool, including bucketTake, collateral removal, take, and settlement operations

name: Rari Capital
description: On May 8, 2021, attacker exploited Rari's ibETH integration; using dYdX flashloan and ibETH.work's arbitrary call capability, attacker artificially inflated ibETH.totalETH() to withdraw more ETH than deposited, draining ~$11M from Rari's Ethereum Pool.

name: Velocore V2
description: Velocore V2 was exploited for ~$6.8M when a fee rate calculation allowed values exceeding 100%. The attacker used a flash loan to shrink the pool and trigger LP token underflow, creating excess LP tokens.

name: Pizza DeFi
description: Pizza DeFi was exploited via an integer overflow in eCurve that allowed unbounded minting of Tripool tokens. The attacker used these tokens as collateral to drain $5M in assets.

name: Transit Swap
description: On 2022-10-02 an attacker exploited a missing payer check in Transit Swap's claimTokens function, pulling tokens from any wallet with an approval to the contract across Ethereum and BSC. Transit Swap lost $28.9 million; the attacker was traced and returned funds the following day.

name: Base Lending
description: On October 25, 2024, an unverified Compound Fork lending protocol on Base Chain was exploited via a deposit logic flaw, resulting in approximately $1M in losses. The vulnerability was in the improper implementation of deposit verification logic.

name: RiskOnBlast
description: On February 25, 2024, RiskOnBlast (GambleFi) presale (420 ETH/$1.29M raised Feb 22-23) became Blast's first rugpull when anonymous team drained balances through MEXC, Bybit, ChangeNOW.

name: Peapods Finance
description: Peapods Finance's WeightedIndex contract suffered a reentrancy attack exploited via flashloan mechanisms. The attacker extracted PEAS tokens from the protocol; the hacker (white-hat) returned approximately 90% of funds on Dec 14.

name: Vista Finance
description: Vista Finance's integration of ERC20FlashMint with staking logic failed to properly distinguish staked from free balances, allowing flashMint to incorrectly calculate available free balance for loans despite tokens being staked.

name: THORChain DEX
description: On May 15, 2026, a flaw in the GG20 threshold-signature scheme securing Asgard vaults allowed a newly churned malicious node to authorize unauthorized withdrawals, draining approximately $10.7-$10.8 million across Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Base.

name: ParticleTrade
description: ParticleTrade suffered an exploit due to unverified user input validation, allowing attackers to manipulate contract state and steal funds.

name: Zircon Gamma
description: On March 18, 2023, Zircon was exploited on Moonriver and BSC via a donation attack on the burnOneSide function in modified Uniswap V2. Attacker donated to inflate pool reserves, then withdrew shares at favorable rates due to incorrect share calculation, draining ~$350K.

name: Tectonic
description: Unverified incident claimed for November 18, 2024 on Cronos chain; extensive search found no credible reports, announcements, or news coverage of a Tectonic hack on this date.

name: BAYC/Otherside
description: Discord accounts of BAYC's community manager were compromised, and attackers posted fake limited-quantity giveaway links to a phishing site. Users were tricked into approving malicious contracts, losing 32 NFTs and over $257K in ETH.

name: Harbor Protocol
description: On August 19, 2023, Harbor Protocol's oracle was manipulated via low-liquidity cSwap prices. An attacker borrowed CMST against inflated stOSMO, LUNA, and WMATIC collateral, draining ~$250K and dropping TVL from ~$370K to ~$81K.

name: Goose Finance
description: Goose Finance on BSC exploited for $8K via share accounting flaw in vault withdrawal logic on March 14, 2026. The bug evaded prior audits.

name: Save
description: Solend on Solana was manipulated when the protocol relied on a single oracle source from Saber pool vulnerable to price manipulation. The attacker inflated USDH price from ~$1 to $15 through transaction spam, creating $1.26 million in bad debt.

name: Hacken Token
description: Hacken's HAI token private key was exposed during bridge architecture changes on Ethereum and BNB Chain. The compromised key allowed minting of 900 million HAI tokens, which were dumped on decentralized exchanges, causing the token price to crash 99%.

name: OlaXBT
description: In September 2025 OlaXBT suffered a multisig wallet compromise resulting in the theft of 32 million AIO tokens (valued at approximately $2 million). The team responded by deploying a new token contract and migrating user holdings.

name: Astera.fi
description: On October 9, 2025, Astera's lending markets on Linea were exploited through a liquidity-index inflation attack. The attacker inflated the index to overvalue their collateral, then borrowed across asUSD, LINEA, and WETH minipools for ~8% of the protocol's TVL. Linea's security team detected the pattern and froze the attack within minutes.

name: Meta Pool
description: On June 17, 2025, Meta Pool's ERC4626 vault contract on Ethereum was exploited via an unprotected mint() function in Staking.sol. An attacker called the public mint function to create 9,705 mpETH tokens (~$27M at face value) without depositing collateral, extracting only $130K due to low liquidity in affected pools.

name: Unibot
description: On October 31, 2023, Unibot's newly-deployed unverified router contract contained a call injection vulnerability allowing attackers to insert arbitrary transferFrom() calls and drain $640,000 in approved tokens from user wallets. The stolen funds were moved to Uniswap then Tornado Cash.

name: LND
description: LND, a Sonic-based Aave fork, lost $1.18M in May 2025 when a developer with unilateral deployment control introduced a malicious access-control modification that reached production unreviewed. Halborn identified the developer as a DPRK IT worker.

name: LianGoPay
description: On February 7, 2023, LianGoPay was exploited by attackers with access to private keys who deployed fake staking pool contracts with addresses similar to legitimate ones. Users were tricked into depositing into these malicious contracts, resulting in a loss of approximately $1.6M in tokens.

name: Bondly
description: Bondly's CEO was phished for admin credentials, allowing the attacker to mint 373M BONDLY tokens and crash the price 82% by dumping on liquidity pools.

name: Alpha Finance
description: Alpha Finance was exploited when an attacker used recursive flash loans to borrow against inflated sUSD debt in the CREAM Iron Bank. A rounding error in the borrow function math enabled manipulation of undercollateralized lending.

name: Cashio
description: Cashio's infinite-mint bug arose from two missing account-validation checks in the collateral deposit path, letting attackers use fake tokens as Saber LP collateral. ~2 billion CASH were minted and swapped for ~$52.8M in USDC, USDT and UST; CASH crashed to $0.00005.

name: Growth DeFi
description: On 8 February 2021 an attacker created a worthless rAXZZ token and a GRO/rAXZZ Uniswap pool, then used the single-asset deposit feature of Growth DeFi's stkGRO/rAAVE farming contract which failed to validate LP token identity, accepting the GRO/rAXZZ LP shares as legitimate GRO/rAAVE LP shares, allowing the attacker to mint 14,513 stkGRO/rAAVE shares and drain the pool.

name: TonUP
description: TonUP's staking contract was exploited due to incorrect parameter configuration, allowing attackers to steal 307,264 tokens worth approximately $107,600. The team quickly suspended redemption and bought back stolen tokens.

name: Bitrue
description: On April 14, 2023 at 07:18 UTC, Bitrue's hot wallet was compromised; attackers withdrew ~$23M in ETH, QNT, GALA, SHIB, HOT, MATIC. Compromised wallet represented <5% of total exchange funds.

name: ZEROBASE
description: Attackers deployed a malicious phishing contract on BSC that impersonated the ZEROBASE frontend, tricking users into authorizing USDT transfers. The fake contract collected token approvals, then drained hundreds of connected wallets of approximately $250K total, with one user losing $123K.

name: APEMAGA
description: APEMAGA smart contract experienced a business logic vulnerability that violated an invariant, allowing attackers to drain approximately 9.4 ETH (~$32K). The exploit was significant enough to be studied for invariant-synthesis security improvements.

name: MFT
description: On November 17, 2024, the MFT protocol on BNB Chain was exploited via a logic flaw in its contract implementation, resulting in approximately $33.7K in losses.

name: xToken
description: On May 12, 2021, xToken was exploited when an attacker used an $81M flash loan (61,800 ETH) from dYdX to manipulate Kyber Network's oracle, enabling minting of xSNXa tokens at manipulated prices for ETH and SNX. The xBNTa contract had an additional flaw allowing minting with any token, not just BNT.

name: Alephium Bridge
description: On May 30, 2026, Alephium TokenBridge was exploited via off-chain backend flaw in guardian message verification. Attackers deployed fake contracts to forge VAAs, disrupted node connectivity to trigger fallback validation, and authorized transfers totaling $815K across Ethereum and BNB Chain, plus 13.76M unbacked ALPH minting.

name: Nereus Finance
description: Nereus Finance on Avalanche was exploited when the protocol lacked time-weighted average price protection for newly introduced collateral types. The attacker manipulated prices through Trader Joe and Curve, extracting $371,000 in USDC.

name: GPU
description: GPU token's balance update logic did not properly account for self-transfers, allowing attackers to arbitrarily inflate their balance by repeatedly transferring tokens to themselves. The vulnerability was amplified via flash loans.

name: Swerve
description: Swerve Finance, a defunct Curve clone, was targeted in a governance attack where the attacker created proposals to transfer $1.3M in stablecoins to their contract. Though the attack ultimately failed due to insufficient voting power, it represented a live governance exploit attempt.

name: Titano Finance
description: Titano Finance relied on a contractor to deploy the PLAY contract, but the contractor included a backdoor allowing either the contract owner or deployer to modify the PrizeStrategy. The contractor exploited this privilege to steal 4,828.7 BNB. All stolen funds were returned to Titano's treasury on February 23rd.

name: Onyx Protocol
description: On November 1, 2023, Onyx Protocol (Compound V2 fork) was exploited for $2.1M. An attacker used a 4,000 ETH flashloan, swapped to PEPE, and donated to inflate the new oPEPE market's exchange rate, exploiting rounding errors in redemption logic.

name: RANT
description: On July 5, 2025, RANT token on Binance Smart Chain was exploited through a vulnerability in the _sellBurnLiquidityPairTokens() function. The flaw allowed attackers to manipulate the token burn process and steal approximately $204,000 from the protocol.

name: EOSBet
description: EOSBet gambling platform was exploited on September 14, 2018 via a smart contract vulnerability. Hackers created a malicious contract that generated fake transfer notifications, tricking EOSBet's verification into sending 44,427 EOS (~$200,000) to attacker accounts. This was discovered when a Reddit user published the exploit code.

name: FutureSwap
description: In December 2025, attacker exploited FutureSwap on Arbitrum using flash loans to acquire temporary governance voting power and pass a malicious proposal transferring protocol funds.

name: Lixir Finance
description: On June 25, 2026, Lixir Finance vaults were exploited via insufficient nonce validation in permit() function. Attacker reused a single non-owner signature across 41 calls on six vault clones to gain allowances and extract USDC, USDT, ETH, and LIX tokens.

name: Xave Finance
description: An attacker submitted a fake verification message to Xave's oracle on October 8-9, 2022, enabling four malicious proposals to pass through the DaoModule. This resulted in the minting of an enormous amount of RNBW tokens sent to the attacker's address, which were then converted to xRNBW.

name: SwissBorg
description: SwissBorg's SOL Earn program lost 192,600 SOL (~$41.5M) when staking partner Kiln's API credentials were compromised. Attacker embedded malicious authorization instructions in unstaking transactions to transfer withdrawal authority to attacker-controlled addresses.

name: pcash
description: The pcash DeFi protocol on EOS was attacked on May 1, resulting in the draining of the main swap contract's liquidity. The attacker stole approximately 2 million EOS tokens and attempted to evade governance by moving funds to EOS EVM accounts. The Pcash team covered user losses and worked with the EOS ecosystem to recover stolen assets, with significant funds recovered through EOS EVM administrative actions.

name: EasyFi
description: On April 19, 2021 an attacker compromised EasyFi CEO Ankitt Gaur's admin machine with malware-tampered MetaMask to exfiltrate admin keys, then transferred 2.98M EASY tokens (~$75M) and drained ~$6M in stablecoins from liquidity pools. The incident was catalogued in Taylor Monahan's Lazarus/BlueNoroff research.

name: ElasticSwap
description: On December 13, 2022, ElasticSwap was exploited on Avalanche and Ethereum via inconsistent accounting between addLiquidity (constant K) and removeLiquidity (pool balance), draining ~$854K.

name: Indexed Finance
description: The ORCL5 index token was exploited through a flaw in the tokenAmountOut output calculation, allowing a flashloan-enabled attack to drain approximately $9,925 from the protocol within 11 minutes of vulnerability discovery.

name: Merlin
description: Merlin Labs (PancakeBunny fork) suffered a second exploit 8 hours after the first on May 26, 2021, draining ~$550K. The priceCalculator had critical math errors in share price computation that allowed attackers to manipulate prices and drain funds.

name: 0G Labs
description: 0G Labs emergencyWithdraw function had improper access control or validation, allowing unauthorized withdrawals of $516K.

name: Reddio RedSonic
description: RedSonic’s permissionless registerErc20() allowed stETH to be registered as a separate vault asset even though the ETH vault’s rsvETH share price already counted the vault’s raw stETH balance through its Lido position. As a result, the same stETH balance simultaneously backed rsvETH and newly minted rsvstETH shares. The attacker deposited stETH to inflate the rsvETH share price, redeemed rsvETH against that inflated valuation, then redeemed rsvstETH to recover the same stETH collateral, effectively using one asset balance to support two share classes

name: Demex Perp
description: Demex’s bridge was exploited through insufficient verification between its bridge module and external-chain contract system. The attacker used a helper contract to falsify token-deployment reports, registering the low-value nLEND token against canonical WETH and WBNB contracts. Subsequent withdrawals released approximately $191,929 in bridge reserves despite deducting only $10.47 worth of nLEND. The withdrawal limiter also failed because it valued the deducted tokens rather than the assets released

name: Meteora DAMM V2
description: On January 17, 2026, Meteora DAMM V2 lost $1.5M when the team transferred funds to a fraudulent OTC counterparty impersonating a legitimate token buyer on Solana, which never delivered tokens.

name: Bankroll Network
description: On June 19, 2025, old BankrollStack contracts containing an integer underflow vulnerability in the sell() function were exploited. Attackers manipulated dividend accounting through lingering token approvals, draining funds from users who had previously interacted with the abandoned contracts.

name: Team Finance
description: Team Finance's migrate function, which moves locked LP positions from Uniswap v2 to v3, never validated that token and pair parameters matched the caller's lock. On 27 October 2022, an attacker locked a worthless token, then used another user's lock parameters to move that liquidity into an attacker-controlled v3 pair at a skewed price. Four locked projects lost ~$15.8M for $2,700 of attacker capital.

name: Ribbon
description: Aevo's legacy Ribbon DOV vaults were drained of $2.7 million on December 12, 2025. An oracle upgrade created a decimal mismatch (8 vs 18 decimals) with legacy assets. The attacker exploited a publicly-accessible oracle price-setting function and minimal collateral requirements to create undercollateralized positions and drain the vaults.

name: Rocket Pool
description: Patricio Worthalter, a major RocketPool token holder and POAP founder, was phished and had 85,900 RPL tokens worth $3.8M stolen. The attacker subsequently exchanged the tokens for ETH and scattered the proceeds across multiple addresses.

name: Bitfinex
description: Bitfinex's hot wallets were compromised in a breach attributed to security gaps and operational errors. Approximately 1,460 BTC were stolen from the exchange's online storage systems.

name: FlashTrade
description: Flash Trade's Solana perpetuals exchange suffered a $98K unauthorized withdrawal when an attacker exploited an incomplete validation path in MagicBlock's SDK. The ephemeral macro's undelegation callback failed to validate a fake account, allowing the attacker to trigger a fake withdrawal.

name: Radix
description: A Radix Engine execution-layer flaw allowed transactions to obtain direct references to arbitrary internal fungible and non-fungible vaults without verifying that the caller owned or was authorized to access them. The attacker supplied internal vault addresses to custom code and directly invoked withdrawal functionality, bypassing the authorization rules of the accounts and components holding those vaults. Across 26 transactions, the attacker drained nearly the entire Radix supply of six Hyperlane-wrapped assets and then used their normal Hyperlane Warp Routes to bridge the stolen assets out of Radix

name: ParaSwap
description: Augustus V6 contract vulnerability allowed attackers to drain approved user wallets. 386 wallets were exposed; approximately $300K was stolen, with 90% returned after the main attacker's wallet was identified and frozen.

name: Impermax V3
description: On November 11, 2025, Impermax V3 on Base suffered a $380K exploit. The attacker created tiny positions in low-liquidity cbBTC-tBTC pairs to push totalBalance toward zero, collapsing the exchange rate and enabling exponential minting of borrowable tokens. When totalBalance hit zero, all deposits were redirected to the attacker.

name: Zaif
description: Zaif cryptocurrency exchange suffered a hot wallet breach on September 14, 2018 when attackers gained access to private keys storing customer funds. Approximately 5,966 Bitcoin, unspecified Bitcoin Cash, and MonaCoin totaling 6.7 billion yen (~$60 million) were stolen from the exchange's operational wallets. Discovery occurred three days after the theft.

name: Pike V1
description: Pike upgraded spoke contracts with new dependencies that altered storage layout, particularly the 'initialized' variable. On April 30, 2024, this storage misalignment allowed attackers to upgrade contracts, bypass admin access, and withdraw funds. The second exploit involved 99,970 ARB, 64,126 OP, and 479.39 ETH.

name: Bitfloor
description: Bitfloor's servers were breached and hackers accessed an unencrypted backup of Bitcoin wallet keys. The founder, Roman Shtylman, had failed to encrypt the digital wallet containing encryption keys during a system upgrade, leaving the backup in unencrypted form on disk.

name: Wintermute
description: On September 20, 2022, Wintermute's $160M DeFi hot wallet was compromised. Attacker brute-forced the private key using a weak 32-bit seed from the Profanity vanity address generator; only DeFi operations were affected.

name: DeltaPrime
description: On November 11, 2024, DeltaPrime was exploited across Arbitrum and Avalanche when an attacker created a malicious trading pair, used it to convert borrowed collateral into fake reward tokens, and withdrew them, leaving the protocol with ~$4.8M in uncollateralized bad debt. This was DeltaPrime's second major hack in 2024.

name: Save
description: On November 2, 2022, an attacker manipulated USDH price on Saber DEX from $1 to ~$15 to inflate collateral value on Solend, borrowing across isolated pools. By locking the Saber account to prevent arbitrage, the attacker created approximately $1.26M in bad debt.

name: YON
description: YON token's transferFrom function lacked proper permission validation, allowing an attacker's contract to drain tokens directly from the liquidity pool shortly after deployment. Attackers exploited this to steal 190 BNB.

name: Spectra Finance
description: On July 24, 2024, Spectra Protocol's router contract was exploited for approximately $73,000 via an arbitrary call vulnerability in the execute function. The attacker crafted inputData to manipulate contract calls with arbitrary parameters, draining 188 quadrillion asdCRV tokens (inflated representation) from approved wallets.

name: AlpsCon AI Trade Hub
description: AlpsCon AI Trade Hub’s V7–V9 contracts incorrectly applied accumulated historical profit-per-share values to balances imported from preceding versions, allowing newly deposited funds to claim rewards accrued before the deposits existed. The attacker used a flash loan to create temporary ALPS service credits and exploited the accounting flaw to extract USDC. The attack was facilitated by an authorization whitelist containing a publicly known Hardhat test account, which the attacker used through EIP-7702 delegation

name: WDZD Swap
description: The attacker exploited a low-level access control flaw in the Swap-LP factory contract, transferring WDZD tokens from trading pairs to the factory address. This artificial manipulation inflated WDZD's value, allowing the attacker to trade WDZD for LP tokens at highly favorable rates and extract approximately 609 ETH (~$1M) by burning the LP tokens.

name: Makina
description: An attacker took a $280M flashloan and used $170M to manipulate Makina's sharePrice oracle via three compounding flaws: permissionless oracle updates, synchronous Curve spot prices with no TWAP, and pre-approved Weiroll paths. Extracted ~$4.2M.

name: Token of Power
description: Attacker acquired >50% voting power of TOP token via Balancer pool and passed malicious governance proposal to mint massive tokens, draining $1.58M WETH from Balancer V1 pool. Vulnerability stemmed from extremely low token supply (16,384 TOP total).

name: Orion Protocol
description: Orion Protocol was exploited via inadequate access control in the PredyPool contract's trade() function. Attackers manipulated the liabilities array and drained liquidity from trading pairs using flash loans.

name: Sentiment
description: On April 4, 2023, Sentiment on Arbitrum lost ~$1M due to reentrancy in integrated Balancer; attacker used flashloan price manipulation to drain funds. Sentiment recovered 90% ($900K+) within days through negotiation.

name: ETHFIN
description: ETHFIN smart contract exploited via an access control vulnerability allowing unauthorized calls to privileged functions.

name: LayerSwap
description: Attackers compromised LayerSwap's GoDaddy registrar account and redirected DNS to a phishing site, draining 50 users of $100K before the company regained access and began refunding users.

name: Dego Finance
description: On February 10, 2022, Dego Finance was hacked when the contract deployer's private key was compromised. Attackers drained approximately $10-14.4M from liquidity pools on Uniswap and PancakeSwap across Ethereum, BSC, and Cronos.

name: Coral
description: The wRAM token contract had a reentrancy vulnerability in the buyram function. When wram::buyram was called multiple times simultaneously, the asynchronous call to eosio::buyram caused the same RAM bytes value to be used across multiple calls, allowing minting of more tokens than intended.

name: Tether
description: On November 19, 2017, $30.95M USDT was removed from Tether's Treasury wallet and sent to an unauthorized address. Tether blocked the tokens and marked them as non-redeemable, preventing their circulation. Tether worked with the Omni Foundation to implement protocol upgrades allowing eventual token reclamation.

name: ArbiSwap
description: On March 2, 2023, ArbiSwap DEX on Arbitrum was rugged by the development team. Team promoted a fake staking scheme with 1330% APY less than 24 hours before draining 85 ETH and $112,000+ in tokens using admin functions.

name: Inputs.io
description: Inputs.io was hacked twice in 2013. Attackers compromised email accounts used for password reset and bypassed two-factor authentication due to a flaw on the server hosting side. The attacker stole 4,100+ BTC across the two separate hacks.

name: Astra Nova
description: Astra Nova's RVV token launch was disrupted when a third-party market maker account was compromised. The attacker gained access and liquidated 8.6% of the token supply for approximately $10.2M in USDT, causing the token price to plummet 75%. The attacker held stolen funds in USDT on a centralized exchange, allowing the team to coordinate recovery efforts.

name: JHY Token
description: JHY Token's TokenDividendTracker contract had a critical flaw where it set user balances to the LP token balance, allowing users to swap more tokens than they owned. This accounting error enabled attackers to drain funds by exploiting the incorrect balance tracking.

name: CoinSpot
description: CoinSpot lost ~1,283 ETH (~$2.4M) on Nov 8-9, 2023 from a compromised hot wallet private key. Attacker converted to BTC and dispersed across multiple wallets.

name: Poly Network
description: On July 2, 2023, Poly Network was exploited across 11 blockchains via insufficient validation of block headers and validator signatures in bridging logic. Attackers minted ~$43B in tokens; limited liquidity and swift exchange intervention (Tether freeze of $33M USDT) contained cashed-out losses to $5-10M.

name: Perpy
description: Perpy Finance's staking contract proxy was not properly initialized, allowing attackers to invoke initialization functions and gain control. The attacker updated the contract and withdrew 58.489M PRY tokens worth 41.895 ETH.

name: CrowdRingCircle
description: CrowdRingCircle's token contract allowed the pair's recorded reserves to desynchronize with actual balances by burning CRC directly from the pair address before calling sync(). An attacker exploited this to artificially inflate CRC's price and drain USDT from the PancakeSwap V2 CRC/USDT pool.

name: TSD (True Seigniorage Dollar)
description: An attacker accumulated 33%+ of TSD governance tokens by purchasing at low market prices, then proposed replacement of the token implementation contract with a malicious version via DAO governance vote. The attacker's voting weight passed the proposal, enabling the malicious contract to mint 11.8B TSD and immediately dump on PancakeSwap.

name: SlurpyCoin
description: SlurpyCoin was exploited via a flash loan attack that targeted its buyback mechanism. The attacker used sandwiched swaps to manipulate price and profit from the deflationary token's burning logic.

name: Kronos Research
description: Kronos Research's API keys were compromised, allowing attackers to drain 26M USD from trading wallets via unauthorized transactions.

name: Float Protocol
description: The attacker used flash-loan-funded swaps to manipulate the Uniswap V3 pool’s slot0 spot price consumed by Float’s Hypervisor contracts. This distorted currentTick() / getTotalAmounts() and consequently the valuation of LP shares, allowing the attacker to repeatedly deposit and withdraw at manipulated share values and extract 10.71 ETH

name: Bancor V3
description: Bancor Network v0.6 smart contract lacked authentication on the 'from' address parameter, allowing anyone to use stored token approvals to steal user funds. The Bancor team conducted a self-exploit withdrawing $409,656, but front-runners capitalized on the same vulnerability extracting an additional $135,229 before patch deployment.

name: SecondFi
description: Between June 21-23, 2026, deterministic nonce reuse in SecondFi's Cardano signing code (one missing line) exposed 374 wallet private keys through all historical signatures. Attacker drained 16.1M ADA (~$2.4M); white hat protected $18.5M ADA. Total exposure: $20M+.

name: Aave
description: On August 28, 2024, the ParaSwapRepayAdapter peripheral contract of Aave was exploited for approximately $56,000. The _buyOnParaSwap function had excessive token allowances that weren't properly adjusted after swap failures, allowing attackers to exploit unvalidated paraswapData parameters and drain accumulated slippage tokens.

name: Stargate Finance
description: An attacker acquired 50,000 STG tokens to create a malicious voting proposal on Stargate Snapshot, posing as a gSTG token launch. The phishing link in the proposal directed over 1,000 users to a fake eligibility-check website, stealing credentials and private keys. PeckShieldAlert confirmed $43K in losses tracked to the attacker's wallet.

name: Bitmor
description: In May 2026, Bitmor DCA contract on Base was exploited; access control flaw allowed attackers to drain wallets of any users with active token approvals.

name: Solido Cash
description: On July 23, 2026, Solido Cash's CDP suffered an oracle attack when the SOLID price feed went stale and fell back to near-par CASH valuation (0.99919999) while SOLID was trading at 22.2 SUPRA per unit. An attacker looped acquire-collateral, mint-CASH, sell-CASH twice across 18:21 UTC and 21:12 UTC transactions, minting 809,052 CASH of unbacked debt and selling it for 293.7M SUPRA.

name: Custom sAVAX Rebalancer
description: On April 19, 2026, a custom rebalancer contract on Avalanche was exploited via an arbitrary external call vulnerability. The attacker abused a public function that executed unchecked external calls while the contract held delegated credit from Aave V3, allowing them to borrow WAVAX on behalf of victims and extract approximately $64K.

name: Balancer V1
description: An attacker first used swaps to reduce the Balancer V1 BPool’s WBTC reserve to near-dust levels, then exploited rounding in joinswapPoolAmountOut. When the function reverse-calculated the WBTC required to mint a caller-specified amount of BPT, 18-decimal fixed-point arithmetic rounded the required input down to 1 satoshi while still minting the full BPT amount. The attacker minted 4,408.8 BPT through these underpriced joins and exited the pool proportionally to drain DPI, USDC, WETH, and WBTC

name: Gate
description: The StatCounter analytics service was compromised on November 3, 2018 and weaponized to target Gate.io users. Attackers injected malicious JavaScript that specifically targeted the Bitcoin withdrawal page (myaccount/withdraw/BTC), replacing withdrawal addresses with attacker-controlled wallets. The script automatically submitted forms when amounts exceeded 10 BTC or the user's daily limit.

name: Bitcoin Mission
description: Bitcoin Mission lost ~$1.3M in wrapped BTC in April 2025 when a privileged wrapped BTC handling function lacked access-control checks, allowing an unauthorized caller to move the protocol's holdings.

name: Platypus Finance
description: Platypus Finance was exploited for $8.5M via flashloan. The attacker manipulated the solvency check's cash/liability ratio calculation by depositing to increase liability and performing swaps to reduce cash, artificially inflating slippage.

name: Radiant V2
description: On January 2, 2024, Radiant Protocol on Arbitrum suffered a flashloan attack exploiting rounding issues in the burn function on a newly activated USDC market. Attacker extracted 1,900 ETH (~$4.5 million) beyond legitimate deposits through three attacks within 6 seconds of market activation.

name: Ekubo
description: On May 5, 2026, Ekubo's EVM swap router contracts were exploited when attackers discovered the contracts failed to verify whether the payer had authorized transactions. Attackers stole 17 wBTC ($1.4 million) and laundered funds via Tornado Cash.

name: Axelar Secret IBC Bridge
description: An attacker exploited the Axelar Secret bridge ics20-for-axelar contract to mint $4.67M of unbacked saTokens by forging IBC deposit packets from a malicious blockchain. The attacker created a minimal Cosmos blockchain with a single validator, opened a fake IBC channel to Secret Network, and sent forged deposit packets that bypassed channel validation. The minted tokens were redeemed back over the legitimate IBC channel to drain Axelar's escrow account, remaining undetected for seven days until a failed cross-chain transfer revealed the empty escrow.

name: AK1111
description: On November 23, 2024, the AK1111 contract on BNB Chain was exploited through an access control vulnerability that allowed unauthorized fund extraction of approximately $31.5K.

name: NiceHash
description: On December 6-7, 2017, NiceHash's payment wallet was compromised after attackers obtained employee credentials via phishing. The attacker accessed the wallet and stole 4,700+ BTC (~$64M). NiceHash eventually repaid all affected users by December 16, 2020.

name: MTDAO
description: The MTDAO contract deployed on BSC was exploited on October 17, 2022 through a malicious function call that bypassed authorization checks. The attacker called transfer functions on both the MT and ULM tokens to extract 1,930 BNB and 487,042.615 BUSD, then routed funds through Tornado Cash.

name: Multichain
description: On February 15, 2023, the AnyswapV4Router contract of Multichain was exploited via a front-running attack. The attacker exploited a lack of signature verification in the permit mechanism to front-run the anySwapOutUnderlyingWithPermit function and transfer WETH worth approximately 87 ETH ($130K) from the contract.

name: BeatXswap
description: BeatXswap’s LiquidityVestingConvert contract used the live V3 pool slot0() price as its sole BTX pricing source, without a TWAP, deviation limit, or manipulation check. The attacker flash-borrowed BTX, dumped it into the BTX/USDT V3 pool to sharply reduce sqrtPriceX96, then deposited 10,000 USDT and 2,000 USDT into the vulnerable contracts. The manipulated quote caused the contracts to contribute an excessive amount of their own BTX when minting LP positions, allowing the attacker to extract the BTX before reversing the swaps and repaying the flash loans

name: Wise Lending V2
description: Wise Lending V2 suffered a flashloan exploit on Arbitrum and Ethereum with significant losses. The exact attack vector remains unclear from available public sources.

name: Inverse Finance Frontier
description: On June 16, 2022, Inverse Finance Frontier was exploited for $1.3M direct loss ($5.8M protocol loss) via oracle manipulation. Attacker flash-borrowed 27K wBTC, swapped into Curve tricrypto to inflate yvcrv3crypto LP price, then borrowed DOLA against inflated collateral.

name: Steadefi
description: Attacker compromised deployer wallet private key to gain owner privileges over Steadefi pools, change pool ownership, and drain $1.148M in WBTC, WETH, and USDC via owner-only withdrawal functions.

name: BitGrail
description: On February 9-12, 2018, BitGrail exchange suffered a massive breach affecting 17M Nano coins (~$170M). The exploit involved a flaw in the withdrawal mechanism that allowed repeated withdrawals of the same funds. Attackers gradually stole 2.5M Nano from hot wallets, with abuse continuing over months for a total of 7.5M+ Nano.

name: Agentic FoF
description: Agentic FoF suffered a security vulnerability that allowed attackers to drain approximately $531K from its vaults. All vaults were subsequently suspended pending an internal investigation, with the Basis vault secured but also halted as a precaution.

name: Allbridge Core
description: In April 2023, Allbridge Core on BNB Chain was drained when an attacker acting as both liquidity provider and swapper manipulated pool prices to drain BUSD and USDT.

name: Nexus Mutual
description: Attacker gained remote access to founder Hugh Karp's computer and replaced his MetaMask extension with a malicious version. The compromised wallet was then used to sign and transfer 370,000 NXM tokens (~$8M) to attacker-controlled addresses. The attacker later demanded 4,500 ETH ransom.

name: OcelotDex
description: On September 20, 2024 OcelotDex (a DEX gateway on Zetachain) suffered an infinite mint exploit draining $4.9 million when attackers exploited a vulnerability in the smart contract minting functionality that failed to enforce supply caps, creating unbounded tokens to flood the market and exchange for stable assets.

name: Elephant Money
description: On April 12, 2022, Elephant Money on BSC was exploited via flash loan attack. Attacker borrowed 131K WBNB and 91M BUSD, manipulated ELEPHANT price via the manipulable oracle, and exploited insufficient flash loan guards in the TRUNK redemption mechanism to steal ~$22.2M.

name: Transit Finance
description: Transit Finance's router contract failed to validate swap pool paths provided by users. An attacker supplied a forged pool address in the path parameter, causing the router to transfer more tokens than intended during swaps.

name: Phemex
description: On January 23, 2025, Singapore-based exchange Phemex's hot wallets were drained across more than a dozen chains (ETH, SOL, XRP, BTC, BSC, Tron) in a coordinated attack, with reported losses ranging from $69.1M to $85M. The hot wallet private keys and signing infrastructure were compromised.

name: Euler V1
description: On March 13, 2023, Euler Finance was exploited via flash loan attack on the donateToReserves function. The attacker stole ~$197M in DAI, USDC, stETH, and WBTC via account balance inflation without actual collateral. The hacker returned funds within weeks; recovery completed by early April.

name: Silo V2
description: Silo's soUSDC vault was exploited through an immutable oracle that priced wstUSR at 1.133 while market price had collapsed to 0.12, combined with accounting flaws that didn't mint shares for external deposits, allowing attackers to inflate redemption payouts.

name: CityDAO
description: CityDAO's Discord was compromised via social engineering, allowing the attacker to hijack an administrator account. The attacker created a fake land-drop announcement pointing users to a phishing site, where victims connected their wallets and unknowingly approved fraudulent transactions. The attacker extracted 29.67 ETH by exploiting Discord webhooks to ensure the phishing announcement immediately appeared to all logging-in users.

name: Polymarket
description: Hackers injected malicious scripts into Polymarket's comment sections, posting phishing links that appeared to offer access to private markets. Users clicking the links were redirected to a fake Polymarket interface where attackers captured their credentials. Over $500K in user funds were drained via compromised email-login accounts.

name: LiveArtX
description: LiveArtX's treasury wallet was compromised on October 16-17, 2022, resulting in the theft of 197 NFTs from the Seven Treasures collection. The attacker exploited poor key management—the private key was shared among multiple team members with no multi-sig protection—to transfer the NFTs to their own address and sell them at depressed prices.

name: LULA
description: On July 29, 2026, LULA (BEP-20 token on BSC) suffered a ~$578K exploit via business logic flaw. Attacker exploited an accessible recycle() function in the Rental contract to transfer LULA directly from PancakeSwap V2 pair, then manipulated pair reserves via sync() call. Repeated recycle() calls drained LULA reserves to near-zero, allowing small swap for nearly all USDT.

name: 2gether
description: Attackers compromised 2gether's infrastructure, stealing approximately 27% of platform funds: 114 Bitcoin and 276 Ether from user accounts. The platform announced reimbursement options converting losses to 2GT tokens.

name: Glide Finance
description: Attacker exploited a fee parameter error in Glide Finance's contract. The team had changed a fee parameter post-audit from 1,000 to 10,000 but failed to update the corresponding value in the contract code, leaving the incorrect parameter at 1,000 and allowing attackers to drain funds via incorrectly-calculated fees.

name: Ref Finance
description: On August 14-15, 2021, Ref Finance was exploited when a faulty security hotfix failed to properly validate and debit users' LP token balances when removing liquidity from pools. This allowed attackers to withdraw more tokens than they should have, extracting approximately 507K NEAR and 1M REF tokens worth ~$3.2M.

name: Curio
description: Curio exploited March 23-25, 2024 via access control flaw in voting power. Attacker with small CGT stake escalated voting power to execute delegatecall to malicious contract, minting ~1B CGT worth $16M.

name: Exactly
description: Exactly Protocol's DebtManager on Optimism was exploited on August 18, 2023 when unvalidated market address parameter allowed attacker to bypass permit checks and reenter crossDeleverage to steal users' deposited collateral. A copycat repeated the attack the same day.

name: BTC24H
description: BTC24H Lock contract on Polygon was exploited in December 2024 for $85,700. The claim function failed to verify if msg.sender was an eligible claimant, allowing anyone to claim BTC24H tokens without authorization.

name: Aventa
description: Aventa Web3 utilities protocol exploited via flash loan attack. The attack mechanism drained approximately 3.9 ETH from the protocol through flashloan-funded exploitation of a protocol vulnerability.

name: Nuls
description: NULS blockchain was hacked on December 23, 2019, losing 2M NULS tokens (~$480K) through exploitation of a signature verification vulnerability in NULS V2.2. Attackers compromised a NULS team account and transferred the funds. Of the stolen tokens, 548K NULS entered trading markets while 1.45M were frozen. NULS responded with an emergency hard fork at block 87,800 to permanently destroy the frozen tokens.

name: Drift Trade
description: On April 1, 2026, Drift Protocol on Solana was exploited for ~$295M when attackers tricked Security Council members into pre-signing transactions via Solana durable nonces, handing over admin control. Attackers whitelisted a worthless fake token (CVT) as collateral, deposited 500M CVT, and withdrew $285M in real assets (USDC, SOL, ETH) in ~12 minutes. Security firms linked the attack to DPRK/Lazarus Group.

name: Syndicate
description: On April 29, 2026, a private key leak allowed attackers to maliciously upgrade Syndicate's Commons bridge contracts and drain approximately 18.5M SYND tokens ($330K-$400K) across two networks.

name: SpaceGodzilla
description: On July 13, 2022, SpaceGodzilla on BSC was exploited via a flash loan attack combined with price manipulation. The attacker borrowed 2.95M BUSD, swapped into SpaceGodzilla tokens to inflate the price in PancakeSwap, then swapped back to BUSD for a profit of 25,378 BUSD, which was converted to BNB and laundered through Tornado Cash.

name: HyperVault
description: HyperVault on Hyperliquid L1 conducted a rug pull in late September 2025, draining $3.6M in user funds. Developers falsely claimed audits by Spearbit and Pashov, then disappeared after moving assets through privacy tools.

name: Trinity Wallet
description: Trinity Wallet suffered a DNS hijacking attack on February 12, 2020 when the Cloudflare nameserver was compromised. Malicious code injected starting January 25 stole 8.55M MIOTA (~$2M to $2.35M) from 50+ users by exfiltrating private key seeds.

name: CFC
description: An attacker exploited CFC's custom transfer logic on a Uniswap V2-style pool by repeatedly transferring tokens to the pair and invoking skim(), triggering the _transfer() function to burn tokens. This reduced the LP pair's actual token balance, allowing the attacker to extract value through the token supply manipulation.

name: ValueDefi
description: On November 14, 2020, Value DeFi's MultiStablesVault was exploited for $7.4M DAI via a two-stage flashloan attack that manipulated stablecoin exchange rates through Curve's AMM-based oracle. The attacker voluntarily returned $2M after Value DeFi offered a $1M bounty.

name: Premint
description: On July 16-17, 2022, Premint's frontend was compromised via a vulnerable open-source image upload tool that allowed an attacker to inject malicious JavaScript into a library file. The attacker created a malicious domain and updated the JavaScript to redirect to their code, which then tricked users into signing setApprovalForAll transactions, allowing theft of 314 NFTs including Bored Apes and Moonbirds.

name: Youbit
description: On December 19, 2017, South Korean exchange Youbit suffered its second breach of the year, losing 17% of total assets (~3,831 BTC equivalent from the first hack in April). Attackers compromised the hot wallet; cold storage remained secure. Korean authorities attributed the attack to BlueNoroff, a Lazarus subgroup. The exchange permanently closed after this incident.

name: TAC Protocol
description: The TON-TAC bridge lacked code-hash verification on jetton wallets. An attacker deployed a counterfeit USD₮ wallet and sent a fraudulent bridge message to receive unbacked minted TAC tokens, draining legitimate locked assets.

name: DoinGud
description: DoinGud’s acceptOffer settlement logic transferred an offer’s USDC price to the caller without deleting or zeroing the consumed offer record. Unlike cancelOffer, the acceptance path omitted the swap-and-pop cleanup. Missing checks also permitted the offerer to accept their own offer and permitted a zero NFT amount. By using amount=0, the attacker avoided listing cleanup and replayed identical acceptOffer calldata, causing the contract to pay the same offer repeatedly. A flash loan supplied the temporary USDC needed to construct the self-funded offer. Independent reporting likewise describes the exploit as failure to clear a bid after acceptance

name: b14g
description: On October 31, 2026, an attacker withdrew approximately 97 million CORE from assets staked through b14g and transferred them to attacker-controlled addresses. The protocol paused the affected contracts and coordinated with security partners and exchanges to trace the stolen funds. Approximately 68 million CORE remained on Core, while exchanges froze another 9 million CORE. BTC staked through b14g was unaffected and remained time-locked on Bitcoin

name: Bithumb
description: On June 19-20, 2018, attackers compromised Bithumb's hot wallet and stole approximately 35,000 ETH and various other tokens worth ~$31M at the time. The attacker's method exploited infrastructure vulnerabilities to gain access to the exchange's online wallet system. Bithumb attributed the attack to Lazarus, the North Korea-linked hacker group.

name: El Dorado Exchange
description: An attacker exploited a closed-source Oracle contract in El Dorado Exchange to manipulate prices and liquidate positions. The attacker extracted approximately $520K but was identified as a white-hat security researcher exposing a price manipulation fraud scheme. After the team admitted code vulnerabilities, the attacker returned over $400K.

name: KyberSwap Elastic
description: On November 22, 2023, KyberSwap Elastic was exploited via a double rounding error in computeSwapStep() that allowed the final swap price to exceed the target threshold without updating liquidity state. The attacker used strategic swaps to corrupt baseL and drain $48M across multiple networks.

name: Seth Green NFTs
description: Actor Seth Green's wallet was compromised via phishing from a cloned Gutter Cat Gang website. Attackers stole multiple NFTs including a Bored Ape with commercial rights to his upcoming TV show. Green recovered the Bored Ape through negotiation.

name: Shoebill Finance
description: On October 30, 2024, Shoebill Finance on BOB Chain was exploited via an oracle misconfiguration during the integration of new solvBTC assets. The vulnerability created an exploitable condition where attackers could borrow funds with minimal collateral. The attacker transferred 19.512 wBTC and 1.597 tBTC across multiple bridges.

name: Zest
description: On April 12, 2024, Zest Protocol on Stacks was exploited during its public launch via collateral list manipulation. An attacker repeated collateral entries to artificially inflate their perceived collateral value, borrowed well beyond their actual holdings, and removed 322K STX (approximately $1M). Zest paused contracts, offered a $100K bounty, and promised treasury-backed reimbursement.

name: MetaPoint
description: MetaPoint was exploited through a public approval function that allowed attackers to transfer all user assets. The attacker created bulk contracts to invoke the unrestricted approve function and drain maximum token amounts from user deposits.

name: Vicuna Lending
description: Vicuna Finance’s S Market and Stablecoin Market were exploited through an oracle manipulation vulnerability, resulting in approximately $700K in losses. The Main Protocol market was unaffected. Following the exploit, Vicuna removed liquidity from the affected submarkets and planned to distribute the remaining assets pro rata to affected users based on their net supplied positions

name: Singularity Finance
description: Singularity Finance on Base exploited for $413K in April 2026 via misconfigured oracle price validation. Attacker manipulated DEX pairs to inflate collateral values.

name: BtcTurk
description: In August 2025, Turkish CEX BtcTurk suffered a second major hack, with $48M drained from hot wallets across 7 blockchains (Ethereum, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Mantle, Polygon) after private keys were compromised.

name: Berally
description: On March 14, 2025, Berally on Berachain suffered a hack when the deployer key was compromised, allowing the attacker to drain all vesting tokens from the liquidity pool. The core dApp contracts remained unaffected.

name: Arcus Perps
description: On November 10, 2026 (UTC), an attacker exploited an accounting flaw in Arcus Perps on Robinhood Chain that allowed transfers between subaccounts to artificially inflate an account's recorded balance. The attacker used the inflated balance to withdraw 2,234,391 USDG, while an additional $3 million in withdrawal requests was blocked by the bridge's rate limit and later reversed. Arcus patched the vulnerability, restricted the exploiter's accounts, and covered the entire shortfall from its company treasury, leaving user balances unaffected

name: Across
description: On November 10, 2026, an attacker compromised Across Protocol's domain through a social engineering attack targeting its registrar, Namecheap, redirecting users to a malicious website designed to steal cryptocurrency through fraudulent wallet interactions. Multiple users reported unauthorized withdrawals after interacting with the compromised interface. Across took its frontend and API offline, worked to block access to the malicious domain, and committed to compensating affected users. The total amount stolen remains undisclosed

name: Aave V3
description: Aave V3 oracle misconfiguration on March 10-12, 2026 caused ~$862K in losses. Chaos Labs' CAPO system reported wstETH at 1.1939 instead of 1.228, triggering liquidations of 34 otherwise-healthy E-Mode positions due to inconsistent snapshot configuration.

name: Iron Finance
description: Iron Finance lost $170,000 when a ValueDefi error inflated farming reward rates by 365x, allowing attackers to drain all SIL rewards from the IRON/SIL and IRON/BUSD pools.

name: BitPoint
description: BitPoint, a Tokyo-based exchange, discovered hot wallet breaches on July 11-12, 2019, losing approximately 3.02B yen (~$27.6M) across multiple assets: 1,225 BTC, 1,985 BCH, 11,169 ETH, and 5,108 LTC. Of the loss, $23M belonged to customers and $9.2M to BitPoint itself. The exchange later recovered ~$2.3M in stolen cryptocurrency from overseas exchanges and reimbursed customers before resuming operations.

name: WEMIX.FI Lend
description: On July 26, 2026, an attacker obtained administrative control of the WEMIX$ stablecoin contract and minted 5.23M counterfeit WEMIX$ tokens. These were swapped for real WEMIX and USDC.e and dispersed across Ethereum and BNB Chain. The total exploit was estimated at $6.25M.

name: ElephantStatus
description: ElephantStatus was exploited via a flashloan-funded price manipulation attack. The attacker borrowed BUSD, swapped for WBNB, and manipulated the liquidity pool to artificially inflate WBNB price, enabling unintended extraction of value.

name: Bisq
description: Bisq v1 was exploited via missing validation on negative miner fee values in trade protocol. Modified client allowed attacker to pull value from multisig outputs; ~11 BTC stolen from 10 users. Bisq v2 and Easy unaffected.

name: Impossible Finance
description: Impossible Finance was attacked via flash loan when an attacker created a fake token (AAA/BBB) to manipulate liquidity pool prices. The attacker extracted 229.84 ETH (~$500K) through multiple swaps at artificial prices.

name: Astroport
description: Neutron governance proposal 9 contained MsgUpdateAdmin messages that reassigned administration of Astroport contracts despite those contracts previously being administered by Astroport’s own governance contract. After the proposal passed, the attacker migrated Astroport Staking and six Astroport pair contracts to attacker-uploaded code containing a withdraw_all entry point and swept their balances. The attack did not exploit Astroport’s swap or pool logic

name: DOGGO
description: DOGGO had a business logic flaw in its withdrawal mechanism where an incorrect formula or missing state update allowed attackers to withdraw more funds than their actual share of the contract.

name: Starlay Finance
description: An improper liquidity index computation in the Starlay USDC lending pool on Acala EVM allowed attackers to withdraw far more than their deposits. The rounding issue in the index calculation enabled the exploit.

name: Gala
description: Gala Games minter private key was compromised on May 20, 2024, allowing minting of 5B GALA tokens (~$200M). The unused and unrotated key was likely stolen; attacker sold ~$200M before returning $22M (~11% recovery).

name: Bittensor
description: Bittensor suffered an $8M hack on July 2, 2024 via a supply chain attack. The PyPI package v6.12.2 was compromised with malware that stole coldkeys when users initiated staking, delegation, or transfer operations.

name: Poly Network
description: Poly Network was exploited for $611M on August 10, 2021 across Ethereum ($273M), BSC ($253M) and Polygon ($85M) via an access control and cryptography vulnerability in cross-chain bridge contracts. The attacker voluntarily returned nearly all funds within 15 days, keeping only transaction fees.

name: Hifi Finance
description: An attacker acquired HIFI governance tokens and used four coordinated votes shortly before voting closed to pass a malicious governance proposal. Proposal 21 would upgrade Hifi’s BalanceSheet contract to introduce a function that incorrectly treats existing collateral as untracked funds, allowing it to be transferred to an attacker-controlled Safe. The proposal would also mint 25 million HIFI tokens to the attacker. At the time of reporting, the proposal was queued but had not been executed

name: Sturdy V1
description: On June 12, 2023, Sturdy Finance was drained of ~$800K via a flashloan-funded read-only reentrancy attack on Balancer pools during oracle checks, inflating B-stETH-STABLE prices.

name: Pine Protocol
description: Pine Protocol was exploited via a flaw where old and new contract versions shared the same liquidity pools. An attacker used this to borrow NFT collateral from the new pool while recording repayment as a flash loan, allowing them to drain vault assets repeatedly across multiple transactions.

name: uniclyNFT
description: A reentrancy vulnerability in uniclyNFT's PointFarm contract allowed an attacker to repeatedly call the deposit() function without proper state updates. The attacker minted rewards multiple times before the contract could update rewardDebt, draining uJENNY tokens through reentrancy into external calls.

name: Revert Lend
description: Revert Lend's Aerodrome Lend vault on Base was exploited on January 29-30, 2026 for $50,101 when missing validation allowed withdrawal of collateral that was still backing an active loan.

name: Coinbase
description: Coinbase's corporate DEX wallet lost $300,000 on August 13, 2025 when MEV bots exploited misconfigured token approvals granted to a 0x protocol swapper contract.

name: Lien
description: On July 23-24, 2026, Lien Finance on Ethereum suffered a $542,000 exploit when an attacker bypassed the burn-before-swap logic in the GeneralizedDotc contract. The attacker minted unbacked bond tokens and swapped them for USDC from OTC pools.

name: Fegex
description: FEG's SmartBridge was drained for ~$1.3M across Ethereum, BSC and Base. The attacker forged Wormhole messages from an unauthorized chain that the relayer accepted as withdrawal requests without verifying the emitter's authority, marking the third major FEG incident.

name: Humanity
description: Humanity Protocol's admin wallets were drained of $32M and 447M H tokens were unauthorized minted after a Humanity Foundation member's private key was compromised.

name: Uniswap V1
description: An attacker exploited a reentrancy vulnerability in Uniswap V1's imBTC liquidity pool using ERC777's callback mechanism. By calling deposit, triggering the ERC777 callback before balance updates, and immediately withdrawing, the attacker could drain tokens from the pool at artificial prices. The Consensys team had discovered the vulnerability in 2019 but no exploitable ERC777 token existed until imBTC launched.

name: Alkimiya
description: Alkimiya's SilicaPools contract unsafely downcast shares from uint256 to uint128 in the collateralizedMint function. An attacker used a flash loan to manipulate the truncated shares value, causing the contract to believe it had issued fewer shares than it actually had and allowing redemption of more collateral than deposited.

name: KuCoin
description: KuCoin's official X (Twitter) account was hijacked for approximately 45 minutes on April 24. Scammers used the compromised account to promote a fraudulent giveaway, tricking users into sending BTC and ETH to a fake address.
