Users lost approximately $22,628 before KuCoin regained control and announced full reimbursement for verified losses.

name: Sperax USD
description: On February 3, 2023, an attacker exploited a bug in the SperaxUSD token contract by pre-computing a Gnosis Safe address and sending 11 USDs to it. When the Safe was created, this triggered an overflow in the balance calculation, allowing the attacker to mint 9.7 billion unbacked USDs and exchange approximately $250K worth before the contract was paused.

name: ALEX
description: On June 6, 2025, ALEX Protocol suffered an $8.37M exploit. Attacker deployed a malicious token with custom transfer logic, used it to spoof as-contract origin and masquerade as the vault, draining 8.4M STX, 21.85 sBTC, and stablecoins due to failed access control verification.

name: UEarnPool
description: UEarnPool on BSC was exploited using a flash loan to repeatedly manipulate the invitor reward distribution mechanism. The attacker inflated their staked ratio by calling the public bindInvitor() function multiple times, allowing the protocol to allocate portions of staked amounts to controlled invitor accounts. Each staking round distributed rewards while allocating the claimable reward back to the attacker.

name: HTX
description: On September 25, 2023, HTX's hot wallet was drained of 5,000 ETH (~$8 million). The attacker gained unauthorized access to internal wallet infrastructure via private key compromise; the attacker returned all funds on October 7, 2023, claiming a 250 ETH white-hat bounty.

name: Oraichain
description: On August 8, 2026, the Oraichain network was exploited via an unbacked cross-chain mint, allowing tokens to be minted without matching collateral on the origin chain. Flagged by the Oraichain team; the loss amount was not disclosed and no dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: RetoSwap
description: RetoSwap (Haveno protocol) on Monero was exploited on June 16-17, 2026 (second incident in 30 days) when dispute resolution logic permitted fund release without proper two-way settlement. Attacker took buy offers, forced arbitration, and released XMR after Bitcoin confirmations without sending BTC.

name: Amun
description: An attacker gained control of Amun's unprotected rebalance manager, rebalanced PECO and DFI indices into a worthless token it controlled, and minted roughly 80 billion tokens to dump on DEXs, causing about $300K in losses.

name: CoinEx
description: CoinEx exchange suffered multi-chain attack on September 12, 2023 when attackers accessed hot wallet private keys, draining $31-54M across Ethereum, Tron, Polygon, and other chains.

name: Biswap
description: Biswap's V3 Migrator contract lacked proper access control and parameter validation when migrating liquidity from V2 to V3. An attacker exploited this to call the migrator contract and steal funds from liquidity providers who had authorized their LP tokens.

name: Venus Core Pool
description: On March 29, 2025 Venus Core Pool on zkSync Era suffered a donation attack when an attacker directly transferred tokens to the cToken contract, distorting exchange rates and accumulator calculations and bypassing collateral accounting and supply cap logic, resulting in $902,000 in losses and bad debt.

name: Abracadabra Spell
description: On October 4, 2025 Abracadabra Money on Ethereum suffered a critical exploit of the cook() multi-action function where improper state handling allowed attackers to bypass solvency checks: Action 5 set needsSolvencyCheck=true, but Action 0 reset the CookStatus, enabling under-collateralized borrowing and withdrawal of 1.79 million MIM tokens.

name: Sovryn Dex
description: On November 1, 2026, an attacker exploited Sovryn's XUSD/WRBTC AMM pool on Rootstock, receiving approximately 541,456 XUSD ($538,749) in an attacker-controlled wallet. Portions of the proceeds were subsequently converted into BTC and ETH, while other assets remained under protocol control. Sovryn implemented emergency fee-control changes, delisted the affected pool on November 2, and began reconciling the impact on liquidity providers. The underlying vulnerability and final realized losses remain under investigation

name: Mixin Network
description: On September 23, 2023, Mixin Network suffered a $200M hack when a cloud service provider's database containing hot wallet credentials was breached, allowing attackers to drain wallets of ETH, BTC, and USDT.

name: WaultSwap
description: On August 4, 2021, WaultSwap was exploited when an attacker manipulated the $WUSD pegging mechanism by repeatedly staking USDT to artificially increase the $WEX price in the USDT-WEX liquidity pool, then swapping $WEX back to $USDT for profit, extracting approximately $930K.

name: AutoShark
description: In May 2021, AutoShark Finance on BSC was exploited for ~$822,800 via flashloan attack. The attacker flash-loaned BNB to manipulate the SHARK-BNB pool, donated tokens directly into SharkMinter to inflate reward calculations, and dumped newly minted SHARK through 1inch and AnySwap.

name: SpankChain
description: SpankChain payment channel hub was exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability on October 6, 2018. An attacker created a malicious token contract masquerading as an ERC20, with a transfer function that called back into the payment channel contract multiple times, draining approximately 165.38 ETH (~$38,000). The attacker returned the stolen funds after negotiation.

name: Ara Finance
description: On June 18-19, 2023, an attacker exploited Ara Finance's unrestricted swap contract by flash-loaning 1.202 million USDT on BNB Chain. The contract lacked access control and held unbounded ARA and USDT approvals, allowing the attacker to steal ~$124,915.

name: Bitcoinica
description: Bitcoinica's production servers were compromised, allowing attackers to steal 18,547 BTC from the exchange's online wallet. The attacker gained access to the wallet infrastructure through a breach of the hosting provider.

name: DualPools
description: A precision truncation vulnerability in DualPools' share calculation allowed attackers to exchange 1.9999... dLINK for massive amounts of LINK by exploiting data truncation to 1 unit. Attackers then drained pools of WBNB, BTC, ETH, ADA, and BUSD.

name: Fluid Lending
description: An attacker compromised operational keys used exclusively by Fluid’s Merkle rewards distribution infrastructure. The attacker used these permissions to submit and approve fraudulent reward allocations, allowing them to claim approximately 125,109 FLUID, 51,946 GHO, and a small amount of cbBTC. The incident was isolated to reward distribution contracts and did not compromise Fluid’s core protocol contracts, lending markets, or user deposits

name: Banana Gun
description: On September 19, 2024, Banana Gun's Telegram message oracle validation failure allowed attackers to forge transfer authorizations and drain $3M from 11 users' wallets. All users were reimbursed from the treasury.

name: swapX
description: swapX on BSC was exploited through a lack of access control in the 0x4f1f05bc function. The attacker repeatedly called this function to manipulate DND token prices and drain approximately $1M from user wallets that had approved the contract.

name: CIVNFT
description: CIVNFT smart contract shipped fund-transfer functions with zero access control. An attacker exploited this to initiate callback functions that transferred CIV and USDT funds to Uniswap for liquidation.

name: PolyYeld Finance
description: On July 28, 2021, PolyYeld Finance was exploited when attackers discovered that the Masterchef contract could not properly handle xYELD's transfer tax reward distribution system. Attackers minted approximately 4.995 billion YELD tokens and converted 4% of them to ~123 ETH (~$250K) before the token crashed 100%.

name: MetaWin
description: On November 4, 2024, MetaWin casino's hot wallets on Ethereum and Solana were compromised, draining approximately $4.4M. The vulnerability was in the platform's frictionless withdrawal system. The attacker was tracked across 115 addresses and moved stolen funds through KuCoin and HitBTC. MetaWin restored 95% of user withdrawals.

name: BingX
description: On September 20, 2024 (4:00 AM Singapore time), BingX hot wallets were compromised via access control bypass, draining ~$43M in two separate transactions: $26M + $16.5M. Assets stolen included 13.25M ETH, 2.3M BNB, 4.4M USDT, and 360+ altcoin types. BingX promised reimbursement from reserves.

name: Virtue
description: An attacker exploited Switchboard’s IOTA guardian-attestation design to replace the signing keys of all 14 production oracles and submit arbitrary IOTA prices. The attacker first inflated IOTA to $10M, allowing 4.94M unbacked VUSD to be minted against 1.027 IOTA, then crashed the reported price to trigger liquidations of healthy positions. By pre-positioning the freshly minted VUSD in Virtue’s Stability Pool, the attacker captured 16.72M IOTA-equivalent of collateral from the manipulated liquidations

name: BearnFi
description: BearnFi's BvaultsBank contract interpreted deposit amounts inconsistently between BUSD and ibBUSD. Attackers exploited this via flashloan cycles to inflate withdrawal amounts.

name: Ronin Bridge
description: On March 23, 2022 the Ronin Network bridge (connecting Axie Infinity sidechain to Ethereum) suffered the largest cryptocurrency theft in history when attackers compromised validator node private keys, gaining control of 5 of 9 validators and using the majority to approve fraudulent withdrawals of 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC ($624M total). The breach was discovered six days later on March 29.

name: Utopia
description: Utopia token on BSC was exploited via a business logic flaw in its swap or price calculation mechanism. The attacker exploited the broken logic to extract 492 BNB from the protocol.

name: Tales of Elleria
description: Tales of Elleria's bridge contract on Arbitrum was exploited on April 20. An attacker forged bridge signatures and minted 5 billion ELM tokens, then drained the associated liquidity pool. Approximately 140 ETH (~$280K) was extracted from the LP before the attack was detected. The project froze operations and announced plans to compensate affected users through an airdrop mechanism.

name: Huma
description: Huma Finance's deprecated V1 BaseCreditPool contracts on Polygon were exploited via a credit-lifecycle logic error combined with unrestricted access control. An attacker created Requested credit records through an open requestCredit() path with preApproved=false, then advanced those unapproved records to GoodStanding using an unrestricted refreshAccount() call. The attacker then exploited drawdown() to borrow the pools' residual balances.

name: Shido
description: Shido on BNB Chain suffered an exploit on June 23, 2023 due to a configuration error. The attack resulted in the loss of approximately 976 BNB worth ~$238.5K at the time of exploit.

name: TUR Staking
description: On March 26, 2026, the TUR staking protocol on BSC was exploited via a spot price manipulation attack. The attacker manipulated the TUR-NOBEL liquidity pool to artificially inflate the spot price, then used this inflated price to trigger oversized reward calculations in the staking contract. The attacker claimed amplified rewards through a referral account and profited approximately $133K by swapping the stolen TUR for USDT.

name: CrossCurve
description: CrossCurve's ReceiverAxelar contract failed to validate message origin, letting attackers forge cross-chain messages. Attackers crafted messages to release tokens without offsetting deposits on other chains, draining $3M across multiple blockchains.

name: CREAM Lending
description: On October 27, 2021, CREAM Finance was exploited for $130 million via flashloan-enabled oracle manipulation. Attacker used flashloans from MakerDAO and Aave to manipulate yUSD price, then minted unbacked yUSD and crYUSD by exploiting vault accounting and composability across Curve and Aave.

name: Avici
description: A vulnerability in a version of Rain’s Solana card contract used by Avici allowed unauthorized withdrawals from the contract holding users’ card balances. Avici reported that 1,685 users were affected for $500,859.22. The vulnerable contract was subsequently upgraded across all affected programs

name: Bonfire
description: BonfireSwap’s public transfer path accepted a caller-supplied token owner address and passed it as the from address to BONFIRE’s transferFrom without verifying that the caller was that owner or otherwise authorized by the owner. Because BONFIRE saw BonfireSwap itself as msg.sender, existing victim-to-BonfireSwap allowances authorized the transfers. The attacker repeatedly selected wallets with standing approvals, transferred their BONFIRE into the BONFIRE/WBNB PancakeSwap pair, and used the router’s public skim path to collect the resulting excess before selling the harvested BONFIRE for BNB. No private key, admin privilege, flash loan, or PancakeSwap invariant failure was required

name: FlashLoopAdapter
description: FlashLoopAdapter’s open()/close() authorization trusted any caller whose isModuleEnabled() response returned true, allowing an attacker-controlled fake Safe to pass the check. The attacker then supplied each real victim Safe as swapRouter and encoded execTransactionFromModule(...) as arbitrary swapCalldata. Because FlashLoopAdapter was already an enabled module on those Safes, they accepted the calls and transferred or withdrew collateral to the attacker

name: Initia
description: Initia suffered a security incident involving the unauthorized minting of multiple assets on its L1. The attacker reportedly transferred and converted some of the minted assets into Ethereum-based holdings. Initia halted its L1 and rollups while investigating the vulnerability and coordinating with validators, exchanges, and security teams

name: Venus Protocol
description: An attacker manipulated XVS spot price via low liquidity on centralized exchanges, driving it from $70 to $143 and back to $76. Using inflated XVS collateral, they borrowed 2,000 BTC and 5,700 ETH. Liquidations cascaded as borrowers defaulted, and Venus absorbed 100M+ USD in bad debt.

name: ToBet
description: ToBet gambling platform was exploited on December 19, 2018 via a rollback attack using EOS's blacklist feature. Attackers rolled back losing wagers to their original states, extracting value from the platform. This was part of a coordinated attack against multiple EOS DApps.

name: Mure
description: Mure's MureDistribution proxy on Ethereum was drained in a single transaction on 21 May 2026 after a caller-controlled signer address was passed to SignatureChecker, causing it to fall through to the ERC-1271 path and return true for a forged signature. This authorized transferFrom of 4.85M QUEST tokens pre-approved to the proxy, which sold for ~5.45 ETH (~$11.7K).

name: Ploutos Money
description: Ploutos Money oracle misconfigured to use BTC/USD feed for USDC pricing. Attacker borrowed 187 ETH by depositing only 8 USDC (~10^12x discrepancy), exploiting the misconfiguration within one block.

name: Crypto Burger
description: On January 16-17, 2022, the CryptoBurgers play-to-earn game was exploited when the BURG token's burn function lacked access control, allowing attackers to burn tokens from the PancakeSwap liquidity pool to manipulate prices. Using flashloans, two attackers drained approximately $700K-$770K in BNB from the protocol by exploiting the unprotected burn mechanism.

name: Flooring Protocol
description: Flooring Protocol was exploited on June 8, 2026 via a packed storage and token-indexing vulnerability in its DN404/BT404 implementation. Attacker deposited small WETH to mint near-infinite fpToken balances, draining multiple NFT pools. Yuga Labs white hats rescued 68 blue-chip NFTs ($500K+) including 29 BAYC, 4 Mutant Apes and 2 CryptoPunks.

name: Ostium
description: On July 15, 2026, Ostium perpetuals DEX on Arbitrum suffered a $23.75M exploit when an attacker used a compromised price oracle private key to sign fraudulent Bitcoin price reports ($5,000 vs. real ~$60,000), opening positions at fake prices and closing at market rates.

name: OTSea
description: OTSea's staking contract had a logical defect in reward calculation and state tracking that allowed attackers to manipulate reward variables and continuously withdraw staking rewards beyond their actual stake.

name: Midas Capital
description: On January 15-17, 2023 Midas Capital's Jarvis Polygon pool was exploited via a flashloan-enabled reentrancy attack targeting a recently-added collateral token, draining $660,000 of MATIC. Midas reached out with a bug-bounty offer and contributed $1,000 USDC weekly for 52 weeks toward affected protocols and users.

name: INK Finance
description: INK Finance's Workspace Treasury Proxy on Polygon was exploited on May 11, 2026 for $140K USDT. Attacker deployed a malicious contract matching a whitelisted claimer address to bypass authorization checks and trigger unauthorized treasury transfers, facilitated by a $25K flash loan.

name: DAO Maker Vesting
description: DAO Maker's vesting system was exploited when the init() function lacked access control, allowing an attacker to reset parameters on 4 token contracts (DERC, CPD, CAPS, SHO) and drain tokens via emergencyExit. Stolen tokens were swapped on DEXes, causing significant price impact.

name: Ethereum Alarm Clock
description: On October 20, 2022, Ethereum Alarm Clock's transaction scheduling protocol was exploited via a gas fee refund calculation vulnerability where the cancel() function calculated refunds too high when given inflated transaction fees, allowing attackers to call cancel with high gas prices and extract approximately 204 ETH (~$260K) in overpaid refunds.

name: X319
description: On November 9, 2024, the X319 contract on BNB Chain was exploited through an access control vulnerability, resulting in approximately $12.9K in losses.

name: ZongZiFa
description: ZongZiFa token exploit where the attacker artificially inflated token price to profit from the protocol's invitation-reward mechanism, netting approximately 391 WBNB.

name: Rivus DAO
description: Rivus DAO's Bittensor liquid-staking protocol was drained when a contracted developer inserted a backdoor in the migration contract. The team recovered funds using the developer's identity documents. Rivus relaunched on October 1, 2024.

name: EvoDefi
description: A design flaw in EvoDefi's MasterChef fork allowed attackers to arbitrage reward distribution by exploiting an incorrect update logic that failed to deduct minted rewards. The vulnerability allowed repeated reward claims without proper accounting.

name: Platypus Finance
description: On October 12, 2023, Platypus Finance on Avalanche was exploited via three flashloan transactions totaling ~$2.2-2.23M. Attackers manipulated swap prices by altering slippage calculations across multiple liquidity pools, then draining value from the protocol.

name: MangoFarmSol
description: On January 6-7, 2024, MangoFarmSOL on Solana was revealed as an intentional rugpull. The frontend and smart contract were malicious drainers that extracted all wallet tokens from users who approved transfers. The team deleted all social media and vanished.

name: NFTG
description: On November 26, 2024, the NFTG protocol on BNB Chain suffered an access control vulnerability that allowed unauthorized fund extraction. The vulnerability was in the contract's access controls, permitting unauthorized callers to drain approximately $10K.

name: Clober Liquidity Vault
description: On December 10, 2024, Clober Liquidity Vault on Base was exploited for ~$501K via reentrancy in the Rebalancer contract's _burn function. The attacker used a malicious contract and 267.4 ETH flashloan to execute repeated state reads before balance updates.

name: zkFinance
description: No credible sources found documenting a zkFinance hack on November 11, 2024, or proximate dates on zkSync Era.

name: Safe Dollar
description: On June 28, 2021, SafeDollar's staking pool on Polygon was exploited via incompatibility with deflationary tokens. The attacker used flash-loaned PLX to deplete the contract's actual balance to ~2 tokens while maintaining inflated deposit records, causing the reward formula to mint massive SDO amounts. These were sold for ~$248K in USDC and USDT.

name: Ethscriptions
description: A vulnerability in the Ethscriptions.com marketplace smart contract allowed unauthorized withdrawals. The contract contained code that permitted users to withdraw Ethscriptions they didn't own, resulting in ~202 inscriptions stolen across ~123 addresses.

name: Aztec Bridge
description: Aztec's private rollup bridge escape-hatch mechanism was exploited via incomplete proof validation, allowing an attacker to manipulate proof data and withdraw 1,158 ETH, 150,000 DAI, and ~0.47 renBTC. This was the second Aztec exploit in June 2026; the June 14 attack drained ~$2.1M via similar proof manipulation.

name: Earning.Farm
description: EFLeverVault, a key component of Earning.Farm, was targeted with flash loan attacks on October 15, 2022. The contract failed to verify the origin of flashloan callbacks, allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate protocol calls and execute unauthorized ETH withdrawals from the collateral pool.

name: SEA Token
description: Suspicious attack on Arbitrum drained ~$153K from SEA token interactions; suspected price oracle or liquidity manipulation but mechanism unconfirmed pending technical analysis.

name: Moonwell Lending
description: Moonwell Lending on Base suffered a $1.78M loss when AI-generated code misconfigured the cbETH oracle to price it at $1.12 instead of nearly $2,200, failing to multiply the exchange rate by the price feed. This enabled abnormal liquidations and borrowing.

name: Build Finance
description: Build Finance DAO suffered a governance takeover when an attacker submitted a proposal to grant themselves minting and treasury controls. Low participation allowed the malicious proposal to pass unnoticed. The attacker minted 1.1 billion BUILD tokens, drained liquidity pools on Uniswap and Balancer, and stole 130,000 METRIC tokens from the treasury, ultimately extracting 160 ETH.

name: Surf Lending
description: A machine with access to Surf Lending’s admin key was compromised. According to Surf’s lead developer, the incident was not caused by a smart-contract bug. Surf placed the protocol into maintenance mode, temporarily migrated user vaults and supplied assets to its multisig treasury wallet, and began migrating the V1 contracts while rebuilding the affected infrastructure in a more secure environment. Surf subsequently described the event as a security incident and prioritized restoring V1

name: NOVAToken
description: NOVAToken on BSC was rugged through malicious unlimited minting. The admin used their privileged access to mint unlimited tokens and drain value from the protocol.

name: Punk Protocol
description: On August 10, 2021, Punk Protocol was exploited for $8.95M when attacker used delegatecall to rerun unguarded Initialize function, changing forge address to gain withdrawal control. White-hat frontran and recovered ~$5M, keeping $1M as finder's fee.

name: Chi Protocol
description: Chi Protocol exploited on July 13, 2026 for ~$8.5K. Attacker flash-loaned 5 WETH, bought depegged USC from a thin Uniswap V2 pool, and burned it against the ReserveHolder. The burn() function assumed a $1 peg without checking, redeeming full-value collateral.

name: Tender Finance
description: Tender Finance on Arbitrum exploited March 7, 2023 for $1.59M via misconfigured GMX oracle. Attacker borrowed using only 1 GMX token (~$70 collateral). White-hat negotiated return for $97K bounty.

name: Hyperdrive HL Lending
description: On September 27, 2025 Hyperdrive (lending protocol on Hyperliquid L1) lost approximately $782,000 to an exploit where attackers exploited an arbitrary router call vulnerability, making repeated withdrawals from the Primary USDT0 Market and Treasury USDT Market and extracting ~673,000 USDT0 and 110,244 thBILL, with stolen funds bridged to Ethereum ($494k) and BNB Chain ($279k).

name: MAAT Protocol
description: MAAT Protocol's withdrawal logic had a critical edge case where not all shares were burned during withdrawals from the BSC Stargate strategy. This left 1 wei of shares in the contract, allowing third-party addresses to call redeem with minimal share input and drain funds without consuming shares.

name: Bodega Market
description: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Bodega Market’s prediction-market contracts to drain rewards and market seed funds. The team associated the exploit with a transaction involving an M-EVIL_ORACLE token, but has not yet disclosed the underlying vulnerability or explained how that token enabled the drain. Because the exploit mechanism remains under investigation, the precise root cause is not yet confirmed

name: BurgerSwap
description: BurgerSwap exploited May 28, 2021 for $7.2M in BURGER, WBNB, and USDC. Missing code line in Uniswap V2 fork enabled reentrancy. Attacker created a fake token to manipulate price, then executed profitable swaps funded by a PancakeSwap flashloan.

name: Opyn
description: The Opyn ETH Put contract had a critical bug in its exercise function: msg.value was checked inside a loop but only the first batch of ETH was actually received. Attackers called exercise() with multiple vaults in a single transaction, reusing the same ETH batch to withdraw collateral multiple times.

name: Edel
description: On June 30, 2026, Edel Finance's xStock lending protocol was exploited via flash loan-enabled oracle manipulation. The attacker manipulated the wGOOGLx (tokenized Google shares) exchange rate, inflating collateral value by ~7,700% due to a missing price oracle fallback, allowing extraction of $403K in bad debt.

name: MBC & ZZSH
description: MBC and ZZSH tokens on BSC suffered access control vulnerabilities combined with business logic flaws. Attackers exploited improper permission checks to drain protocol funds.

name: FilDA
description: An attacker manipulated token pricing used by FilDA’s Glide LP price oracle on Elastos Smart Chain, allowing the attacker to exploit distorted asset valuations and drain more than 140,000 ELA and 5,800 USDC from the lending protocol. FilDA subsequently suspended its ESC deployment and announced that it would permanently shut it down

name: AFI Protocol
description: On 30 May 2026 the afiUSD vault of AFI Protocol, a proof-of-reserve and yield-vault platform for RWAs on Ethereum, was drained of approximately $480,000. AFI paused the affected vault within hours, rotated operational keys across the platform, and reported that its other vaults and the remaining ~$225M TVL were unaffected. The attacker swapped ~$252k DAI to ETH and sent ~150 ETH through Tornado Cash. AFI has not published the exploit path.

name: Ribbon
description: On June 24, 2022, Ribbon Finance suffered a similar DNS hijacking attack that same week, likely using similar methodology as the Convex attack. Users were redirected to a phishing site and tricked into approving malicious contracts, resulting in limited token losses and a mass withdrawal from the protocol.

name: Transit Finance
description: On May 12, 2026, Transit Finance on Tron was exploited for $1.88M via deprecated contract officially discontinued in 2022 but left active on-chain. Attacker exploited historical vulnerabilities to drain DAI and other assets.

name: Revert Finance
description: Revert Finance's V3Utils contract was exploited through an access control vulnerability allowing arbitrary code execution. Attackers transferred approved user funds by executing unauthorized contract calls, stealing approximately $29K before the team deployed a refund bot to recover all victim funds.

name: Omnipus
description: On September 11, 2024, Omnipus presale contracts were exploited for approximately $30,000 when a commented-out check in OAppSender.sol's payNative() function allowed attackers to bypass validation. The contract mistakenly refunded ETH to attackers who claimed overpayment, enabling unauthorized fund extraction.

name: Myriad Markets
description: An attacker exploited a previously exposed private key belonging to Myriad’s automated market management wallet. The key had reportedly been leaked through a vulnerability in a third-party library used by a backend service. The attacker used the wallet’s privileges to manipulate positions and force incorrect resolutions across 10 prediction markets on BNB Chain. Myriad revoked the wallet’s permissions, secured the remaining funds, and announced that all affected markets would be voided and users refunded

name: RuggedArt
description: A reentrancy vulnerability in the RuggedArt contract allowed attackers to manipulate contract state during transaction execution and drain funds through unsafe external calls.

name: PrismaLST
description: Prisma Finance was exploited on March 28, 2024 via a flash loan attack on MigrateTroveZap. The onFlashLoan callback lacked origin validation, allowing the attacker to spoof migration logic and hijack troves, extracting 3,257.69 ETH (~$11.6M) in collateral.

name: AutoShark
description: Attacker exploited AutoShark's swap mining reward calculation using large-volume trades via flash loan. By performing multiple swaps in a single block to accumulate 3.18M FINS tokens, the attacker bypassed the single-transaction mitigation measures that AutoShark had previously deployed after an earlier attack.

name: Binance CEX
description: On May 7, 2019, Binance's hot wallet private keys were compromised, resulting in theft of 7,000 bitcoin (~$40 million). The exchange halted transactions for one week and reimbursed all affected customers from its insurance fund.

name: OpenSea
description: OpenSea's listing system contained a bug where transferred NFTs remained listed on the marketplace via the API despite appearing delisted. Attackers exploited this to purchase previously thought-delisted NFTs at old, far below-market prices and immediately resold them for profit. Three attackers collectively extracted over $1M by buying popular NFTs like Bored Ape Yacht Club at historical listing prices.

name: BlueMove DEX
description: BlueMove DEX's liquidity pools were drained on July 11, 2026 totaling 700K+ SUI ($500K-700K) via either an LP token double-minting mechanism introduced in a May 31 upgrade or an arithmetic overflow in the legacy AMM code. BlueMove announced shutdown and promised compensation.

name: AIDC
description: On June 28, 2026, AIDC's _sellTransfer() accumulated a 30% burn without deducting it from the seller. An attacker exploited this to withdraw from the PancakeSwap LP at inflated rates, stealing ~$121K.

name: BonqDAO
description: On February 1, 2023, BonqDAO's collateral pricing read directly from TellorFlex's last reported value with no TWAP, dispute delay, or bounds. An attacker staked 10 TRB to become a reporter, posted an arbitrary wALBT price, minted ~98.65M BEUR against near-worthless collateral, then reversed the price to liquidate other troves. Nominal damage was ~$120M but illiquidity capped realized gains to ~$1-2M.

name: JUDAO
description: On April 28, 2026, JUDAO was exploited on BSC via a double-sync bug in the token transfer hook that miscalculated pool balances. The attacker used a Moolah flash loan (2.3M USDT) to manipulate pricing and sell JUDAO at artificially inflated prices.

name: SashimiSwap
description: SashimiSwap was exploited via improper swap and router architectural design. An attacker used a 400 ETH flash loan to create fraudulent token pairings with liquidity, then exploited the UniswapRouter contract's swap logic to extract value. The attack was initiated on December 30, 2021 at 09:06 UTC, resulting in approximately $210K in losses.

name: Sonic ICP
description: Sonic DEX, a decentralized exchange on Internet Computer, suffered an exploit involving transaction atomicity failures during asynchronous canister execution. The attacker submitted coordinated, high-frequency requests that exploited race conditions during intermediate state transitions, allowing unauthorized withdrawals before the protocol completed reconciliation. The attack affected 26 liquidity pools and resulted in approximately $276,000 in losses. Sonic paused the protocol and began implementing changes to prevent similar state inconsistencies

name: Purrlend
description: Purrlend's 2-of-3 admin multisig was compromised on HyperEVM and MegaETH, allowing attackers to assign themselves the bridge role and inherit elevated permissions to drain liquidity pools.

name: Set Protocol
description: ETHMACOAPY’s actualizeFee() rounded redemption backing upward even when no fee was payable. Attackers donated collateral to trigger recalculation, temporarily acquired Set tokens, then redeemed them for more collateral than they contributed, with the difference coming from existing holders’ backing. Two separate EOAs repeated the process across two transactions, draining approximately 8.11 WETH

name: Blend Pools V2
description: On February 22, 2026, an attacker pumped Stellar's thin USTRY market from ~$1.06 to ~$106.74, inflating collateral values. Two transactions drained $10.97M (1M USDC + 61M XLM) from YieldBlox DAO's Blend V2 lending pool, exploiting the lack of liquidity checks and anomaly detection in the oracle.

name: Convergence
description: On August 1, 2024, Convergence Finance lost $212K worth of CVG tokens when input validation was missing from the claimMultipleStaking function. The attacker passed an arbitrary malicious contract address to mint 58 million CVG tokens directly, then converted them to 60 WETH and 15.9K crvFRAX.

name: Binance CEX
description: On October 29, attackers exploited Binance’s operational infrastructure to execute unauthorized withdrawals across multiple blockchains, resulting in approximately $6.3 billion in losses. Binance’s preliminary investigation identified a potentially compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that allowed access to a service container, with no evidence of wallet private key leakage. Approximately $3 billion in stolen assets were later frozen with help from industry partners. Binance committed to covering all losses using its SAFU fund and company reserves

name: ChiSale
description: On November 7, 2024, ChiSale on Ethereum was exploited through a logic flaw in its contract implementation, resulting in approximately $16.3K in losses.

name: Hinkal
description: Attackers exploited deprecated note format in Hinkal's shielded-pool, performing unauthorized proofless deposits and bypassing proof verification for withdrawals. Attack was isolated to Ethereum.

name: EOSBet
description: EOSBet gaming platform was attacked on October 15, 2018 using a forged transfer notification exploit. Attackers leveraged the fake transfer notification vulnerability to drain funds from the contract. This was the second major hack of EOSBet within a month, with this incident resulting in losses of approximately $338,000.

name: Conic Finance
description: On July 21-22, 2023, Conic Finance suffered two exploits via read-only reentrancy in CurveLPOracleV2. Attackers manipulated perceived prices to drain $3.26 million from the ETH omnipool; a second exploit of $300K occurred shortly after.

name: Seneca
description: Seneca Protocol's Chamber contract was exploited on February 28, 2024 via improper token approval handling that allowed unauthorized transfers of ~1,900 ETH and 50,000 senUSD. The attacker later returned 80% of funds after being offered a 20% bounty.

name: Sweat Foundation
description: On April 29, 2026, an attacker exploited a logic flaw in the SWEAT token contract on NEAR Protocol, draining 13.71B SWEAT tokens (~$3.5M) from foundation wallets within 30 seconds via a malicious drain contract. Stolen tokens were quickly liquidated via MEXC and Rhea Finance; Sweat Foundation patched the contract and restored all external user balances.

name: Balancer V2
description: Balancer's DNS was hijacked and redirected users to phishing frontend, stealing ~$238K from users. Smart contracts were unaffected; only DNS infrastructure was compromised.

name: Crema Finance
description: On July 2, 2022, Crema Finance's Solana protocol was exploited when an attacker bypassed owner verification on tick accounts used for fee calculations. The attacker created a fraudulent tick account, obtained a flashloan from Solend, added liquidity to the CLMM pool, and exploited the manipulated pricing to drain $8.78M (69,500 SOL + $6.5M stablecoins).

name: Mars Perps
description: On December 14, 2025, Mars Protocol's Perps market on Neutron was exploited for ~$973K via skew-based pricing arbitrage. The attacker executed the same-block arbitrage pattern 15 times, exploiting that funding rates were only applied between blocks rather than within them, eliminating downside risk.

name: Mosca
description: Mosca is an on-chain MLM/membership program where users join by depositing USDT, BUSD, or USDC for internal credits to withdraw later. The exitProgram function had incomplete state resets—only user.balance was zeroed after withdrawal but not user.balanceUSDT and user.balanceUSDC, enabling repeated withdrawals of the same funds from these alternate balance fields.

name: Polkatrain
description: The POLT_LBP contract's rebate mechanism lacked maximum rebate limits or exhaustion checks. An attacker repeatedly called the swap function to extract rebate rewards, draining 57K DOT (~$3M) from the contract. The contract's _update function failed to validate rebate constraints.

name: TMX TRIBE
description: On January 5-6, 2026, attacker exploited TMX TRIBE perpetual futures (Arbitrum/Optimism) via flawed AUM calculation ignoring USDG liabilities. Repeated mint-stake-swap loops allowed artificially inflated redemptions, draining $1.4M.

name: 42DAO
description: 42DAO's Balance Coin collapsed from $1 to $0.0012 on July 22, 2026 when attacker fed a fake low BTCB price to the oracle via the Spotter module. The oracle lacked drawdown limits and price floors, triggering liquidations of BTCB vaults at far-below-market prices.

name: YOLO Games
description: YOLO Games' Bazaar LBP (Liquidity Bootstrapping Pool) on Blast was exploited on June 11, 2024 for $1.5M. The exitPool function failed to verify msg.sender, allowing anyone to withdraw assets as a liquidity provider. Unchecked function arguments permitted use of BazaarLBPFactoryBlast address as sender.

name: Bitstamp
description: Six Bitstamp employees were targeted in a sophisticated weeks-long phishing campaign starting in November 2014. The attacker sent social engineering emails to the CTO and system administrator, culminating in malware installation that gave the attacker access to the exchange's hot wallet infrastructure.

name: SurgeBNB
description: SurgeBNB suffered a reentrancy attack funded by a 10,000 BNB flash loan. The sell function updated balances after external calls, letting attacker repeatedly withdraw value.

name: WOO X
description: WOO X exchange suffered a phishing attack via a fake open-source collaboration request that lured a developer to open a malicious development tool. Attackers gained access to the development environment and executed unauthorized withdrawals across nine user accounts, draining $14M across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Arbitrum, and BSC.

name: Levana Perps
description: Over December 13-26, 2023, Levana Protocol on Osmosis was exploited for $1.1M (10% TVL) via Pyth oracle staleness combined with Osmosis fee market bugs. Attacker executed profitable trades during volatile windows with stale price data; elevated gas costs amplified profitability.

name: SYFI
description: An anonymous trader exploited a rebase bug in SYFI's unaudited contract code. By staking a small amount and leveraging the arithmetic error in the rebase logic, they extracted nearly $250K in realized gains while crashing the token price from $174 to $0.0004.

name: Zilliqa
description: A buffer-copy error in the Zilliqa Ledger app's Schnorr signing code since 2019 fixed the top 64 bits of every nonce at zero. Attackers recovered private keys from ~5 on-chain signatures using lattice reduction and stole approximately 683.13M ZIL, with exploitation first spotted on July 19, 2026.

name: Hashflow
description: A vulnerable function in Hashflow's contract allowed attackers to trigger transferFrom() on approved user tokens. The attacker exploited an approve-related issue across five chains, draining approximately $605K. The white-hat nature of the attack was later confirmed, and a recovery function was provided by the attacker, with Hashflow committing to compensating all affected users.

name: Polymarket International
description: On June 25, 2026, Polymarket frontend was compromised via third-party vendor, injecting malicious JavaScript that phished users into approving fraudulent token transfers, draining $3M from at least 11 wallets.

name: Step Finance
description: On January 31, 2026, Step Finance suffered a $40 million operational loss when attackers compromised executive team devices, gaining unauthorized access to treasury and fee wallet signing keys/credentials. The protocol had no smart contract vulnerabilities.

name: Rikkei Finance
description: Rikkei Finance lending protocol lacked permission controls in the setOracleDate function, allowing an attacker to manipulate oracle prices. With only 0.0001 BNB as collateral, the attacker borrowed all USDC, BTC, DAI, USDT, and BUSD from liquidity pools by inflating collateral value through the malicious oracle.

name: uniBTC
description: On September 26, 2024, a former employee planted malware in Bedrock's Cargo.toml file, providing persistent access for three weeks through IDE execution. The attacker then exploited a flaw in the uniBTC minting mechanism that allowed arbitrary minting against ETH, draining $1.7M-$2M from the liquidity pool.

name: Peapods Finance
description: Peapods Finance's aspLONGsUSDe pod on July 8, 2025 exploited for $207K via oracle misconfiguration. Attacker manipulated the WETH/aspLONGsUSDe price to inflate collateral values. The issue was in user-created pod logic, not core contracts.

name: Yapizon
description: On April 22, 2017, Yapizon suffered an attack where hackers compromised four hot wallets and stole 3,816 BTC (~$5M), representing 37% of user funds. South Korean authorities later alleged the breach was perpetrated by North Korea. Yapizon replaced lost balances with Fei tokens representing IOUs.

name: TiFi
description: TIFIToken on BSC suffered a flash loan price manipulation attack. The attacker used a flash loan to artificially move the token price, enabling profitable transactions on decentralized exchanges.

name: Floor Dao
description: FloorDAO's staking contract for the rebasing sFLOOR token contained a logic flaw that could be exploited during rebasing operations. The vulnerability was discovered and exploited on September 5, 2023, with post-mortems published by the FloorDAO team.

name: Bald
description: On 31 July 2023 the anonymous deployer of the BALD memecoin on Base removed the two-sided liquidity provided two days after launch, crashing the token roughly 90%.

name: Jimbos Protocol
description: On May 28, 2023, Jimbos Protocol on Arbitrum (launched <20 days prior) was exploited for 4,090 ETH via flashloan-enabled oracle manipulation. Attacker took $5.9M flashloan and manipulated JIMBO price to exploit shift/conversion logic lacking slippage protection.

name: FTX
description: On November 11-12, 2022, a SIM-swapping gang stole approximately $450M in crypto from FTX by walking into AT&T stores with fake IDs, hijacking employee phone accounts, intercepting 2FA codes sent to FTX users, and draining their wallets during the company's bankruptcy.

name: Bisq
description: Bisq's trade arbitration did not verify that the payout address for time-locked fallback transactions was the legitimate Bisq donation address. Attackers posing as sellers set their own donation address, then let trades time out, causing the platform to send the buyer's deposit, payment, and security deposit to the attacker's wallet instead of the Bisq DAO address. Six traders lost a total of 34.86 BTC on March 28 and April 7.

name: MERLIN DEX
description: On April 25, 2023, zkSync DEX Merlin was exploited for $1.82 million. The attacker drained pools through the feeTo address in MerlinFactory which had unlimited asset transfer permissions and lacked multi-sig governance.

name: Venus Protocol
description: Venus LUNA market had a hardcoded $0.10 minimum price while Chainlink froze updates due to LUNA volatility. Attackers bought LUNA at drastically reduced prices and used it as collateral at $0.10/token to borrow other assets, extracting $11.2M before Venus suspended the market.

name: Alpha Homora
description: MEV bot extracted value from Alpha Homora V2 via sandwich attack on Uniswap V2 addLiquidity function. The attacker took advantage of implicit assumptions in Uniswap's contract that were not enforced at the contract level, allowing slippage to bypass checks on certain trade paths.

name: Pond.fun
description: Pond.fun's lead software engineer Genesis exploited privileged access to the platform's smart contracts, manipulating withdrawal functions to drain 64.8 ETH from the liquidity pools. The stolen funds were bridged to Railgun for privacy before moving to centralized exchanges. Chainalysis and Elliptic were contracted to track and prevent laundering of the stolen assets.

name: Force DAO
description: Force DAO was exploited hours after launch when the xFORCE vault contract assumed failed ERC20 transfers would revert. The Aragon Minime token returns false instead, allowing attackers to claim tokens without proper validation and drain ~$367K in FORCE.

name: Zenterest
description: On August 16, 2024, Zenterest lending protocol was exploited for approximately $21,000 when an attacker exploited severely stale oracle prices. The ZenterestPriceFeed had not been updated for 570 days, displaying MPH Token at an inflated price of 944,836,858,607,953 versus the actual 0.4677 USD, enabling excessive borrows that the attacker profited on.

name: PGNLZ
description: PGNLZ's flawed burn mechanism allowed attackers to burn tokens directly from the PancakeSwap USDT-PGNLZ pool's balance without proper synchronization. This artificially reduced pool reserves, creating sharp price distortions that enabled attackers to execute reverse swaps and drain approximately $100K in USDT.

name: Bankroll Network
description: Bankroll Network's token sale contract lacked validation on the _customerAddress parameter, allowing attackers to manipulate profitPerShare_ calculations and extract dividends without sending WBNB tokens.

name: DEUS Finance
description: DEUS Finance lost $6.5M across Arbitrum, BSC, and Ethereum when an attacker exploited a parameter ordering error in the DEI stablecoin's burnFrom function, reversing approval relationships in the allowances mapping.

name: Wiener DOGE
description: Wiener DOGE token exploited via flash loan attack. The deflationary token failed to exclude LP pairs from transfer fees, allowing an attacker to drain tokens from liquidity pools. The k-value was destroyed, and the attacker profited approximately 78 BNB.

name: ReHold
description: ReHold's CEO and co-founder Renat Gafarov unilaterally withdrew $700K in net profits and initial capital from the protocol's smart contracts without approval from his co-founder, then seized control of company infrastructure and domain access.

name: OWNLY
description: OWNLY's unstake function lacked claim status validation, allowing attackers to repeatedly call unstake() and extract 930M OWN tokens without authorization. The staking contract was drained of ~$37K in BNB equivalent before discovery.

name: IRA Financial / Gemini
description: Hackers obtained IRA Financial's master API key from unencrypted emails between Gemini and IRA, which contained a single point of failure that bypassed security protocols. The attackers consolidated funds from all sub-accounts into one and withdrew approximately $36M in Bitcoin and Ether within a two-hour window before Gemini could freeze accounts.

name: Nesa
description: Nesa was exploited through a Cosmos EVM vulnerability involving inconsistent balance accounting between Cosmos EVM and the Cosmos SDK. In the shared exploit mechanism documented by Cosmos Labs, delegation of locked tokens from a vesting account through the staking precompile could cause an unchecked EVM balance underflow to approximately 2^256. The resulting artificial balance could then be used to overflow a high-balance victim account, reducing the victim balance to zero while transferring its legitimate tokens to the attacker, with no net increase in token supply. Nesa has confirmed exploitation of a Cosmos EVM vulnerability but has not publicly disclosed its Nesa-side exploit transaction or victim account, so application of the exact shared mechanism to Nesa remains strongly supported but not independently demonstrated at transaction level

name: DeltaPrime
description: DeltaPrime on Arbitrum suffered a $1M loss on July 23, 2024 when a flawed account ownership transfer allowed attackers to take control of accounts and withdraw collateral.

name: Citadel.one
description: Citadel.one, a portfolio management dApp on Arbitrum, suffered an access control vulnerability that allowed unauthorized extraction of wrapped Ethereum (WETH) and USD Coin (USDC). The attackers exploited improper access controls in the smart contract to drain approximately $93,000 in user funds.

name: Verge
description: Between April and May 2018, attackers exploited Verge's timestamp validation mechanism by mining blocks with spoofed timestamps set one hour in the past, forcing rapid difficulty adjustments. This allowed mining at inflated rates, generating counterfeit coins valued at ~$1.75M. The attackers manipulated multiple mining algorithms to maximize coin generation.

name: WOOFi Swap
description: WOOFi Swap on Arbitrum was exploited on March 5, 2024 via a flash loan attack on its synthetic proactive market making algorithm. An attacker borrowed 7.7M WOO tokens, exploiting the missing Chainlink price fallback to crash the price and profit ~$8.75M across three swaps in 13 minutes.

name: Blizz Finance
description: Blizz Finance on Avalanche was drained of ~$8.3M in May 2022 when Chainlink froze LUNA pricing at $0.10 far above market value during Terra's collapse, allowing overcollateralized borrowing.

name: Pond0x
description: Pond0x's directTransfer() function allowed any account to transfer tokens from any other address without authorization. The function exposed an internal _transfer function with no access controls, enabling attackers to drain funds by moving tokens from any address to their own.

name: Xai
description: Malicious actors impersonated the legitimate Xai gaming blockchain project to deceive unsuspecting ETH holders. Victims transferred 374 ETH to the fraudulent scheme believing they were interacting with the Xai Launchpool or legitimate project channels.

name: Pando Rings
description: On November 5-6, 2022, Pando Rings suffered an oracle manipulation attack when an attacker inflated sBTC-WBTC LP token values in the oracle, enabling borrowing against inflated collateral and stealing approximately $20-22M.

name: Syscoin Bridge
description: Syscoin bridge exploited via parsing inconsistency between Syscoin Core and NEVM relay. A malformed UTXO burn proof with duplicate asset commitments was accepted as valid by the relay, enabling unauthorized minting of ~5B SYS tokens.

name: EOSCast
description: EOSCast gaming contract was exploited via a fake EOS token attack. The attacker created a malicious token contract named 'EOS' and launched 17 transfer attacks of varying amounts (100, 1,000, and 10,000 counterfeit tokens). The contract failed to verify the token issuer, allowing the hacker to extract 72,912 real EOS from the bonus pool.

name: Scroll Token
description: The Scroll Token contract contained an arithmetic error in its transfer function allowing integer underflow from zero-balance addresses. Attackers exploited this to mint unlimited tokens, causing the price to collapse 99.99%.

name: ForceBridge
description: On June 2, 2025, Force Bridge (Nervos Network) was exploited via missing access controls on privileged functions. Attackers drained $3.9M across ETH and BSC (539 ETH, 898,300 USDC, 257,800 USDT, 0.79 WBTC).

name: UXLINK
description: An attacker exploited a delegatecall in UXLINK's multisig wallet to rewrite the owner set without signer approval. This enabled draining ~$11.3M in stablecoins/ETH/WBTC, seizing ~490M UXLINK tokens, and minting 1-2B more before the token crashed over 70%.

name: Fortress Loans
description: On May 8, 2022 at 20:34 UTC Fortress Loans was exploited via an insufficient governance quorum (400k FTS tokens valued at ~$18K) when an attacker acquired governance quorum and passed proposal #11 to set FTS collateral factor to 700,000,000,000,000,000, then borrowed inflated collateral value combined with oracle manipulation to steal 1,048.1 ETH and 400,000 DAI (~$2.98M total).

name: SBI Crypto
description: On September 24, 2025 roughly $21M in BTC, ETH, LTC, DOGE and BCH flowed out of hot wallets belonging to SBI Crypto (Japanese SBI Group's mining pool) through five instant exchangers and into Tornado Cash. ZachXBT and Cyvers linked the laundering pattern to DPRK-affiliated actors; SBI Group never publicly confirmed the incident.

name: Curve DEX
description: On July 30, 2023, multiple Curve Finance pools were exploited via a Vyper 0.2.15/0.2.16/0.3.0 compiler bug in reentrancy guards. Attackers stole ~$61.7M across pETH-ETH, alETH-ETH, msETH-ETH, and others; ~68% was later recovered.

name: WIFCOIN
description: WIFCOIN_ETH experienced a business logic flaw on June 16, 2024 that allowed fund extraction. Technical details documented in DeFiHackLabs security research.

name: SQUID
description: On April 8, 2024, the SQUID Game Coin on BSC was exploited via swap logic vulnerability in the SquidTokenSwap contract. An attacker used a flashloan to acquire 163M SQUID tokens, then exploited the V2 PancakeSwap interaction to drain approximately $87K through unintended arbitrage opportunities.

name: Kelp
description: On April 18, 2026, Kelp DAO's rsETH bridge was exploited for $293 million when attackers compromised LayerZero's RPC nodes via social engineering and injected fraudulent cross-chain messages. Kelp's 1-of-1 verifier configuration created a single point of failure, affecting validation across 20 chains. The attack was attributed to Lazarus Group.

name: Aeternity
description: Unknown attacker(s) controlled over 51% of Aeternity's hash power on December 5-8, enabling double-spend attacks. The attacker deliberately reorganized blocks and double-spent 29 million Æ coins across targeted exchanges (OKEx, Huobi, Gate.io, Binance). A subsequent January 8 attempt to repeat the attack was detected and blocked by community members.

name: Omni
description: On July 10, 2022, Omni, an NFT money market, was exploited via reentrancy across two functions lacking reentrancy guards and not following the checks-effects-interactions pattern. The attacker used NFTs as collateral to borrow ETH, then cleared the debt at the reentrancy point, making the borrowing bad debt and removing the need to repay, stealing 1,300 ETH in testing funds.

name: Holograph
description: On 13 June 2024 a former Holograph technical contractor exploited inadequate access control on the mint/operator functions to mint 1 billion HLG across nine transactions using internal knowledge, with HLG falling roughly 80% within nine hours of the exploit.

name: Mosca2
description: Mosca2's join() function was a balance multiplier due to composable logic flaws. The function attempted to top-up a member's balance but instead allowed permissionless balance inflation, enabling complete treasury drainage.

name: Limit Break Payment Processor
description: A vulnerability in Limit Break’s Payment Processor allowed an attacker to abuse users’ existing token and NFT approvals to transfer assets without a legitimate marketplace purchase. Payment Processor V2 on Ethereum was exploited first, and V3 contained the same vulnerability. Limit Break paused V3 where possible, while whitehats transferred vulnerable NFTs to safe custody because V2 could not be paused and ApeChain V3 could not immediately be paused. The same underlying approval flaw could be used in reverse against WETH approvals, resulting in 660 WETH being stolen along with other tokens before whitehats could secure it

name: Affine Protocol
description: The Affine Protocol's flashloan callback failed to validate userData parameters from untrusted sources. Attackers exploited this to trigger the upgrade path and steal collateral assets.

name: Synthetify
description: Synthetify was compromised through a governance attack targeting an inactive DAO with pure token-based voting. The protocol was frozen and no funds were recovered as stolen assets were mixed through Tornado Cash.

name: Rain
description: Rain lost ~$14.8M on April 29, 2024 when exchange wallet private keys were compromised across four chains (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP). Stolen assets were consolidated into 137.9 BTC and 1,881 ETH via instant exchanges; the breach wasn't disclosed until ZachXBT surfaced it two weeks later.

name: Astrid Finance
description: On October 28-29, 2023, Astrid Finance on Ethereum was exploited for $228K via missing input validation on withdraw() parameters. Attacker manipulated _restakedTokenAddress to create counterfeit tokens and convert to ETH; returned ~$182K after legal threat.

name: BNBS
description: BNBS token on BSC was exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability where the contract failed to update state before transferring funds. The attacker invoked the vulnerable function repeatedly before completion, draining funds from the contract.

name: Bancor V3
description: Bancor decentralized exchange platform suffered a security breach on July 9, 2018 where attackers gained unauthorized access to the platform's wallet containing BNT tokens, ETH, and other ERC-20 tokens. The attacker drained approximately $23.5 million in assets. Bancor identified the breach, secured affected accounts, and announced recovery and user compensation measures.

name: Gamee
description: Gamee's deployer private key was compromised via an unsecured GitLab environment, enabling an attacker to gain control of the project's deployer address on Polygon. The attacker exploited recoverERC721s() function bypass protections and stole approximately 600 million GMEE tokens worth ~$7M at the time.

name: BBOX
description: BBOX token on BSC was exploited through a flash loan price manipulation attack. The attacker used a flash loan to artificially move the token price on DEX, enabling profitable transactions.

name: Fogo Foundation
description: An unknown actor compromised the Fogo Foundation and transferred 400M FOGO tokens to an attacker-controlled destination. Fogo has not disclosed the specific attack vector, affected Foundation wallet, or how authorization over the tokens was obtained. The Fogo blockchain itself was not initially compromised; the network was subsequently halted as a precaution to prevent movement of the affected tokens and upgrade the network to restrict associated addresses

name: Upbit
description: Upbit's Ethereum hot wallet was compromised on November 27, 2019, resulting in theft of 342,000 ETH (~$49.3M). The South Korean exchange immediately froze all deposits and withdrawals and transferred remaining hot wallet funds to cold storage. Upbit announced it would cover the loss from its own funds. Lazarus/Andariel hacking groups were later attributed responsibility by authorities.

name: Polycule
description: On January 13, 2026, Polycule's Telegram bot for Polymarket was hacked when the server storing user private keys was breached. The bot stored keys unencrypted on a central server with inadequate security, allowing attackers to drain $230,000 from affected users.

name: Bunny
description: On July 16, 2021, attacker minted 2.1M unbacked polyBUNNY tokens via QuickSwap price manipulation on Polygon. The token crashed 82% ($10 to $2), causing $2.4M loss. Bunny compensated users with $2.4M in MND tokens.

name: BarnBridge
description: BarnBridge suffered a governance attack on July 15, 2026 when an attacker passed a malicious proposal, replaced the SMART Yield provider contract, and drained ~$776K by exploiting pre-existing USDC approvals from 50 users.

name: XT Exchange
description: XT.com lost ~$1.7M on November 28, 2024 when the hot wallet was compromised. Attacker drained twelve token types and swapped to 461.58 ETH. The exchange halted withdrawals and said user funds were covered by 1.5x reserves.

name: BitMart
description: BitMart's hot wallets were compromised on December 4, 2021, resulting in theft of $196M: $100M on Ethereum and $96M on Binance Smart Chain.

name: Ledger Connect Kit
description: Attackers compromised a former Ledger employee's NPMJS account via phishing and published malicious versions of Ledger Connect Kit (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) containing Angel Drainer malware. The code rerouted user transaction approvals through rogue WalletConnect instances for less than two hours before detection.

name: Pickle
description: Pickle's ControllerV4.swapExactJarForJar function lacked jar whitelisting, allowing an attacker to create fake jars and siphon 19.76M DAI from the pDAI jar via missing input validation.

name: Hector Lending
description: Hector Lending's cross-chain bridge on Fantom was exploited on June 2, 2023. An unlimited USDC approval on a beta bridge contract was exploited to drain ~650,000 USDC, after which the network voted to liquidate $16M in treasury.

name: WealthManagementV2
description: The attacker obtained control of WealthManagementV2’s owner privileges, suspected to have resulted from a leaked owner private key. After taking ownership, the attacker used updatePlanConfig() to set period=0 and interestMultiplier/unlockMultiplier=528,300,000. Because the privileged configuration function had no timelock or parameter bounds, the attacker could invest and immediately redeem to generate artificially inflated interest, then use a second investment to unlock and withdraw the resulting balance

name: OpenLeverage
description: On April 1, 2024, OpenLeverage on BSC suffered a business logic vulnerability exploited via flashloan attack. An attacker manipulated protocol accounting to extract funds from the leveraged trading protocol. OpenLeverage's insurance and buyback funds were mobilized to compensate affected users.

name: SquidRouterModule
description: SquidRouterModule, a third-party Gnosis Safe module for Squid Router, was exploited via a verification error in executeSameChainActions(). The function accepted a publicly available constant string as proof of message security. An attacker with this fixed string could impersonate Safe wallet owners and execute arbitrary calldata to drain 86 Gnosis Safe vaults over two hours, consolidating ~$3.2M worth into DAI.

name: Litecoin
description: A zero-day in Litecoin's MWEB transaction validation allowed attackers to craft malformed transactions that non-updated nodes accepted, enabling unauthorized peg-outs. Fixed via 13-block chain reorganization.

name: CoinStats
description: CoinStats portfolio service suffered a breach affecting private keys for 1,590 user wallets, resulting in $2.2M in direct theft. Attackers compromised multiple CoinStats internal services and external integrations through sophisticated multi-vector intrusion. Lazarus Group is suspected as the attacker.

name: Vee Finance
description: Vee Finance on Avalanche was exploited on September 21, 2021 for ~$34-35M ($9M BTC + $26.2M ETH). The attacker manipulated Pangolin DEX prices by creating fake trading pairs and executing manipulative trades to distort prices that Vee Finance used as its single oracle source.

name: General Bytes
description: General Bytes' Bitcoin ATM cloud service was compromised through a zero-day vulnerability in the master service interface. Attackers uploaded malicious Java applications to decrypt API keys, accessed hot wallet funds, and stole user credentials by scanning private keys entered at ATMs.

name: NEAR Intents
description: NEAR Intents was exploited through a bug in the interaction between its Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure and the NEAR Intents smart contract, allowing unauthorized withdrawals. The team stopped services, patched the contract-side vulnerability, and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals across multiple networks while completing fixes to the Omni infrastructure. The stolen funds were traced toward KuCoin and then BTC, and NEAR Intents said the losses would be compensated in full

name: Lazy Summer Protocol
description: On July 6, 2026, Summer.fi's Lazy Summer Protocol USDC vaults were exploited when an impaired Silo vault (from November 2025 Stream Finance collapse) remained in NAV calculations. The attacker accumulated vault tokens whose value hadn't reflected economic impairment, transferred them to inflate totalAssets, and redeemed at inflated price for $6.04M in genuine USDC.

name: Ambient
description: On October 17, 2024, Ambient Finance frontend domain was hijacked via compromised registrar credentials and redirected to malicious site. Users were tricked into approving token transfers via the fake site. Ambient recovered the domain and reimbursed affected users; smart contracts remained unaffected.

name: Notional V2
description: An attacker exploited an unchecked uint128 cast in Notional V1’s collateral valuation logic. By minting two fCash positions against the same payer with notionals of 1 and 2^128-1, the attacker engineered a debt balance of exactly 2^128. When the free-collateral check converted the debt to ETH, uint128(balance.abs()) truncated 2^128 to zero, making the insolvent payer appear to have no debt. The attacker then settled the fabricated fCash claims and withdrew approximately $1.73M in USDC and DAI from the Escrow

name: Allbridge
description: Allbridge’s CCTPTokenMessenger treated a valid Circle-attested message as proof that USDC had actually been transferred. An attacker created an arbitrary CCTP message on Polygon declaring a 1,000,000 USDC transfer without burning any USDC and directed its recipient to an attacker-controlled contract rather than Circle’s TokenMessengerV2. Circle legitimately attested the generic message, but redeeming it on Base minted no USDC. Allbridge nevertheless trusted the attacker-controlled amount encoded in the message and recorded a 1,000,000 USDC deposit without checking for a corresponding token balance increase. The attacker flash-loaned 808,844 USDC to temporarily bring the router’s balance to the declared amount, redeemed the phantom credit for 999,000 USDC, repaid the loan, and drained the router’s existing liquidity. A copycat subsequently used the same technique to take the remaining funds

name: Matcha
description: Matcha Meta users lost $13.43M on January 25, 2026 when the SwapNet aggregator was exploited for arbitrary-call ability. The vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to user-approved tokens across Base and Ethereum. The frontend UI inadequately warned about approval risks.

name: Sovryn
description: On October 4, 2022, Sovryn's legacy Lend/Borrow pool was exploited via cross-contract reentrancy in closeWithDeposit. Attacker manipulated iToken price through fallback functions triggered by RBTC/rUSDT transfers, draining 44.9368 RBTC and 282,351.9644 rUSDT (~$1.1M).

name: Upbit
description: Upbit hot wallet was drained on November 27, 2025 in 54 minutes for $36M in Solana tokens (USDC, BONK, JTO, SONIC, RAY, RENDER, ORCA, PYTH). Attacker exploited weak digital signature infrastructure that allowed private key derivation from on-chain transaction history.

name: Verus-Ethereum Bridge
description: On May 17-18, 2026, the Verus-Ethereum bridge was exploited when an attacker forged a cross-chain payload that passed all cryptographic checks but lacked amount reconciliation between chains, converting ~$10 in VRSC fees into $11.58 million in Ethereum assets (103.6 tBTC, 1,625 ETH, 147,000 USDC).

name: SushiSwap
description: SushiMaker malicious-pool fee capture attack where an attacker created a malicious pool and redirected SushiSwap fees to it. The attacker captured approximately 15,000 USD in accumulated fees through access control vulnerabilities in the fee-distribution mechanism.

name: Nobitex
description: Nobitex hot wallet private keys compromised on June 18, 2025, leading to $82-90M theft across blockchains. Attackers deliberately destroyed the stolen funds by sending to inaccessible addresses as a political statement.

name: KiiChain
description: An attacker exploited chained balance-accounting defects in the shared Cosmos EVM module used by KiiChain. By deploying a contract at a precomputed vesting-account address and delegating one wei more KII than its spendable balance, the attacker triggered an arithmetic underflow in the staking precompile’s EVM balance write-back. Combined with a missing overflow guard in the EVM value-transfer path, this allowed real KII to be redirected from victim accounts to attacker-controlled addresses without increasing total supply. The sequence was repeated against 18 targets

name: Platypus Finance
description: Platypus's liquidity conversion logic for LP-USDC assumed a 1:1 ratio between USDC and USDC.e, ignoring market price discrepancies. When exchanging USDC for USDC.e, the calculation produced unreasonably large quantities, allowing arbitrageurs to extract value.

name: Visor Finance
description: An attacker compromised a single admin account managing Hypervisor emergency withdraw functions, enabling extraction of 504,845 USD from unpositioned assets awaiting LP placement. The team had not yet migrated to a multisig setup and the attacker lacked full visibility into safeguards, limiting losses. The team restored all withdrawn amounts using treasury funds.

name: Parity Multisig
description: On November 8, 2017, a user called 'devops199' accidentally exploited a vulnerability in Parity's multi-sig wallet library contract by calling initWallet then kill(), permanently disabling over 500 multi-sig wallets containing approximately 500,000 ETH. The library lacked protection against reinitialization and destruction by non-owners.

name: Eterbase
description: Attackers compromised Eterbase's internet-connected hot wallets holding Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Tezos, Algorand and TRON. The stolen funds were transferred to attacker-controlled addresses and subsequently moved through multiple exchanges including Binance and Huobi.

name: CoWSwap
description: On February 7, 2023, CoW Swap was exploited through a vulnerability in the SwapGuard contract which permitted arbitrary external calls. The attacker forced the GPv2Settlement contract to approve a malicious contract and transferred DAI tokens worth approximately $180K from the settlement contract.

name: BNO
description: BNO's emergencyWithdraw function on BNB Chain lacked access controls and didn't check for NFT rights records. An attacker exploited this to deposit both NFT and ERC20 tokens, then withdraw only the ERC20 via emergencyWithdraw, bypassing reward calculations and earning undeserved mining rewards.

name: Serenity Shield
description: The Serenity Shield deployer wallet was compromised via spear-phishing attack, allowing attackers to access private keys. The attacker then transferred 6.9M SERSH tokens valued at $5.6M at the time, but only realized $586K after selling on available liquidity.

name: Starstream Finance
description: Starstream Finance's treasury was drained via an unprotected execute() function in the DistributorTreasury contract that allowed external calls bypassing owner restrictions on token withdrawals.

name: FutureSwap
description: FutureSwap's changePosition collateral accounting was exploited via a large short position opened with an Aave V3 flash loan. The attacker corrupted the protocol's internal stableBalance tracking, enabling withdrawal of far more collateral than deposited, resulting in the loss of $395K in USDC.

name: Popsicle Finance
description: On 3 August 2021 an attacker exploited Popsicle Finance's Sorbetto Fragola UniswapV3 optimizer pool where share transfers did not update fee-tracking state, allowing the same fee rewards to be claimed multiple times across accounts, draining ~$20.7M.

name: MakerDAO ETH-A Liquidation Keeper Bot
description: A dormant third-party MakerDAO ETH-A liquidation keeper had an unprotected drain routine that lacked ds-auth authorization. Any caller could invoke the function and provide the withdrawal recipient. The attacker triggered Flipper.deal() for four auctions the keeper had won in 2020, causing 200 WETH of previously unclaimed collateral to move through Vat.flux to the keeper, then used GemJoin.exit() to send it to an attacker-controlled recipient and unwrap it to ETH. MakerDAO’s core contracts behaved as designed; the vulnerability was in the third-party keeper

name: LAXO
description: LAXO token's flawed burn mechanism allowed an attacker to execute a burn-before-sync exploit via flash loans. By burning LAXO directly from the PancakeSwap pool without triggering a reserve sync, the attacker artificially collapsed pool reserves and extracted 487k USDT through manipulated swaps.

name: Namada Shielded Pools
description: On June 19, 2026, approximately $600K in assets (ATOM, USDC, OSMO, TIA, NYM) were drained from Namada's Multi-Asset Shielded Pool via an IBC transfer logic flaw. The loss went initially undetected due to a stale indexer continuing to display funds as available while live RPC queries showed zero balance.

name: Treasure
description: Treasure marketplace's buyItem() function failed to validate token types, allowing attackers to purchase NFTs by specifying incorrect ERC721/ERC1155 amounts for free.

name: Stake DAO Yield
description: On May 27, 2026, Stake DAO on Arbitrum was exploited when a compromised deployer key reconfigured the LayerZero v2 OFT peer. The attacker minted 5.4 trillion vsdCRV tokens; despite massive nominal value, poor liquidity limited actual extraction to ~$91K.

name: CoW
description: On November 7, 2024, CoW Protocol on Ethereum was exploited through an access control vulnerability, resulting in approximately $59K in losses.

name: Gondi V3
description: Gondi V3 exploited March 9, 2026 when the Purchase Bundler lacked caller verification. Attacker drained 78 NFTs (~$230K) with lingering approvals from prior loan operations by calling the unprotected buy() function.

name: Dolomite
description: An old Dolomite DEX contract on Ethereum (deployed 2019) was exploited via a reentrancy vulnerability. The attacker bypassed the noEntry reentrancy guard by calling the callFunction through the TradeManager contract, which lacked proper reentrancy protection, allowing recursive fund drainage from users who had approved the contract.

name: Cascade Liquidity Strategy
description: On July 15, 2026, Cascade Liquidity Strategy's perpetuals vault suffered a $1.34 million USDC drain through oracle price feed manipulation affecting deposit/withdrawal logic.

name: Tectonic
description: The attacker built a leveraged TONIC/tTONIC collateral position through 98 recursive operations, then transferred TONIC directly into the tTONIC contract twice without minting corresponding tTONIC, increasing the tTONIC exchange rate outside the normal deposit path. The attacker also increased TONIC’s market price, while Tectonic’s price feed relied on VVS Finance and Crypto.com Exchange pricing without smoothing or a circuit breaker. These effects compounded the collateral valuation, allowing the attacker to borrow and remove more than $120M of assets from Tectonic’s lending markets within roughly 11 minutes

name: TheNFTV2
description: TheNFTV2 contained a business logic flaw in its withdrawal mechanism that incorrectly calculated user shares and balances. An attacker exploited the logic error to withdraw more assets than their proportional stake, extracting funds from the protocol.

name: Kipseli
description: On April 22, 2026, an MEV bot exploited Kipseli's PropAMM Router on Base via a denomination/decimals mismatch in the quote logic, swapping 0.04 WETH for 0.926 cbBTC worth ~$72.35K.

name: DODO AMM
description: DODO's V2 Crowdpooling contract left init() callable after funding, allowing an attacker to reconfigure pools with worthless tokens and drain the real reserves. Around $3.8M was taken, but $3.1M was returned within a day as MEV bots captured most of the exploit profit.

name: Feminist Metaverse
description: Attackers exploited the FM token's skim() mechanism via flashloan, redirecting 75.15M FM tokens to SakeSwapPair and then to their own address for sale. 1838 BNB (~$540K) was extracted and sent to Tornado Cash.

name: Panoptic V1.1
description: On August 25, 2025, a critical hash-collision vulnerability was discovered in Panoptic V1.1's position fingerprinting scheme. The non-collision-resistant XOR-hashing would have allowed attackers to bypass collateral checks and drain liquidity pools, but was reported by security researchers before exploitation.

name: Numbers Protocol
description: Numbers Protocol's bridge integration with Multichain exposed a vulnerability in how excessive permissions were handled in the permit mechanism. An attacker exploited a user's unlimited permit grant to steal 557,754 NUM tokens, converting them to 13 ETH and draining multiple user accounts.

name: Nomad
description: On August 1, 2022, Nomad bridge was exploited when the protocol initialization set trusted roots to 0x00, matching the untrusted root value. This caused the Replica contract to accept any messages as valid, enabling 300+ copycat attackers to drain $190M total.

name: HackDao
description: Attackers exploited HackDao's token fee mechanism and skim() function via flashloan, borrowing and liquidating themselves repeatedly without repaying. The contract's flawed accounting allowed extraction of 200 BNB (~$65K) before theft detection.

name: RetoSwap
description: On May 20, 2026, RetoSwap (Haveno fork on Monero) failed to verify ACK message sources. Attackers registered attacker-controlled addresses as arbitrators for multisig wallets, stealing $2.7M from traders.

name: SquidMulticall
description: SquidMulticall exposes a permissionless run() function that executes arbitrary external calls with no access control. When users mistakenly approved tokens directly to SquidMulticall (instead of Squid Router), attackers could call run() with transferFrom() payloads to drain those approvals across multiple chains. A wallet with $623K in infinite approvals was compromised, resulting in $517K extracted.

name: KyberSwap Classic
description: KyberSwap frontend was compromised on September 1, 2022 via Google Tag Manager API key compromise, injecting malicious code that tricked whale wallets into approving fraudulent transfers, stealing $265K from 2 wallets.

name: SharedStake
