description: On September 1, 2023, SharedStake was exploited when improper ownership checks allowed an attacker to gain admin access. The attacker created a minter address with unlimited permissions, minted sgETH tokens without collateral, and withdrew approximately 105 ETH from the protocol.

name: YO Protocol
description: YO Protocol's Automated Harvesting System executed a rebalance with a misconfigured slippage tolerance of 17,872,058 (disabling protection). The order routed through high-fee Uniswap v4 pools (85-88%), returning only 112,036 USDC for 3,840,651 stkGHO, costing ~97% of vault stkGHO. YO's multisig bought the position back the same day.

name: Flooring Protocol
description: Flooring Protocol's contract upgrade introduced a vulnerability in its multicall mechanism that lacked proper context isolation. Attackers exploited this to call transferFrom on user NFT approvals without consent, stealing 36 Pudgy Penguins and 14 Bored Apes.

name: Meter
description: On February 5-6, 2022, Meter's bridge was exploited via missing validation on an alternative deposit function variant. Attacker called the function directly with arbitrary amounts, draining $4.4M from Meter and causing $3.3M cascading loss in Hundred Finance collateral pools.

name: Impermax V3
description: On April 26, 2025, Impermax V3 on Base was exploited for $300K via fee accounting mismatch in collateral valuation. Attacker manipulated LP pool price ticks, accumulated fees, then overborrowed against LP collateral with incorrectly valued uncollected fees.

name: SATURN
description: SATURN's transfer logic had a flaw where sync operations were performed before processing incoming token transfers. This allowed attackers to manipulate token reserves via flash loans and extract approximately 15 WBNB from the pool.

name: Arena SocialFi
description: On October 7, 2023, Stars Arena (an Avalanche friend.tech clone) was exploited via reentrancy when the share issuance function lacked reentrancy guards. The attacker called the function multiple times in one transaction to manipulate weight calculations, buying 1 share and selling it at ~274k AVAX to drain $2.97M.

name: BT Finance
description: BT Finance was exploited via flash loan attack that manipulated price oracles, draining over $1.5 million from the protocol.

name: Troves
description: On October 31, an attacker exploited permissions retained by a legacy rebalancing contract after it had been replaced, resulting in approximately 8.6 BTC in losses from Troves' xWBTC/WBTC vault. Troves revoked the legacy contract's permissions and paused three vaults as a precaution. No impact on other vaults has been identified

name: Set Protocol
description: On July 30, 2026, Set Protocol was exploited for ~$9.6K via reentrancy in Index Coop's ExchangeIssuance contract. Attacker supplied malicious manager pre-issue hook that inflated positionMultiplier mid-issuance. Unlocked state allowed the hook to mutate position accounting, causing overpayment of assets.

name: StableMagnet
description: StableMagnet team deployed an intentional smart contract backdoor hidden in unverified linked libraries (block explorer gap), enabling them to drain liquidity pools and steal tokens from wallets with active approvals.

name: Kraken
description: A hacker compromised a whale account holding 1,200 BTC, placed orders to purchase BTC at artificially low prices, then dumped the stolen BTC to trigger execution and pocket $10.45M from liquidations of other users' positions.

name: Snowdog
description: SnowdogDAO ($SDOG) on Avalanche launched November 14, 2021, raising $45M in 8 days. On November 25, the team moved liquidity to a private Snowbank-controlled AMM pool requiring a secret challenge key. Only 7% of holders could liquidate, while three addresses drained $10M, $7.7M, and $3.3M, blocking $18.1M in total liquidity.

name: Startale
description: Attacker exploited Startale ERC-7579 smart-account initialization logic to take control of pre-funded counterfactual accounts as they were deployed. The initializeAccount(bytes) permitted an attacker-controlled bootstrap to execute via delegatecall, while an initialization authorization flag stored with transient storage remained set for the entire transaction. The attacker could therefore deploy a victim’s pre-funded account and reinitialize it again in the same transaction with a malicious bootstrap, allowing its assets to be swept

name: StablR
description: On May 24, 2026, one of StablR's three multisig keys was compromised. The attacker minted 8.35M USDR and 4.5M EURR against zero collateral and dumped them for ~$2.8M in ETH.

name: ChainConnect
description: On July 26, 2026, ChainConnect's EVM integration was compromised through unauthorized access, allowing attackers to drain ~$650,000 in tokens from bridge contracts on Ethereum, BNB Chain, Avalanche C-Chain, and Polygon across 23 transactions. Venom Network assets were unaffected.

name: Thunder Terminal
description: Thunder Terminal's MongoDB connection URL was compromised, allowing attackers to retrieve session tokens and execute unauthorized withdrawals from 114 user wallets. The attacker drained 86.5 ETH and 439 SOL in less than 9 minutes.

name: GERA
description: The GERA token's deployer private key was compromised, allowing an attacker to transfer ownership of the smart contract to another address. This gave the attacker full control over the token contract.

name: Hundred Finance
description: On April 15, 2023, Hundred Finance was drained of $7.4M on Optimism via a flashloan-funded donation to an empty WBTC pool, exploiting rounding errors in exchange rate calculation.

name: PeopleDAO
description: On March 6, 2023, PeopleDAO lost 76.5 ETH (~$120K) when an accounting lead accidentally shared a public editable Google Sheets form in Discord. An attacker added a hidden fraudulent 76.5 ETH transaction row, which the multisig signers failed to catch during review and approved.

name: BXH
description: Attacker gained access to BXH's administrative private key, allowing digital signature of a transaction transferring $139 million in tokens directly to the attacker's account. The details suggest an insider or compromised system with access to the admin key storage, making this likely an inside job or successful targeted malware infection.

name: Radiant V2
description: On 16 October 2024 attackers compromised three Radiant core contributors' devices with the INLETDRIFT macOS backdoor (delivered via Telegram impersonation of a former contractor) and manipulated the Safe{Wallet} front-end so signers saw legitimate data while signing malicious transactions, taking ownership of and draining Radiant lending markets on BSC and Arbitrum. Mandiant attributed the attack to DPRK-nexus actors.

name: AROS
description: Suspicious attack on BSC drained ~$295.3K USDT from AROS/USDT PancakeSwap; suspected contract logic flaw or price oracle manipulation but mechanism unconfirmed pending technical analysis.

name: SNK (Snooker)
description: The SNK token on BSC suffered an exploit of its referral reward mechanism. The attacker exploited the bindParent function of the SNKMiner contract to establish relationships between attack contracts, amplifying staking rewards based on child account SNK balances. By creating multiple attack contracts and establishing referral chains, the attacker was able to claim inflated rewards totaling approximately $197,725.

name: ATM
description: On June 4, 2026, ATM token on BSC was exploited for $243K via improper loop control in automatic swap-on-transfer mechanism. Contract was designed to convert 20% of transfers to BSC-USD, but flaw allowed repeated triggering beyond standard limits.

name: Deribit
description: On November 1-2, 2022, Deribit's BTC, ETH, and USDC hot wallets were compromised, draining ~$28M in crypto assets. Client assets in cold storage and Fireblocks vaults were unaffected. Deribit covered the loss with company reserves; the specific compromise method remains undisclosed.

name: Floating Point Group
description: Floating Point Group, an institutional crypto prime brokerage, suffered a cybersecurity breach resulting in a loss of $15-20M from custody accounts. The attackers gained unauthorized access to the company's systems, leading FPG to freeze third-party accounts and migrate funds to secure wallets while working with law enforcement.

name: DBXen
description: DBXen's ERC2771 meta-transaction implementation had an identity confusion bug where burnBatch() used _msgSender() to identify the actual user but onTokenBurned() used msg.sender() to identify the forwarder, allowing attackers to claim accumulated fees from 1,085 cycles using brand-new addresses.

name: CCC
description: The CCC sell() flow allowed CCC held by the PancakeSwap liquidity pair to be burned and then synchronized the pair’s reserves. This artificially reduced the pair’s CCC reserve and distorted its AMM price, enabling the attacker to repeatedly sell CCC against the manipulated pool and extract BNB liquidity

name: CoW Swap
description: The cow.fi domain was hijacked through social engineering at the .fi domain registrar. For 4.5 hours, users were redirected to a pixel-perfect phishing clone where they unknowingly signed malicious transactions draining funds.

name: YIEDL
description: On April 24, 2024, the YIEDL protocol on BSC was exploited via insufficient input validation on the dataList parameter in the redeem function. An attacker bypassed redemption share requirements by manipulating the dataList parameter and profited from repeated token exchanges totaling approximately $150K.

name: WebKeyDAO
description: WebKeyDAO's buy() function lacked proper access controls, allowing an attacker to purchase WKEYDAO tokens at artificially low prices set via an unprotected setTokenInfo() call. The attacker exploited this to acquire tokens at 1/10th market price and immediately sold them on DEX for profit, limited only by a built-in 67-token sale cap.

name: Ethereum Classic
description: A 51% attack on Ethereum Classic's Proof of Work chain allowed attackers to reorg the blockchain and double-spend 219,500 ETC on two separate occasions. Low mining hashrate and cheap rental hashpower via services like NiceHash enabled the attack.

name: Grinex
description: Grinex custodial wallets on Tron and Ethereum were compromised in April 2026, resulting in ~$13.74M drained. Attackers immediately swapped USDT into TRX and ETH to defeat stablecoin freezes before the exchange suspended operations.

name: Locus Finance
description: On December 30, 2023, Locus Finance vaults were exploited when an attacker compromised a developer's private key during a CTO transition. Without multisig security, the attacker used administrative access to drain $320,964 from vaults.

name: Remitano
description: On September 14-15, 2023, a third-party data breach exposed private keys to Remitano's exchange hot wallets. An attacker used these keys to drain approximately $2.7M in cryptocurrency across Ethereum, Tron, and Bitcoin Cash chains ($1.4M USDT, $208K USDC, and Ankr tokens).

name: Corepound
description: Corepound (AI yield aggregator on Core DAO) rug-pulled on 23 September 2025 when the team used privileged control over the aggregator's vaults to withdraw roughly $400,000 of deposited user funds. The Core community acknowledged the incident and organized an impacted-user response with promises of stricter ecosystem vetting.

name: UwU Lend
description: On June 13, 2024, UwU Lend suffered a second $3.7M exploit three days after a $20M hack on June 10. The attacker reused sUSDe tokens stolen in the first exploit as collateral to drain additional pools (uDAI, uWETH, uLUSD, uFRAX, uCRVUSD, uUSDT) because the protocol failed to freeze compromised collateral or revoke stolen token permissions between incidents.

name: Chainflip AMM
description: An attacker exploited Chainflip’s TRON-specific swap instruction and refund handling. Unlike Chainflip’s other integrations, TRON swap instructions were derived from transaction memos. The attacker could attach a different memo to a transaction already signed by Chainflip validators, causing Chainflip to interpret the transaction as another swap. When that duplicate instruction failed, the protocol refunded it even though the underlying deposit had already produced a payout, effectively allowing the same deposit to be paid twice. The attacker attempted the sequence eight times over approximately 90 minutes, with six unauthorized payouts succeeding

name: Flow
description: Flow's execution layer was exploited on December 27, allowing the attacker to mint FLOW tokens and bridge assets (WBTC, WETH, and stablecoins) via Celer and Debridge for $3.9M. The exploit was likely enabled by a compromised privileged admin key.

name: EOSDice
description: EOSDice gambling platform was attacked in November 2018 via exploitation of its controlled-seed randomness flaw. Attackers predicted the random number generation by analyzing blockchain state information. EOSDice was one of eight EOS DApps targeted simultaneously in coordinated randomness attacks.

name: Convex Finance
description: On June 23, 2022, Convex Finance's DNS was hijacked after a customer support agent at NameCheap was compromised. The attacker redirected www.convexfinance.com to a phishing site with malicious smart contracts mimicking the original addresses. At least 40 wallet addresses were tricked into approving transactions, though only limited tokens were stolen. Convex reimbursed all affected users from their treasury.

name: Sharwa.Finance
description: Sharwa Finance on Arbitrum was exploited in October 2025 via sandwich attacks on margin trading. Attackers created margin accounts, borrowed additional assets via leverage, and sandwiched their own swaps to extract ~$61K and ~$85K before the platform paused.

name: CoinDCX
description: CoinDCX lost ~$44.2M on July 19, 2025 when a server breach compromised the operational hot wallet's private key used for liquidity provisioning. Stolen assets were bridged from Solana to Ethereum; customer cold storage funds were unaffected.

name: Milady Maker
description: A rogue developer with access to the Remilia Collective treasury (backing the Milady Maker NFT project) siphoned $1M in accumulated fees from the Bonkler reserve-backed NFT system. The developer also attempted to seize control of project codebases and social media accounts, though Remilia's core reserves and NFT holdings remained secure.

name: Nimiq
description: Nimiq’s Polygon swap contracts served as OpenGSN forwarders while relying on their own preRelayedCall path to authenticate requests rather than independently verifying the user’s signature inside execute(). An attacker registered an EIP-7702 EOA as an OpenGSN relay manager, relay worker and permissive paymaster, then selected Nimiq’s HTLC handlers as the forwarders. This allowed forged open() requests purportedly originating from a partner liquidity wallet to reach the handlers without the expected signature validation. Because that wallet had existing token approvals to the handlers, HTLCs were opened using its USDC, USDT0 and USDC.e, with the attacker-controlled contract as recipient, and subsequently redeemed by the attacker

name: CF Token
description: CF token contract exposed a public _transfer function with an unvalidated 'from' address parameter, allowing arbitrary transfers from any holder. The attacker executed 6 transactions to transfer 4.2M CF tokens, converting them to 4,200+ BNB and cashing out via Tornado Cash.

name: Bithumb
description: Bithumb hot wallet was compromised by insiders with access to private keys, resulting in theft of 12.5M EOS and 6.2M XRP. All stolen funds were company assets as user funds were stored in cold storage.

name: DeltaPrime
description: DeltaPrime suffered a $5.98M exploit on September 16, 2024 when an attacker compromised the ProxyAdmin private key (not multi-sig protected). The attacker used it to upgrade liquidity pool proxy contracts to malicious implementations that allowed unlimited minting of deposit receipt tokens and systematic draining of USDC, WBTC, and WETH pools.

name: Etbox
description: Lazarus Group targeted Etbox exchange infrastructure using Worldbit-bot phishing tactics to obtain exchange wallet private keys and API credentials, resulting in theft of cryptocurrency assets.

name: Aerodrome V1
description: The centralized domains for both Aerodrome and Velodrome were hijacked via a NameSilo registrar compromise. Attackers bypassed multisig controls, removed DNSSEC, and redirected domains to malicious pages. Users were silently redirected to phishing interfaces with malicious signature flows and unlimited approval prompts, resulting in $700K in losses. The underlying smart contracts remained uncompromised.

name: four.meme
description: On February 11, 2025, four.meme was exploited when an attacker created a malicious PancakeSwap V3 pool with an inflated sqrtPriceX96 parameter (368 trillion times correct). Four.meme's migration logic used the pool without verification, allowing the attacker to drain WBNB by providing minimal tokens at the fake price.

name: Kokomo Finance
description: On March 26-27, 2023, Kokomo Finance developers initiated an exit scam, stealing ~$4M in user funds. The team manipulated the cBTC reward token contract, halted borrowing, converted the token implementation into a malicious contract, and removed all social media and website within days of launch.

name: Cozy V2
description: Cozy Finance confirmed an exploit affecting its v2 protection markets on Optimism, draining funds from the Main Set and Rabbithole Set. The affected markets relied on UMA’s Optimistic Oracle to resolve covered events. Cozy subsequently paused the affected Sets and stated there were no longer any open proposals against its UMA-based markets while it coordinated with UMA regarding dispute resolution. The precise mechanism that allowed the attacker to obtain payouts has not yet been confirmed

name: FixedFloat
description: On March 31, 2024, FixedFloat exchange suffered a hosting control breach through Time4VPS vulnerability. An attacker exploited residual access after an earlier February incident. FixedFloat suspended operations for two months to rebuild security infrastructure and relocate servers away from the compromised hosting provider.

name: AUR Protocol
description: AUR token on BSC lacked proper permission checks in critical functions. The missing access control allowed attackers to call privileged functions and drain token assets.

name: Zoth ZeUSD
description: Zoth's admin key was compromised, allowing the attacker to upgrade the proxy contract and execute unauthorized transfers of $8.85M in USD0++ stablecoins, converting them to 4,223 ETH.

name: GoldPesa
description: GoldPesa’s GPXHooks rebalanced protocol-owned GPX/USDC liquidity through Uniswap v4’s shared PositionManager without ensuring its currency deltas were isolated and settled. An attacker created an unpaid WETH/USDC position within the same PoolManager unlock and then triggered GoldPesa’s hourly rebalance. Because TAKE_PAIR operated on the PositionManager’s net credit, GoldPesa’s legitimate USDC credit offset the attacker’s outstanding debt, allowing the attacker to burn their position and withdraw the resulting USDC. Uniswap v4 itself behaved as designed

name: Barley Finance
description: Barley Finance, a volatility farming protocol, was exploited on its wBARL pod contract that had been deployed just two days prior. The attacker minted over 10% of the total BARL supply in a single transaction, extracting approximately $130K in value. The vulnerability was in the newly deployed pod contract.

name: Ethereum Classic
description: Attackers executed a second 51% attack on Ethereum Classic within a week, controlling the network's hash power to reorganize 4,236 blocks and execute double-spends. The attack lasted over 15 hours, resulting in at least $1.68M in stolen value through block reorganization and transaction reversal.

name: BONK Fun
description: BONK Fun's domain was hijacked via social engineering of registrar support to remove 2FA. The attacker replaced the site with a cloned frontend running Inferno Drainer, a wallet-draining contract that prompted users to sign malicious transactions.

name: Loopring
description: On June 9, 2024, Loopring's Official Guardian 2FA service (off-chain infra) was compromised, allowing attackers to masquerade as wallet owners, reset ownership, and steal $5M from Smart Wallets. Users with single guardian reliance were especially vulnerable.

name: Blur Finance
description: On August 10, 2022, Blur Finance developers executed a coordinated exit scam, withdrawing $600K from BSC and Polygon contracts, deleting social media, and disappearing, collapsing the token 99%.

name: FOOM Cash
description: On March 2, 2026, a misconfigured Groth16 verifier allowed attackers to submit forged zero-knowledge proofs and withdraw $2.26M from FOOM Cash. A white-hat recovered $1.84M (81%) of the stolen funds.

name: Terra (LUNA)
description: Scammers ran malicious Google ads for Terra ecosystem projects, impersonating Anchor and Astroport. Users were redirected to fake sites where they entered seed phrases after connecting wallets, allowing attackers to drain 52 wallets totaling $4.31M between April 12-21.

name: USM
description: On August 9, 2026, USM on Ethereum was exploited via an arithmetic error in its token accounting logic, resulting in a loss of approximately $136,000. Flagged by SlowMist; no dedicated post-mortem has been published.

name: Lympo
description: Lympo's hot wallet was compromised, resulting in the theft of 165.2 million LMT tokens worth $18.7M. The attacker transferred the stolen tokens across 10 project wallets before consolidating them into a single address and swapping them for ETH on Uniswap and SushiSwap. The LMT token price dropped 92% following the incident. Cold wallet reserves remained secure.

name: Bunni V2
description: On September 2, 2025, a rounding error in Bunni V2's withdrawal logic allowed attackers to systematically withdraw more tokens than entitled, draining $8.4M across Ethereum ($2.4M) and UniChain ($5.9M).

name: Z123
description: On April 22, 2024, the Z123 token on BSC was exploited via a flashloan-enabled price manipulation attack. An attacker used a flashloan to acquire large token quantities and manipulate the trading pair price, extracting approximately $136K before repaying the flashloan.

name: Wanchain
description: On July 21, 2026, Wanchain's Cardano-BNB Chain bridge was drained of ~515M NIGHT tokens. The TreasuryCheck validator concatenated 14 variable-length fields without separators, allowing a signature authorizing ~3,110 NIGHT to be reused for vastly larger redemptions.

name: Ploutoz
description: Attacker manipulated the DOP token price on Ploutoz Finance and used it as collateral to borrow CAKE, ETH, BTCB and other assets. After exchanging borrowed tokens to BNB via ParaSwap and PancakeSwap, attacker cashed out through Tornado Cash. Initial funds for the attack were withdrawn from Tornado Cash, indicating pre-planned coordination.

name: MSCST
description: On December 29, 2025, an attacker exploited missing access control in MSCST's releaseReward() function, flash loaning 46.8M GPC tokens to inflate GPC/WBNB price on PancakeSwap and extract ~$130K in BNB profit.

name: Solend
description: On August 19, 2021 at 12:40 GMT, Solend's UpdateReserveConfig() admin function was exploited when an attacker bypassed authorization checks by invoking the function with the admin's public key without requiring a valid signature. The attacker attempted to make lending accounts liquidatable, resulting in $16K in liquidations that were fully compensated by the liquidator.

name: Arbix Finance
description: Arbix Finance on BSC executed a rug pull on January 4, 2022, draining ~$10M in user funds via admin minting privileges. Team deleted web/social presence and moved funds via AnySwap.

name: Nimbus
description: Nimbus Platform's reward distribution mechanism was exploited via a flash loan attack. An attacker manipulated the token ratio in the NIMB/GNIMB pool using a 278 BNB flash loan to artificially inflate their staked ratio, dramatically increasing their rewards payout.

name: Cardex
description: On February 18, 2025 Cardex (fantasy trading card game on Abstract layer-2) suffered a session key compromise affecting approximately 9,000 wallets when a session signer private key was exposed on the frontend, allowing attackers to impersonate all active user sessions and drain approximately $400,000 from users who had approved session keys.

name: numa.
description: Numa's NumaVault on Sonic was exploited on August 10, 2025 for ~$313,000. Using a flash loan, the attacker inflated synthetic liabilities to collapse the collateral price, then liquidated under-collateralized positions before bridging 74.3 ETH to Ethereum.

name: Haven Protocol
description: Beginning June 22, 2021, Haven Protocol was exploited through multiple vulnerabilities including miner reward validation bypass, xJPY to xBTC conversion exploitation, and hidden burn/mint amount bugs. An unknown quantity of XHV tokens were minted before the network rolled back to pre-attack state on July 20 via hard fork.

name: Monkey Kingdom
description: Monkey Kingdom's Discord was compromised via a breach in Grape (a Solana token-membership protocol), allowing attackers to impersonate admins. Bots flooded the Discord with fake minting links directing users to malicious websites requiring wallet connection. Users who authorized the transactions had their SOL tokens stolen. Some victims lost as much as 650 SOL each.

name: DEUS Finance
description: DEUS Finance exploited on April 28, 2022 for $13.4M via flashloan oracle manipulation. A $143M flashloan skewed the DEI/USDC pool on Solidly, inflating DEI's oracle price to enable overborrowing. Attacker moved funds through Tornado Cash.

name: Sonne Finance
description: On May 15, 2024, Sonne Finance on Optimism was exploited for $20M through a donation attack. Market setup was split into separate timelock transactions, allowing the attacker to control execution order and manipulate collateral factors in a newly-created market before protective guards were applied.

name: BBT
description: BBT smart contract exploited via business logic flaw in protocol's core functions. Specific mechanism and loss amount not disclosed but documented in DeFiHackLabs vulnerability database.

name: Acala
description: A misconfiguration in the iBTC/aUSD liquidity pool's incentive mechanism allowed unlimited minting of aUSD tokens instead of LP tokens. Over 1.2 billion aUSD were minted before the network was paused and funds recovered.

name: Cork V1
description: On May 28, 2025, Cork Protocol suffered a $12 million exploit when an attacker created fraudulent market structures with an unprotected beforeSwap hook lacking authorization checks. Missing input validation on market configuration and token validation logic allowed the attacker to create fake token derivatives, draining 3,761 wstETH.

name: Infini
description: Infini suffered a $49.5M exploit on February 24, 2025 when a rogue former developer who had retained vault-draining privileges drained the contract. The attacker immediately converted USDC to ETH (17,696 ETH) through Uniswap, Sky Protocol, and 0x.

name: Moola Market
description: On October 18, 2022, attacker exploited Moola Market on Celo by manipulating MOO token's low-liquidity price oracle to inflate collateral value, allowing unauthorized borrows and draining $8.4M in multiple tokens.

name: ALEX
description: On May 15-16, 2024, Alex Lab's XLink bridge private key was compromised through a phishing attack attributed to state-sponsored actors. Attackers transferred approximately $300,000 in BTC, $3.3M in stablecoins, and $75,000 in SKO tokens across the bridge.

name: Mobius Token
description: Mobius Token's minting function applied 10^18 decimal scaling twice to price data, allowing an attacker to mint ~9.73 quadrillion tokens and swap them for stablecoins, stealing $2.15M.

name: Visor Finance
description: Attacker exploited Visor's OHM-ETH 1% LP management contract by manipulating the Uniswap V3 pool price through large swaps. The steep liquidity gradient in the OHM-ETH pair made it susceptible to price manipulation via asset dump-and-buyback. User funds were secured and losses were covered by Visor's treasury.

name: Bitcoin Gold
description: Bitcoin Gold suffered two 51% attacks on January 23-24, 2020, resulting in 29 blocks being reorganized and deep chain reorgs that enabled double-spending attacks. Attackers rented hash power from NiceHash for ~$1,200 per attack and successfully double-spent approximately 7,167 BTG (~$70K) across two separate attacks. Binance adjusted its confirmation requirements after the incident.

name: Initia
description: On November 10, 2026, an attacker used compromised rollup infrastructure keys to fabricate IBC transfers and withdraw assets from escrow accounts on Initia's Layer 1 that held funds bridged to multiple rollups. Approximately $615,000 in assets, including 605,000 USDC, was transferred out through Noble before validators halted the Initia network at 06:18 UTC. Additional assets were moved from the affected escrow accounts but remained on the halted blockchain. Initia began investigating the compromise with security teams and exchanges, while the full scope of the incident and recovery status remained undetermined

name: Neutra Finance
description: Neutra Finance's convert() function used spot price to value LP tokens, but two LP tokens with the same name (CMLT-LP) from different pools could be swapped for each other. An attacker exploited this by converting from one LP token pool (CMLT-LP-65eb) to the other (CMLT-LP-2ea3), extracting value from the price differential.

name: HireVibes AirDropsDAC
description: EOSIO.SG testing account sym111111add was compromised and used on November 12, 2018 to attack the AirDropsDAC contract. The attacker misappropriated HireVibes tokens (HVT) and other airdrop tokens, selling portions of the stolen HVT on Newdex and transferring profits to controlled accounts.

name: PEPE
description: PEPE team insiders including developer Zachary Testa gained control of the multisig by reducing its signature requirement from five-of-eight to two-of-eight, then transferred ~16 trillion PEPE tokens (~$16.9M gross, ~$15M net after slippage) to CEXs. Insiders subsequently deleted themselves as signers and removed social media accounts.

name: Reaper Farm
description: ReaperVaultV2 contract's withdraw function failed to validate vault share ownership. Attackers exploited this access control flaw to destroy other users' vault shares and withdraw tokens from multiple vaults.

name: DAO Swap
description: DaoSwap's reward system had a flaw allowing users to set themselves as their own inviter. Attackers exploited this access control vulnerability to gain unauthorized mining rewards by claiming referral bonuses.

name: Symbiosis
description: A BridgeV2 receive transaction on BSC minted approximately 2^62 raw units of syBTC to a fresh attacker-controlled EOA, creating an enormous quantity of unbacked syBTC. The same beneficiary subsequently used the unbacked syBTC against syBTC/WBTC liquidity on Ethereum Uniswap V4, extracting and selling approximately 4.39 WBTC. The exact flaw that caused BridgeV2 to accept or authorize the malicious receive has not yet been publicly established

name: THORChain DEX
description: On July 23, 2021, THORChain's ETH Router was exploited when an attacker deployed a custom contract to trick Bifrost Protocol into accepting fake asset deposits, triggering refunds of real assets. The attacker limited impact and requested a 10% bug bounty, suggesting a white-hat teaching lesson.

name: GarudaDefi
description: Between October 20 and 31, 2026, Garuda DeFi suffered multiple security breaches affecting its NFT staking, cross-staking, governance, treasury, frontend and CW20 staking systems on Terra Classic. Attackers migrated staking contracts to malicious code, transferred user assets and rewards, compromised developer wallets to obtain administrative privileges, and injected malicious wallet approval prompts into the protocol's website. The incidents affected 1,114 NFTs and numerous staking tokens, while the total financial loss remains undisclosed. Garuda restored parts of its infrastructure, introduced multisignature administration and began preparing a recovery plan for affected users

name: Juicebox V3
description: On April 20, 2026, Juicebox V3 REVLoans was exploited for 21.77 ETH (~$52,000). Attacker exploited unvalidated source struct in borrowFrom to forge accounting context; by matching forged and destination currencies, attacker bypassed oracle and priced loan against inflated share price using attacker-controlled decimals.

name: Poker EOS
description: Poker EOS game's private key was compromised and disclosed publicly, allowing attackers to drain the game's funds. Over 26,992 EOS were extracted and transferred to exchanges.

name: Cetus CLMM
description: Cetus CLMM on Sui suffered a math error in its checked_shlw function where an incorrect overflow threshold (0xffffffffffffffff << 192 instead of 1 << 192) allowed attackers to craft positions with phantom liquidity. Using flashloans to manipulate prices and create tight tick ranges, attackers minted enormous liquidity while depositing minimal real tokens, then withdrew actual reserves.

name: KlaySwap
description: KlaySwap was compromised via BGP hijack against its infrastructure provider, redirecting traffic to serve a malicious JavaScript SDK. The attack captured user transactions and stole approximately $1.9 million.

name: AscenDEX
description: On December 11, 2021, AscendEX exchange discovered unauthorized transfers of $77 million from its hot wallets across Ethereum, BSC, and Polygon due to compromised private keys, likely via phishing or malware.

name: Bunny
description: On May 19, 2021, PancakeBunny was exploited via flashloan-enabled oracle manipulation. Attacker manipulated USDT/BNB and BUNNY/BNB exchange rates to mint 7M BUNNY and steal 114,631 WBNB (~$45M), crashing BUNNY price.

name: Payy Network
description: Payy’s RollupV1 bridge processed a malicious verifyRollup batch containing an unauthorized 1,828,589.378132 USDC withdrawal to the attacker alongside ordinary withdrawals. The batch was submitted using Payy’s prover and validator infrastructure. ExVul reports that the malicious withdrawal had an all-zero burn hash that users cannot normally generate through Payy’s public circuits, indicating that the forged withdrawal entered during proving or aggregation rather than through an ordinary user withdrawal. Payy has confirmed the bridge exploit but has not yet established whether the cause was compromised prover/validator credentials or a proof-aggregation verification flaw

name: IPC AI
description: IPC AI token deployed on BSC suffered a flash loan attack where the attacker bypassed the flash loan protection mechanism and exploited the deflationary burning mechanism in the token pair. The attacker leveraged the swap() function to circumvent protective measures and extract approximately $590,000 from the liquidity pair.

name: Loopscale Lending
description: In late October and early November 2026, Loopscale was targeted by a sustained attack campaign involving more than 30,000 malicious API requests per day, primarily directed at its SOL and USDC Genesis Vaults on Solana. On November 5, the protocol paused operations after detecting an escalation in the activity. Loopscale stated that the affected vaults had been made whole and that no user deposits incurred losses, but did not disclose whether funds had been stolen or explain the attack mechanism. The protocol remained paused pending further investigation and security improvements

name: Unverified_35bc
description: An unverified smart contract on BSC was exploited via reentrancy, where the attacker repeatedly triggered a function that transferred funds before updating state.

name: Ronin Bridge
description: On August 6, 2024, Ronin Bridge was exploited for $12M (4K ETH + 2M USDC) due to an incomplete contract upgrade. The bridge manager was upgraded to v4, but the v3 initialization function, which set critical voting weights, was never called, leaving _totalOperatorWeight uninitialized and breaking vote-weight validation.

name: CoinDCX
description: CoinDCX experienced approximately $16 million in suspicious outflows from TRON addresses associated with its exchange infrastructure. The exchange attributed the incident to addresses compromised during its July 2025 security breach, which continued receiving deposits after being deprecated. CoinDCX acknowledged that its deposit-sweeping process failed temporarily and stated that it absorbed the resulting losses while crediting affected users. Investigators disputed whether the addresses had genuinely been removed from active operations

name: Alchemix V2
description: Alchemix alETH vault exploited via incorrect vault indexing in the deployment script. Wrong index in debt calculations allowed collateral withdrawal without loan repayment.

name: Adshares
description: On May 16-17, 2026, the Adshares cross-chain bridge was exploited when the bridge-minter EOA signed three wrapTo() calls with non-existent native-chain transaction IDs. The attacker minted fake wrapped ADS tokens and dumped ~$628K worth (148.5 ETH + 305K USDC) on Ethereum.

The 796 exchange suffered from a vulnerability in its withdrawal system that allowed attackers to modify withdrawal addresses. A hacker exploited this by submitting a withdrawal with a modified address that the exchange staff failed to notice, routing 1,000 BTC to the attacker instead of the legitimate customer.
